card_unit_shibata_regiment.name: card_unit_shibata_regiment
card_unit_shibata_regiment.title: SHIBATA REGIMENT
card_unit_shibata_regiment.text: When the enemy gives an order, deal 1 damage to the enemy HQ.
card_unit_shibata_regiment.flavorText: The 16th Infantry Regiment Shibata was part of the 2nd Division of the Imperial Japanese Army. The division was formed in 1871 and participated in several engagements in the First Sino-Japanese War and the Russo-Japanese War. During the Pacific War the division was one of the first to occupy the Dutch East Indies, and in 1942 after the surrender of Dutch forces, it was transferred to Papua New Guinea. From there the 2nd Division was sent to Guadalcanal where it fought in the Battle for Henderson Field and later the Battle for Guadalcanal, where it lost almost 7,000 men. The division was deployed to garrison duty in Malaya and Singapore, and was deployed to Burma in 1944 where it was almost annihilated in the conflict against the Allies. The survivors were assigned to the Japanese 38th Army in French Indochina where it was disbanded at the end of WWII.

card_unit_type94_tk.name: card_unit_type94_tk
card_unit_type94_tk.title: TYPE 94 TK
card_unit_type94_tk.text: Deployment: Add a SURPRISE ATTACK to your hand.
card_unit_type94_tk.flavorText: The Type 94 TK was a Japanese tankette used by the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII and earlier conflicts. The Type 94 TK was produced from 1935-1937 and 823 units were produced. It was rarely used in combat since it had a very thin armor and was armed only with a single machine gun. Some Type 94 TK’s were used as ammunition tractors, but most were used for general infantry support. Many were attached to infantry divisions in Tankette Companies and used for reconnaissance. Tankette’s were considered obsolete by most Western armies when WWII started, but even so the Type 94 TK was used in front line service by the Japanese until 1945.

card_unit_type_1_37mm.name: card_unit_type_1_37mm
card_unit_type_1_37mm.title: TYPE 1 37mm
card_unit_type_1_37mm.text: Deployment: Gets +1+1 and Blitz if your HQ has 10 or less defense.
card_unit_type_1_37mm.flavorText: The Type 1 37mm was an anti-tank gun used and developed by the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII. Prior to that time they had been using the Type 93 37 mm AT Gun, but it had its shortcomings and was not capable of piercing the armor of new Soviet tanks. The solution was to modify the Type 93 AT Gun with a longer barrel which would provide it with greater firepower. The new gun was designated Type 1 37mm Anti-tank Gun and 2,300 guns were produced. The gun was used in frontline service in the Pacific Theater and was moderately effective against Allied light tanks but did little damage against medium tanks such as the M4 Sherman.

card_unit_type_1_chi_he.name: card_unit_type_1_chi_he
card_unit_type_1_chi_he.title: TYPE 1 Chi-He
card_unit_type_1_chi_he.flavorText: The Type 1 Chi-He was a Japanese medium tank used by the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII. The tank was an improved version of the Type 93 Chi-Ha with improved armor, firepower and engine. The Type 1 Chi-He had a crew of 5, a main armament of a Type 1 47mm tank gun and a secondary armament of 2 x 7.7mm Type 97 light machine guns. A total of 170 tanks were produced between 1943-44 which were all allocated to the Japanese home islands to defend against an expected Allied attack.

card_event_air_superiority.name: card_event_air_superiority
card_event_air_superiority.title: AIR SUPERIORITY
card_event_air_superiority.text: Deal 1 damage to a unit. If you have an air unit on the battlefield, deal 3 damage.
card_event_air_superiority.flavorText: Early in WWII the Japanese Army Air Force had air superiority over most battlefields, both due to the qualities of their aircraft and the crews combat experience. However, as the war continued the Allies got the upper hand, mainly due to their superior production capabilities.

card_event_amphibious_assault.name: card_event_amphibious_assault
card_event_amphibious_assault.title: AMPHIBIOUS ASSAULT
card_event_amphibious_assault.text: Destroy an enemy unit that has 3 or less attack.
card_event_amphibious_assault.flavorText: Amphibious warfare is a type of offensive where attacks are launched from the sea by naval and landing forces against hostile shores.

card_event_ancient_empire.name: card_event_ancient_empire
card_event_ancient_empire.title: ANCIENT EMPIRE
card_event_ancient_empire.text: Set your HQ's defense to 8. Draw an ANCIENT EMPIRE.
card_event_ancient_empire.flavorText: The Empire of Japan was considered a colonial empire and existed as such from 1868 until the enactment of the 1947 constitution of modern Japan.

card_event_blade_of_the_samurai.name: card_event_blade_of_the_samurai
card_event_blade_of_the_samurai.title: BLADE OF THE SAMURAI
card_event_blade_of_the_samurai.flavorText: The ancient Samurai sword was known as katana, wakizashi or tachi. The swords issued to officers of the Japanese Imperial Army were called Kashi-kan shin-gunto (e. army non-commissioned officer's sword) and had the same design as the ancient Samurai sword. The shin-gunto was part of their regulation equipment, and it was used in combat occasionally as well.

card_event_bombing_raid.name: card_event_bombing_raid
card_event_bombing_raid.title: BOMBING RAID
card_event_bombing_raid.text: Deal 3 damage to an enemy target and 2 damage to adjacent targets.
card_event_bombing_raid.flavorText: The most famous Japanese bombing raid was the attack on Pearl Harbor which was lead by the Japanese Imperial Navy. During WWII the Japanese Navy and Army mostly used tactical bombing against ships, airfields, military positions, and military installations, but they also bombed Chinese cities such as Shanghai, Wuhan, and Chongqing, as well as conducting air raids on Philippines and Northern Australia.

card_event_burning_sun.name: card_event_burning_sun
card_event_burning_sun.title: BURNING SUN
card_event_burning_sun.text: Friendly air units have +3 attack until end of turn.
card_event_burning_sun.flavorText: Through the ages the sun has played a big role in Japanese mythology and religion. This is embodied in the Japanese national flag, known as Nisshōki (日章旗, 'flag of sun') or Hinomaru (日の丸, 'circle of the sun'), which became a symbol of Japan’s war effort in Asia and the Pacific during WWII and earlier conflicts. The flag was often signed and given away as farewell presents to departing soldiers. They were called “prayer flags” and the text on them often wished the soldiers good luck and fortune in their fight for Imperial Japan.

card_event_burst_of_fire.name: card_event_burst_of_fire
card_event_burst_of_fire.title: BURST OF FIRE
card_event_burst_of_fire.text: Give a friendly fighter +1 attack and Fury this turn.
card_event_burst_of_fire.flavorText: Aircraft of the Japanese Imperial Army used both Type 89 7.7 mm machine guns (copy of Vickers Class E) and Ho-103 12.7 mm machine guns (based on Browning M1921). For rear armament (defensive use) they used Type 89 7.7 mm machine gun (based on Type 11), Type 98 7.92 mm machine gun (copy of MG 15) and Ho-104 12.7 mm machine gun (based on Browning M1921). Navy aircraft used Type 92 7.7 mm machine guns (British Lewis),  Type 97 7.7 mm machine gun (Vickers) and Type 3 13.2 mm machine gun (Browning with Hotchkiss 13.2mm cartridge). For rear armament (defensive use) they used Type 92 7.7 mm machine gun (British Lewis), Type 1 7.92 mm machine gun (German MG 15), Type 2 13 mm machine gun (German MG 131) and Type 99-1/Type 99-2 20 mm cannon (Oerlikon FF).

card_event_code_of_bushido.name: card_event_code_of_bushido
card_event_code_of_bushido.title: CODE OF BUSHIDO
card_event_code_of_bushido.text: Choose and discard an air unit to destroy a unit with 5 or less attack.
card_event_code_of_bushido.flavorText: Bushido means "the way of the warrior" and is a Japanese term for the codes of honor and ideals that dictate the samurai way of life. The code is typified by 8 virtues: Righteousness and justice, heroic courage, benevolence and compassion, respect, honesty and sincerity, honor, duty and loyalty, self-control. These all seem like righteous codes and a roadmap to good living and happiness. However, perverse theories of Bushido dominated Japanese intellectual life and military command from 1930-45, which seemed to fuel Japan’s determination to fight to the very last man and woman and many link it to the atrocities committed by their soldiers during WWII.

card_event_deadly_duty.name: card_event_deadly_duty
card_event_deadly_duty.title: DEADLY DUTY
card_event_deadly_duty.text: Destroy a friendly unit. Draw 2 cards.
card_event_deadly_duty.flavorText: Many Japanese soldiers and civilians, especially during the final stages of WWII, considered it more honorable to die in the service of the Emperor (Hirohito), rather than to surrender or be captured alive.

card_event_divine_wind.name: card_event_divine_wind
card_event_divine_wind.title: DIVINE WIND
card_event_divine_wind.text: Destroy a unit. Discard a random card from your hand.
card_event_divine_wind.flavorText: Divine wind is the English translation of the word Kamikaze, which allegedly were the two storms that saved Japan from two Mongol fleets under Kublai Khan. This word was later used during WWII for suicide attacks by Japanese pilots in the Pacific war. The metaphor meant that the pilots were to be the "Divine Wind" that would again sweep the enemy from the seas.

card_event_empire_of_the_sun.name: card_event_empire_of_the_sun
card_event_empire_of_the_sun.title: EMPIRE OF THE SUN
card_event_empire_of_the_sun.text: Destroy an enemy unit. Draw cards equal to its attack.
card_event_empire_of_the_sun.flavorText: The Empire of Japan existed from the Meiji Restoration in 1868 to the enactment of the 1947 constitution of modern Japan. Due to how the name is written with Japanese characters and its flag, it was also given the exonym Empire of the Sun.

card_event_for_prosperety.name: card_event_for_prosperety
card_event_for_prosperety.title: FOR PROSPERITY
card_event_for_prosperety.flavorText: The Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere was a concept promoted by the Empire of Japan. It represented the desire to create a self-sufficient block of Asian nations led by the Japanese and free of Western powers.

card_event_for_the_emperor.name: card_event_for_the_emperor
card_event_for_the_emperor.title: FOR THE EMPEROR
card_event_for_the_emperor.text: All friendly Japanese units have +1 attack and operate for one less until end of turn.
card_event_for_the_emperor.flavorText: To many Japanese soldiers and citizens, and according to the Shinto religion, Emperor Hirohito was considered a living god and there was no greater honor than to serve under him and/or to die for him in battle.

card_event_home_defense.name: card_event_home_defense
card_event_home_defense.title: HOME DEFENSE
card_event_home_defense.text: Costs 4 if your HQ is at 10 or less. Add TYPE 3 CHI-NU and AICHI D3A-2 to the support line.
card_event_home_defense.flavorText: A series of battles and engagements between the American and Japanese forces took place in and round the Japanese Home Islands during the final stages of WWII. There were two major island battles: The Battle of Iwo Jima and the Battle of Okinawa, and one naval battles: Operation Ten-Go. Including the aforementioned engagements, the American conducted air raids and naval bombardment on Japanese cities. However, the Japanese forces refused to surrender, and although the Americans were victorious they had to pay a steep price. Japan still had a homeland army of approximately two million soldiers and enough resources to halt an Allied invasion for a considerable time. However, it never came to use since Japan surrendered after the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

card_event_honor.name: card_event_honor
card_event_honor.title: HONOR
card_event_honor.text: Give a friendly unit +4+4. At the end of your turn, destroy it.
card_event_honor.flavorText: "Victory or death" was a principle strongly promoted by the Imperial Japanese Army. This idea framed the refusal to surrender and the decision to fight to the last as part of an extreme form of wartime mobilization.

card_event_imperial_order.name: card_event_imperial_order
card_event_imperial_order.title: IMPERIAL ORDER
card_event_imperial_order.text: Fully repair a unit and give it +1+1.
card_event_imperial_order.flavorText: Although the Japanese fought the war in Emperor Hiroshitos name, the extent of his power and impact on military decisions and orders is still being questioned by historians. It can however be said that Hiroshito took his nation to war, to surrender, and finally to peace.

card_event_imperial_strength.name: card_event_imperial_strength
card_event_imperial_strength.title: IMPERIAL STRENGTH
card_event_imperial_strength.text: Discard all activated countermeasures. Deal 2 damage to the enemy HQ.
card_event_imperial_strength.flavorText: Before and during WWII Japan had occupied or taken control of regions that counted approximately 464 million inhabitants. Control over all territories except the Japanese mainland and surrounding islands was renounced by Japan in the unconditional surrender after World War II.

card_event_kamikaze.name: card_event_kamikaze
card_event_kamikaze.title: KAMIKAZE
card_event_kamikaze.text: Deal 1 damage to the enemy HQ. Draw a card.

card_event_last_rites.name: card_event_last_rites
card_event_last_rites.title: LAST RITES
card_event_last_rites.text: Shuffle 8 KAMIKAZE cards into your deck.
card_event_last_rites.flavorText: Before kamikaze pilots departed on their final missions they were given military decorations and ceremonies were carried out where they shared ceremonial cups of sake or water known as “mizu no sakazuki”. The pilots would also compose and read a death poem, a tradition stemming from the samurai’s, who did so before committing seppuku. The kamikaze pilot would wear a “senninbari”, a "belt of a thousand stitches" given to them by their mothers and carry prayers from their families on the final mission. In the final moments before impact, the pilot was to yell "hissatsu" which translates to "certain kill".

card_event_lightning_conquest_new.name: card_event_lightning_conquest_new
card_event_lightning_conquest_new.title: LIGHTNING CONQUEST
card_event_lightning_conquest_new.text: Friendly infantry units are immune to damage and can both move and attack this turn.
card_event_lightning_conquest_new.flavorText: The Japanese Imperial Army started out as military conquerors of the Pacific and East Asia. However, as the war progressed and the US and Soviet allies joined the war against Japan their strategy changed to a defensive war.

card_event_naval_operation.name: card_event_naval_operation
card_event_naval_operation.title: NAVAL OPERATION
card_event_naval_operation.text: Pin all enemy ground units and deal 1 damage to them.
card_event_naval_operation.flavorText: At the beginning of WWII the Japanese Imperial Navy was the third most powerful in the world, with only the British and American navies being more powerful. During the first 6 months of the Pacific War the Japanese Navy managed to inflict devastating damage to the Allied naval forces and were practically undefeated. However, through their great industrial output and the modernization of their air and naval forces, the Americans soon got the upper hand in the war.

card_event_naval_supply_run.name: card_event_naval_supply_run
card_event_naval_supply_run.title: NAVAL SUPPLY RUN
card_event_naval_supply_run.text: Give your units +2+1. At start of your next turn discard a card at random.
card_event_naval_supply_run.flavorText: The Imperial Japanese Navy used ships at night to deliver personnel, supplies and equipment to Japanese forces operating in and around New Guinea and the Solomon Islands during the Pacific Campaign of WWII. The operation involved loading personnel or supplies aboard fast warships, mainly destroyers and later submarines, and delivering it under cover of darkness and being back to base before daylight in order to avoid being intercepted by the Allies. The Allied called this operation the Tokyo Express.

card_event_reconnaissance.name: card_event_reconnaissance
card_event_reconnaissance.title: LONG RANGE RECON
card_event_reconnaissance.text: Your HQ gains defense equal to the number of all cards on the battlefield.
card_event_reconnaissance.flavorText: Long range reconnaissance aircraft were crucial to the Japanese war effort due to the vast territory they had to patrol and fight over in the Pacific War. The Japanese Navy had quite a few seaplanes that were used for this purpose, including the Kawanashi H8K (Emily), a long range reconnaissance/bomber aircraft (depicted in the image).

card_event_rising_sun.name: card_event_rising_sun
card_event_rising_sun.title: EXPANSION
card_event_rising_sun.text: If you control a Japanese unit in the frontline, draw 2 cards.
card_event_rising_sun.flavorText: Following the attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941 the Japanese had a long series of military successes in Asia and the Pacific. That same month Thailand surrendered to the Japanese only 5 hours into the invasion, and Hong Kong, Guam and Wake Island fell shortly after. In January 1942 Manila, the capital city of the Philippines, was occupied, Singapore was conquered in February and Rangoon (Burma) and the Dutch East Indies fell in early March. It wasn’t until the mid year of 1942 that the forces of Australia and New Zealand in New Guinea and the British forces in India managed to halt the Japanese advance. Furthermore, the Japanese Navy had not managed to drive the US Navy out of the South Pacific and would soon receive a crippling blow in the Battle of Midway, which is considered to be a turning point in the Battle of the Pacific. After that the Allied forces slowly gained air and naval supremacy in the Pacific and the tables were turned.

card_event_surprise_attack.name: card_event_surprise_attack
card_event_surprise_attack.title: SURPRISE ATTACK
card_event_surprise_attack.text: Pin an enemy unit. If already pinned, destroy it instead.
card_event_surprise_attack.flavorText: Throughout history surprise military attacks have turned the tables and changed the course of history. The most famous Japanese surprise attack during WWII was the military strike conducted by the Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service against the US naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, on the morning of December 7, 1941. The attack led to the United States formal entry into WWII, both in the Pacific and European theaters, which eventually led to the surrender of Imperial Japan and the Axis powers.

card_event_tora_tora.name: card_event_tora_tora
card_event_tora_tora.title: TORA! TORA! TORA!
card_event_tora_tora.flavorText: Tora was code word sent by the leader of the first wave of Japanese fighters that attacked Pearl Harbor to superior officers on the aircraft carrier Akagi. The word tora means "tiger" in Japanese, but in this case it is an abbreviated radio code word, an acronym for totsugeki raigeki, which literally means "lightning attack," indicating to his superior commanders that the objective of complete surprise had been achieved. TORA! TORA! TORA! is the name of an American movie, which is a dramatic retelling of the Pearl Harbor attack.

card_event_yamamoto.name: card_event_yamamoto
card_event_yamamoto.title: ADMIRAL YAMAMOTO
card_event_yamamoto.text: Give friendly air units on the battlefield +1 attack and Blitz this turn.
card_event_yamamoto.flavorText: Isoroku Yamamoto (April 4, 1884 – April 18, 1943) was a Marshal Admiral of the Imperial Japanese Navy and the commander-in-chief of the Combined Fleet during WWII until his death. He was the commander-in-chief during the early years of the Pacific War and oversaw major engagements including the attack on Pearl Harbor and the Battle of Midway. He was killed after American code breakers identified his flight plan, which enable the US air force to intercept and shoot down his plane.

card_unit_15th_cavalry_regiment.name: card_unit_15th_cavalry_regiment
card_unit_15th_cavalry_regiment.title: 15th CAVALRY REGIMENT
card_unit_15th_cavalry_regiment.flavorText: The 15th Cavalry Regiment was attached to the 2nd Cavalry Brigade. The Japanese Imperial Army retained a few cavalry units during WWII but most of them were used for reconnaissance.

card_unit_1st_signal_regiment.name: card_unit_1st_signal_regiment
card_unit_1st_signal_regiment.title: 1st SIGNAL REGIMENT
card_unit_1st_signal_regiment.text: When another friendly unit is destroyed, deal 1 damage to the enemy HQ.
card_unit_1st_signal_regiment.flavorText: The 1st Signal Regiment was attached to the Japanese 25th Army which was formed in 1941 and participated in the Battle of Malaya and Battle of Singapore. After that the 25th Army served as a garrison force in the occupied territories until the surrender of Japan in August 1945. The signal regiment was made up of several wire companies, several radio platoons, a fixed radio unit, a radio intercept unit and a field pigeon unit.

card_unit_28cm_coasttal_howitzer.name: card_unit_28cm_coasttal_howitzer
card_unit_28cm_coasttal_howitzer.title: 28cm COASTAL HOWITZER
card_unit_28cm_coasttal_howitzer.flavorText: The 28 cm howitzer L/10 was a Japanese coastal and siege howitzer. It was developed by the British manufacturing company called Armstrong before 1892 and saw service in the Russo-Japanese War during the siege of Port Arthur and the Second Sino-Japanese War. Due to a lack of other alternatives the Japanese reactivated the 28 cm howitzer for coastal defense in 1945, and it was used with some success during the Soviet invasion of Manchuria in 1945.

card_unit_2nd_raiding_brigade.name: card_unit_2nd_raiding_brigade
card_unit_2nd_raiding_brigade.title: 2nd RAIDING BRIGADE
card_unit_2nd_raiding_brigade.text: Deployment: Destroy an enemy unit with attack 2 or less.
card_unit_2nd_raiding_brigade.flavorText: The 2nd Raiding Brigade was a part of raiding group called Teishin Shudan which was a Japanese special forces/airborne unit during WWII which operated under the Imperial Japanese Army Air Force. The group took part in special operations but for most parts they were deployed as elite light infantry. In 1944 some 750 men, mostly from the 2nd Raiding Brigade, were assigned to Operation "Te" which was assigned to attack American air bases on Luzon and Leyte. They were flown in Ki-57 transports, but most of the aircraft were shot down on the way. Around 300 of them managed to land in the Burauen area on Leyte and managed to destroy some planes and inflict numerous casualties before they were defeated by Allied forces.

card_unit_33rd_recon.name: card_unit_33rd_recon
card_unit_33rd_recon.title: 33rd RECON
card_unit_33rd_recon.text: When this unit takes damage, draw a card.
card_unit_33rd_recon.flavorText: The 33rd Recon Regiment was attached to the 33rd Division and took part in the Second Sino-Japanese War and the Burma Campaign (the first Battle of Changsha, the Battle of Yenangyaung and the Battle of Imphal). Reconnaissance regiments were types of units tasked with combat scouting and attached to many Japanese divisions during WWII.

card_unit_41st_bicycle_regiment.name: card_unit_41st_bicycle_regiment
card_unit_41st_bicycle_regiment.title: 41st BICYCLE REGIMENT
card_unit_41st_bicycle_regiment.flavorText: The 41st Bicycle Regiment of the Imperial Japanese Army was subordinate of the 9th Infantry Bicycle Brigade of the 5th Division. The division participated in the Second Sino-Japanese war and later in the war in the Pacific where it saw action in numerous battles and campaigns. In WWII the Imperial Japanese Army used bicycles extensively in their campaigns in Southeast Asia as they thought it was an efficient form of transportation and cheap for the war effort. Their bicycle soldiers could carry 36 kilograms of equipment and it often allowed them to move faster across terrain than the Allied forces.

card_unit_6th_infantry_regiment.name: card_unit_6th_infantry_regiment
card_unit_6th_infantry_regiment.title: 6th INFANTRY REGIMENT
card_unit_6th_infantry_regiment.flavorText: The 6th Infantry Regiment was attached to the 3rd Division, which was first formed in 1871 and was one of the oldest divisions of the Imperial Japanese Army. Prior to WWII the division participated in the First Sino-Japanese War, the Russo-Japanese War, the Siberian Intervention and the Shandong Incident and was considered a crack unit.

card_unit_75mm_field_artillery.name: card_unit_75mm_field_artillery
card_unit_75mm_field_artillery.title: 75mm FIELD ARTILLERY
card_unit_75mm_field_artillery.text: Enemies adjacent to target attacked by 75mm FIELD ARTILLERY are dealt 1 damage.
card_unit_75mm_field_artillery.flavorText: The Type 90 75mm field gun used by the Imperial Japanese Army in WWII. It was designed in 1930 and was intended to replace the Type 38 75 mm field gun, but due to budget constraints and industrial limitations only a few of them were built. It was rarely deployed against the Allies in the Pacific War, and often it was used as an anti-tank gun, and often deployed with armored units.

card_unit_75mm_mountain_gun.name: card_unit_75mm_mountain_gun
card_unit_75mm_mountain_gun.title: 75mm MOUNTAIN GUN
card_unit_75mm_mountain_gun.flavorText: The type 41 75 mm mountain gun was used as an infantry gun and normally each regiment had four of them deployed. The 75 mm mountain gun was referred to as "rentai ho" (regimental artillery).

card_unit_a5m4_claude.name: card_unit_a5m4_claude
card_unit_a5m4_claude.title: A5M4 CLAUDE
card_unit_a5m4_claude.text: Deployment: Give another friendly unit -1 operation cost.
card_unit_a5m4_claude.flavorText: The Mitsubishi A5M was a Japanese carrier based fighter and the world's first monoplane shipboard fighter to enter service, and the predecessor of the famous Mitsubishi A6M "Zero". It was introduced in 1936 and was highly effective in the early stages of the Second Sino-Japanese War. Even though the aircraft was only armed with two 7.7 mm machine-guns, it proved effective and damage-tolerant, with excellent maneuverability and robust construction.  Later in WWII the A5M's also provided much-needed escorts for the vulnerable Mitsubishi G3M bombers.

card_unit_aichi_d3a.name: card_unit_aichi_d3a
card_unit_aichi_d3a.title: AICHI D3A-2
card_unit_aichi_d3a.text: Has +2 attack for each other AICHI D3A you control.
card_unit_aichi_d3a.flavorText: The Aichi D3A-2 (a D3A variant) was primarily a dive bomber used by the Imperial Japanese Navy from 1940 to 1945. The Allies referred to it as "Val" and it was first used in the attack on Pearl Harbor. During WWII this aircraft sank more Allied ships than any other Axis aircraft.  1,495 D3A's were built, including variants.

card_unit_akita_regiment.name: card_unit_akita_regiment
card_unit_akita_regiment.title: AKITA REGIMENT
card_unit_akita_regiment.text: Destruction: Deal 2 damage to a random enemy.
card_unit_akita_regiment.flavorText: The 17th Infantry Regiment (Akita) was part of the 2nd Infantry Division of the Japanese Imperial Army. The regiment participated in the Battle of Khalkhin Gol, the Battle of Java, the Guadalcanal Campaign and the Battle of Central Burma. Several regiments were raised in Akita, the capital city of Akita Prefecture. These regiments served in several divisions in the Japanese Imperial Army.

card_unit_c6n_saiun.name: card_unit_c6n_saiun
card_unit_c6n_saiun.title: C6N SAIUN
card_unit_c6n_saiun.text: Cannot be attacked by ground units while in the support line. Countermeasures cannot trigger.
card_unit_c6n_saiun.flavorText: The Nakajima C6N Saiun was a carrier-based reconnaissance aircraft used by the Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service in WWII. The Allied reporting name of the C6N Saiun was Myrt and it was the fastest carrier-based aircraft put into service by Japan during the war. However, it didn't enter service until 1944 when only a few carriers were left to operate from which meant that most were flown from land bases. 463 aircraft were produced including a few variants.

card_unit_dinah.name: card_unit_dinah
card_unit_dinah.title: M6A1 SEIRAN
card_unit_dinah.flavorText: The Aichi M6A1 Seiran was a Japanese submarine-launched attack floatplane used by the Imperial Japanese Navy during WWII. It was intended to operate from I-400 class submarines and its original mission was to conduct aerial attacks against the United States. Only 28 aircraft were built, including variants, and it was first used in service in 1945, not long before Japan surrendered. Many of the M6A1's were destroyed to prevent capture and only one exists today at the Udvar-Hazy Center of the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum.

card_unit_g4m1_betty.name: card_unit_g4m1_betty
card_unit_g4m1_betty.title: G4M1 BETTY
card_unit_g4m1_betty.text: If discarded, add to support line instead. Deployment: Discard a random card from your hand.
card_unit_g4m1_betty.flavorText: The Mitsubishi G4M, nicknamed Betty by the Allies, was the main twin-engine, land-based bomber used by the Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service during WWII. The G4Ms were first used in service in 1940 and were mostly used as torpedo bombers in anti-shipping roles. The aircraft performed very well, especially in operational range which was achieved by its structural lightness and an almost total lack of protection for the crew, which was its weakness when confronted with American fighters. A total of 2,435 G4Ms were built, including a few variants.

card_unit_himeji_regiment.name: card_unit_himeji_regiment
card_unit_himeji_regiment.title: HIMEJI REGIMENT
card_unit_himeji_regiment.flavorText: The 39th Infantry Regiment Himeji was attached to the 10th Division of the Imperial Japanese Army, which was code named the "Iron Division". The division fought in the Russo-Japanese War, the Second Sino-Japanese War and during WWII. By the end of WWII they were sent to  Luzon in the Philippines to fight against the American forces where the division was almost entirely annihilated in the Battle of Luzon in 1945. However, the 39th Regiment continued a guerrilla war until the surrender of Japan on August 15, 1945.

card_unit_j1n1_gekko.name: card_unit_j1n1_gekko
card_unit_j1n1_gekko.title: J1N1 GEKKO
card_unit_j1n1_gekko.flavorText: The Nakajima J1N1 Gekko was a Japanese twin-engine aircraft used by the Japanese Imperial Navy during WWII as a night combat, reconnaissance aircraft and lastly for kamikaze missions. It was first introduced in 1942, first for reconnaissance and later as a night fighter. The night fighter variant had a twin 20 mm Type 99 Model 1 cannon firing upward in a 30° upward angle, and a second pair firing downward at a forward 30° angle, allowing attacks from above or below. This arrangement was effective against the Allied B-17 Flying Fortress Bombers and B-24 Liberators. By the end of the war a number of Gekko's were used for Kamikaze attacks where they had 250 kg bombs attached to the wings.

card_unit_jade_division.name: card_unit_jade_division
card_unit_jade_division.title: JADE DIVISION
card_unit_jade_division.text: Gets +1+1 when you play a Japanese card, and Guard when attack is 10+.
card_unit_jade_division.flavorText: The call sign of the 1st Infantry Division was Jade Division and it was one of the oldest divisions in the Japanese Imperial Army. During WWII the division engaged in combat in the Battle of Khalkhin Gol, the Battle of Leyte and the Battle of Luzon.

card_unit_ki_27_nate.name: card_unit_ki_27_nate
card_unit_ki_27_nate.title: Ki-27 NATE
card_unit_ki_27_nate.text: Destruction: Add a random Japanese unit that costs 1 or less to your hand.
card_unit_ki_27_nate.flavorText: The Nakajima Ki-27 was the main fighter aircraft used by the Imperial Japanese Army Air Force up until 1940. Allegedly it was named "Abdul" in the "China Burma India" theater but it was generally known to the Allies by the nickname "Nate".

card_unit_ki_44_tojo.name: card_unit_ki_44_tojo
card_unit_ki_44_tojo.title: Ki-44 TOJO
card_unit_ki_44_tojo.text: Deployment: The enemy discards a random bomber from hand.
card_unit_ki_44_tojo.flavorText: The Nakajima Ki-44, code named “Tojo” by the Allies, was a single engine fighter used by the Imperial Japanese Army Air Force during WWII. It first entered service in 1942, and although it was overall a superior combat aircraft compared to its predecessor the Ki-43, it was disliked by pilots due to its poor visibility on the ground, its higher landing speed and restrictions on maneuvering. However, it did have a much better armament than its predecessor, four 12.7mm machine guns or two 12.7mm guns and two 20 mm cannons, instead of only the two 12.7mm machine guns on the Ki-43. Although it was a useful interceptor and could match many Allied fighters capabilities, its performance suffered due the lack of properly trained pilots, which was often the case for the Japanese during the later stages of the war.

card_unit_ki_61_hien.name: card_unit_ki_61_hien
card_unit_ki_61_hien.title: Ki-61 HIEN
card_unit_ki_61_hien.flavorText: The Ki-61 Hien, official name Kawasaki Ki-61 Hien (meaning "flying swallow" in Japanese), was a Japanese fighter aircraft used by the Imperial Japanese Army Air Force in WWII. It was first introduced in 1942 and was used in combat missions throughout the war. 3,078 aircraft of this type were built and they were used in combat service throughout the war. The Allies code name for the aircraft was "Tony".

card_unit_ki_84_frank.name: card_unit_ki_84_frank
card_unit_ki_84_frank.title: Ki-84 FRANK
card_unit_ki_84_frank.flavorText: The Nakajima Ki-84, code named "Frank" by the Allies, was a Japanese single-seat fighter aircraft used during the last two years of WWII. The Ki-84 was considered the best Japanese fighter, because it combined high speed capability with excellent maneuverability, and excellent firepower. The aircraft was a perfect match against any Allied single engine fighter, plus it had enough firepower to take down the high flying and well-defended Boeing B-29 Superfortress.

card_unit_kumamoto_regiment.name: card_unit_kumamoto_regiment
card_unit_kumamoto_regiment.title: KUMAMOTO REGIMENT
card_unit_kumamoto_regiment.flavorText: The 13th Infantry Regiment (Kumamoto) was attached to the 6th Infantry Brigade of the 6th Division and participated during the Second Sino-Japanese War. The regiment fought in the later stages of WWII, assigned to the Japanese Seventeenth Army, at Bougainville Island in the Solomon Islands.

card_unit_mito_regiment.name: card_unit_mito_regiment
card_unit_mito_regiment.title: MITO REGIMENT
card_unit_mito_regiment.text: Destruction: Deal 2 damage to the enemy HQ.
card_unit_mito_regiment.flavorText: The 2nd Infantry Regiment (Mito) was attached to the 14th Division of the Imperial Japanese Army. In 1944, the 2nd Infantry Regiment (Mito) was sent to Peleliu, where one of the fiercest battles of the Pacific War took place.

card_unit_model_25.name: card_unit_model_25
card_unit_model_25.title: MODEL 25
card_unit_model_25.text: Deployment: Give a friendly infantry +2 attack until end of turn.
card_unit_model_25.flavorText: The Vickers Crossley Armoured Car, aka Model 25, was a British made armored car that was exported to different countries, including Japan, during the 1930s. The Model 25 had a crew of 5 and a main armament of 2 x Vickers 7.7 mm machine guns.

card_unit_nakajima_b5n.name: card_unit_nakajima_b5n
card_unit_nakajima_b5n.title: B5N KATE
card_unit_nakajima_b5n.text: When you discard a card, deal 1 damage to all enemies.
card_unit_nakajima_b5n.flavorText: The Nakajima B5N, called "Kate" by the Allies, was a standard carrier torpedo bomber of the Imperial Japanese Navy during WWII. The B5N first saw combat in the Sino-Japanese War, and later variants were used in the attack on Pearl Harbor. Later in the war it was used in secondary roles, such as training, target towing, and anti-submarine warfare.

card_unit_p1y_ginga.name: card_unit_p1y_ginga
card_unit_p1y_ginga.title: P1Y GINGA
card_unit_p1y_ginga.text: When discarded, deal 1 damage to all enemies. Deployment: Deal 1 damage to all enemies.
card_unit_p1y_ginga.flavorText: The Yokosuka P1Y Ginga (Ginga meaning "Galaxy") was a twin-engine bomber used by the Imperial Japanese Forces in WWII. Although it was developed by the Imperial Japanese Navy, it was land based and could both be used for dive bombing and torpedo bombing, but at the end of the war it was also used for Kamikaze attacks against Allied ships. The Allied code name for the P1Y Ginga was "Frances".

card_unit_pete.name: card_unit_pete
card_unit_pete.title: F1M2 PETE
card_unit_pete.text: Cannot be attacked by ground units while in the support line.
card_unit_pete.flavorText: The Mitsubishi F1M  was a Japanese sea plane used in WWII (nicknamed "Pete" by the Allies). Although it was built as an reconnaissance aircraft it took on a number of roles including convoy escort, bomber, anti-submarine, maritime patrol, rescue, transport, and anti-shipping strike.

card_unit_sally.name: card_unit_sally
card_unit_sally.title: Ki-21 SALLY
card_unit_sally.text: If this unit is discarded, draw 2 cards.
card_unit_sally.flavorText: The Mitsubishi Ki-21, or Type 97 Heavy Bomber, was a Japanese heavy bomber used in WWII. It was first used in combat in the Second Sino-Japanese War, and in the first stages of the Pacific War. Several variants were built throughout the war, but production was halted in 1944. The Allied reporting name of the Mitsubishi Ki-21 was "Sally".

card_unit_sendai_regiment.name: card_unit_sendai_regiment
card_unit_sendai_regiment.title: SENDAI REGIMENT
card_unit_sendai_regiment.text: Deployment: Remove an enemy unit until SENDAI REGIMENT leaves the battlefield.
card_unit_sendai_regiment.flavorText: The 4th Infantry Regiment (Sendai) was attached to the 2nd Division of the Imperial Japanese Army and was one of the divisions that occupied the Dutch East Indies early in the war. The regiment later fought in the New Guinea Campaign and saw action in the Battle of Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands. In 1944 it was ordered to Burma to resist the British reoccupation, but after a defeat the remnants of the division were assigned to the Japanese 38th Army in French Indochina before it was disbanded by the end of the war.

card_unit_shiden.name: card_unit_shiden
card_unit_shiden.title: N1K-J SHIDEN
card_unit_shiden.flavorText: The Kawanishi N1K-J Shiden (Violet Lightning) was an Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service WWII fighter, a land-based version of the N1K Kyōfū which was a Navy float plane. The Allied nicknamed the aircraft "George" and both pilots and opponents considered it to be one of the finest land-based fighters flown by the Japanese during WWII. The N1K-J Shiden entered service in early 1944 and 1,007 aircraft were produced before production was switched to the improved N1K2-J.

card_unit_sonia.name: card_unit_sonia
card_unit_sonia.title: AICHI D3A-1
card_unit_sonia.text: Destruction: If it is the enemy turn, add an AICHI D3A-2 to your support line.
card_unit_sonia.flavorText: The Aichi D3A-1 (a D3A variant) was primarily a dive bomber used by the Imperial Japanese Navy from 1940 to 1945. The Allies referred to it as "Val" and it was first used in the attack on Pearl Harbor. During WWII this aircraft sank more Allied ships than any other Axis aircraft.  1,495 D3A's were built, including variants.

card_unit_takasagi_regiment.name: card_unit_takasagi_regiment
card_unit_takasagi_regiment.title: TAKASAKI REGIMENT
card_unit_takasagi_regiment.text: Destruction: Your enemy discards a card.
card_unit_takasagi_regiment.flavorText: The 15th Infantry Regiment (Takasaki) was attached to the 14th Division of the Japanese Imperial Army and was with them from 1937 and throughout WWII. In 1944 parts of the regiment took part in the Battle of Peleliu.

card_unit_type_3_chi_nu.name: card_unit_type_3_chi_nu
card_unit_type_3_chi_nu.title: TYPE 3 Chi-Nu
card_unit_type_3_chi_nu.text: Has Ambush and Guard while in your support line.
card_unit_type_3_chi_nu.flavorText: Type 3 Chi-Nu  was a Japanese medium tank used by the Imperial Japanese Army in WWII. The tank was an improved version of the Type 97 Chi-Ha and used a Type 3 75 mm tank gun which was one the largest tank guns used by the Japanese forces in the war. 144 to 166 units were produced from 1944 to 1945 and due to its late arrival it did not see combat during the war as all units were used for defense of the homeland for the anticipated Allied invasion. The Type 3 Chi-Nu had a crew of 5 and a secondary armament of a single 7.7 mm Type 97 machine gun.

card_unit_type_4.name: card_unit_type_4
card_unit_type_4.title: TYPE 4 Ho-Ro
card_unit_type_4.flavorText: The Type 4 Ho-Ro was a self-propelled gun developed and used by the Imperial Japanese Army in WWII. It was inspired by the German Grille series of self-propelled artillery and had a Type 38 150 mm howitzer mounted on a tracked chassis of a slightly modified Type 97 Chi-Ha chassis. The Type 4 Ho-Ro had a crew of 6 and a maximum rate of fire of only 5 rounds per minute. Only a handful of them were produced (approx. 12 units) and only one of them was captured by the Allies at Luzon and is now preserved at the United States Marine Corps Museum in Quantico, Virginia.

card_unit_type_88_aa_gun.name: card_unit_type_88_aa_gun
card_unit_type_88_aa_gun.title: TYPE 88 AA GUN
card_unit_type_88_aa_gun.text: Air units that attack or are attacked by TYPE 88 AA GUN are pinned.
card_unit_type_88_aa_gun.flavorText: The Type 88 75 mm AA gun was a Japanese anti-aircraft gun used by the Imperial Japanese Army from 1927 to 1945. It was first designed as a medium anti-aircraft weapon, but the Japanese forces soon found out that it was a very effective anti-tank weapon when it was fired horizontally. During WWII, both in the Battle of Iwo Jima and the Battle of Okinawa, it was used effectively against American M4 Sherman tanks, and as a coastal-defense gun. By the end of the war many of the guns were withdrawn from front line services and used for Japan's homeland defenses against Allied air raids and to prepare for the threat of the Allied invasion.

card_unit_type_89.name: card_unit_type_89
card_unit_type_89.title: TYPE 89 Chi-Ro
card_unit_type_89.text: When a HQ gains defense, it takes that much damage instead.
card_unit_type_89.flavorText: Type 89 Chi-Ro was a medium tank used by the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII. The tank was a 1920s design, built to support infantry, but due to its weak armor and lack of firepower it proved ineffective against Allied tanks, and by 1942 the Type 89 Chi-Ro was withdrawn from frontline combat service. The tank had a crew of 4, a main armament of 57 mm Type 90 gun and a secondary armament of 2 x 6.5 mm Type 91 machine guns.

card_unit_type_93.name: card_unit_type_93
card_unit_type_93.title: TYPE 93
card_unit_type_93.flavorText: Type 93 was an armored car used by the Imperial Japanese Army and naval landing forces in WWII. It had a crew of 4-6 a main armament of 1x 7.7mm Vickers Mk I Medium Machine Gun and a secondary armament of 4x 6.5mm Type 91mm Machine Guns or Nambu Type 11 machine guns.

card_unit_type_95.name: card_unit_type_95
card_unit_type_95.title: TYPE 95 Ha-Go
card_unit_type_95.text: When an order is given, deal 1 damage to the HQ of the player giving the order.
card_unit_type_95.flavorText: Type 95 Ha-Go was a light tank used by the Imperial Japanese Army in WWII. This was the most produced armored vehicle, with 2300 units manufactured. It was considered useful against infantry, but it was not designed to fight other tanks. The Type 95 Ha-Go had a crew of 3, a main armament of Type 94 (1934) 37 mm tank gun and a secondary armament of 2x 7.7 mm Type 97 machine guns.

card_unit_type_96_25mm_aa_gun.name: card_unit_type_96_25mm_aa_gun
card_unit_type_96_25mm_aa_gun.title: TYPE 96 AA GUN
card_unit_type_96_25mm_aa_gun.text: Enemy air units enter the battlefield with defense of 1. Destruction: Draw a card.
card_unit_type_96_25mm_aa_gun.flavorText: The Type 96 25mm Gun was an automatic cannon used by the Imperial Japanese Navy during WWII. It was designed in 1935 as a weapon against armored vehicles and aircraft, but was primarily used as an anti-aircraft gun in fixed mounts with between one and three guns. 33,000 units were built and military personnel generally considered it the most reliable Japanese anti-aircraft gun.

card_unit_type_97.name: card_unit_type_97
card_unit_type_97.title: TYPE 97 Chi-Ha
card_unit_type_97.flavorText: The Type 97 Chi-Ha was a medium tank used by the Imperial Japanese Army in WWII. The tank was widely produced, but after 1941 it was considered less effective than most Allied tank designs. The Type 97 Chi-Ha had a crew of 4, a main armament of Type 97 57 mm tank gun and a secondary armament of 2x 7.7 mm Type 97 machine guns.

card_unit_type_98_ke_ni.name: card_unit_type_98_ke_ni
card_unit_type_98_ke_ni.title: TYPE 98 Ke-Ni
card_unit_type_98_ke_ni.text: Gets +1 attack if you have attacked with another unit this turn.
card_unit_type_98_ke_ni.flavorText: The Type 98 Ke-Ni light tank was designed as a replacement for the older Type 95 Ha-Go light tank. Construction only started in 1942 and only 104 were completed before the end of the war. It had a powerful engine giving it a maximum speed of 50 km/h (31 mph). The Type 98 had a two-man turret, making more room for the commander/gunner to operate the 37mm tank gun.

card_unit_zero.name: card_unit_zero
card_unit_zero.title: A6M2 ZERO
card_unit_zero.flavorText: The Mitsubishi A6M "Zero" was a long-range fighter aircraft, used by the Imperial Japanese Navy from 1940 to 1945. The A6M ZERO was considered one of the best carrier-based fighter aircraft of its time, with excellent maneuverability and a very long range. In the early stages of the war it gained a legendary reputation as a dog fighter and it was not until 1942 that the Allies managed to capture an almost intact Zero and managed to gather intelligence about its strengths and weaknesses. This allowed the Allies to design aircraft to measure up to the Zero, which resulted in the design of the Grummen Hellcat.

card_event_command_failure.name: card_event_command_failure
card_event_command_failure.title: COMMAND FAILURE
card_event_command_failure.text: Destroy target unit with less attack than defense.
card_event_command_failure.flavorText: One notable example of Japanese troops exploiting an Allied weakness during WWII was the capture of Singapore in February 1942. The British had heavily fortified the southern coast of the island, expecting a naval assault, but they neglected to defend the northern part effectively, assuming the dense jungle would prevent an attack from Malaya. Japanese forces, under General Tomoyuki Yamashita, advanced swiftly down the Malay Peninsula, using bicycles and light tanks to move through the jungle terrain, which the British had believed to be impassable. The speed and surprise of the Japanese advance overwhelmed British defenses. When the Japanese reached the unprotected northern side of Singapore, they launched a rapid assault, crossing the Johor Strait and attacking from the landward side. The British forces were not prepared for a land invasion and soon faced shortages of supplies and declining morale. Finally the British forces surrendered on February 15th, 1942, in one of the most significant Allied defeats of the war.

card_event_defeat_in_detail.name: card_event_defeat_in_detail
card_event_defeat_in_detail.title: DEFEAT IN DETAIL
card_event_defeat_in_detail.text: Your units get: "Gets +1+1 when it damages the enemy HQ."
card_event_defeat_in_detail.flavorText: The Battle of Savo Island, also known as the First Battle of the Solomon Sea, was fought on August 8-9, 1942. It was a significant naval battle during WWII and part of the larger Guadalcanal Campaign in the Pacific Theater. It was the first major engagement between Allied and Japanese naval forces following the US invasion of Guadalcanal. A Japanese cruiser force, under Vice Admiral Gunichi Mikawa, launched a surprise night attack on Allied ships patrolling off Savo Island, near Guadalcanal. The Allies, primarily American and Australian forces, were unprepared for the assault. Mikawa’s fleet sank four Allied heavy cruisers (three American, one Australian) and heavily damaged another, marking one of the worst defeats in US Navy history. The Japanese achieved a decisive tactical victory, inflicting heavy losses on the Allies. However, the Japanese failed to press their advantage by not attacking the transport ships supporting the Guadalcanal invasion. This allowed the US forces to maintain a foothold on the island, which became a critical turning point in the Pacific War. The battle highlighted the effectiveness of Japanese night-fighting tactics, which allowed the Japanese Navy to defeat Allied naval forces in detail, suffering only light damage in return.

card_event_duty_bound.name: card_event_duty_bound
card_event_duty_bound.title: DUTY BOUND
card_event_duty_bound.text: Give a friendly unit +1+1, plus +1+1 for each previously played DUTY BOUND.
card_event_duty_bound.flavorText: For Japanese soldiers during WWII, honor was paramount. A soldier was expected to fulfill his duty with no regard for his own life. This put peer pressure on all who fought together and built up determination and disregard for their own self. This fanatical approach made the Japanese fearsome and those who fought against them were often surprised at how willing to sacrifice themselves for duty they were. The phrase "Death is lighter than a feather, but duty is heavier than a mountain" from the 1882 Japanese Imperial Rescript to Soldiers and Sailors embodies the intense sense of honor and self-sacrifice that defined Japan's wartime mentality during World War II. It reflects the belief that death in battle was a noble and inevitable consequence of fulfilling one's duty to the Emperor and country. Soldiers were urged to put aside personal fears, viewing death as insignificant compared to the weight of their obligations. This philosophy encouraged extreme loyalty, often leading to kamikaze missions and other acts of martyrdom during the war.

card_event_exhaust_all_options.name: card_event_exhaust_all_options
card_event_exhaust_all_options.title: EXHAUST ALL OPTIONS
card_event_exhaust_all_options.text: Pin target unit and adjacent units. Pin units deployed and added by the enemy next turn.
card_event_exhaust_all_options.flavorText: The Battle of Bataan was fought from January 7th to April 9th, 1942 and was a major battle opposing the Japanese to the US and Filipino forces during the early stages of WWII in the Pacific Theater. It took place on the Bataan Peninsula in the Philippines and was part of the broader Japanese invasion of the Philippines. Following the attack on Pearl Harbor, Japanese forces advanced across Southeast Asia, and by December 1941, they were pressing into the Philippines. American and Filipino forces, commanded by General Douglas MacArthur and later by Major General Edward P. King, retreated to the Bataan Peninsula, where they established defensive positions. Outnumbered, outgunned, and suffering from severe shortages of food, medicine, and supplies, the defenders fought a grueling, three-month-long battle against the Japanese. Despite their valiant efforts, the Allied forces were overwhelmed by the superior Japanese troops. On April 9th, 1942, Major General King was forced to surrender Bataan, marking one of the largest surrenders in US military history. Around 76,000 American and Filipino soldiers were captured and subjected to the infamous Bataan Death March, during which thousands of prisoners died from exhaustion, disease, and brutal treatment by their captors.

card_event_seek_and_destroy.name: card_event_seek_and_destroy
card_event_seek_and_destroy.title: SEEK AND DESTROY
card_event_seek_and_destroy.text: Your units get: "After this unit attacks the enemy HQ, draw a card."
card_event_seek_and_destroy.flavorText: The Imperial Japanese Army tactical doctrine relied on Fukutsu no seishin, unrelenting spirit. This relied on unrelenting attack, surprise and the destruction of the enemy. Retreat or surrender were not part of this doctrine and the Japanese despised those who surrendered. The weak are meat, the strong eat is a proverb from the 8th century. In the Malayan campaign the Japanese repeatedly infiltrated the defenses of the British Commonwealth army units and had them surrounded before they realized they were under attack.

card_event_shadow_strike.name: card_event_shadow_strike
card_event_shadow_strike.title: SHADOW STRIKE
card_event_shadow_strike.text: Give a friendly unit Shock. At the end of turn, give it Smokescreen if possible.
card_event_shadow_strike.flavorText: Early in WWII, fighter aircraft were largely ineffective at night due to limited visibility, and pilots were not trained for night landings. This allowed Japanese bombers to operate freely, although nighttime navigation was difficult, and bombs were rarely accurate. However, Japanese G4M "Betty" bomber pilots developed deadly night torpedo tactics, using bright floating flares to illuminate Allied ships, like at the Battle of Rennell Island in 1943. As the war progressed the Allies more or less managed to counter these attacks with the advancement of airborne radar technology which allowed night fighters to operate independently to locate and attack the Japanese bombers.

card_unit_388th_independent.name: card_unit_388th_independent
card_unit_388th_independent.title: 388th INDEPENDENT
card_unit_388th_independent.text: Destruction: The enemy draws a card.
card_unit_388th_independent.flavorText: The 388th Independent infantry battalion was part of the 117th Infantry division of the Imperial Japanese Army. In 1945, the 117th Division was transferred to the Kwantung Army. It saw combat during the Soviet invasion of Manchuria and kept fighting even after the official surrender of Japan. The Japanese forces had a formidable reputation and managed to put up strong resistance in some areas. But overall they proved to be no match against the Soviet forces who were battle-hardened veterans from the European theater, and had far superior tanks and equipment.

card_unit_58th_infantry_regiment.name: card_unit_58th_infantry_regiment
card_unit_58th_infantry_regiment.title: 58th INFANTRY REGIMENT
card_unit_58th_infantry_regiment.text: Has +2 attack while it has Shock.
card_unit_58th_infantry_regiment.flavorText: The 58th Infantry Regiment was part of the 31st Division of the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII. The division was formed in Thailand in March 1943 and became part of the Japanese Burma Area Army. On March 15, 1944, the division participated in the Japanese U-GO offensive with the objective of capturing the city of Kohima in British India. During its advance, the division faced strong opposition from Indian and British troops in the Battle of Sangshak, which significantly delayed their progress. The division began the siege of Kohima on April 3, 1944, launching attacks that forced British and Indian defenders into a small defensive area, later known as the Battle of the Tennis Court. By April 17, the defenders were in a desperate situation, but British artillery and RAF air support struck Japanese positions, halting their attacks. The British had gathered significant artillery, while the Japanese had limited artillery and ammunition. With the road to Kohima reopened, the siege was lifted. The remaining forces of the 31st Division continued resisting the Allied reoccupation of Burma but had lost their strength and were no longer an effective fighting unit.

card_unit_77th_regiment.name: card_unit_77th_regiment
card_unit_77th_regiment.title: 77th REGIMENT
card_unit_77th_regiment.text: After this unit destroys a unit, add a 20th INFANTRY REGIMENT to your support line.
card_unit_77th_regiment.flavorText: The 77th Infantry Regiment was a regiment of the 30th Division of the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII. The division was formed in 1943 and was initially stationed on Mindanao in the Philippines, but it was sent to Leyte to reinforce the Japanese defenses during the Battle of Leyte. The division faced heavy fighting, but was unable to stop the US advance. After failing to hold Leyte, the division retreated to Mindanao Island, where it established defensive lines but was overstretched and couldn't prevent US forces from pushing inland. Scattered remnants of the division retreated to the mountains of Central Mindanao, where they survived until Japan's surrender in August 1945. Smaller detachments were eliminated in Sarangani Bay in July 1945.

card_unit_cedar_division.name: card_unit_cedar_division
card_unit_cedar_division.title: CEDAR DIVISION
card_unit_cedar_division.text: Becomes Veteran if you have 4 or less kredit slots.
card_unit_cedar_division.flavorText: The 8th Infantry Division of the Imperial Japanese Army, formed in 1898, was nicknamed Cedar Division (杉兵団, Sugi-heidan). During WWII it served as part of the Kwantung Army in Manchuria until it was transferred to the Philippines in 1944. There, it took part in the intense combat against the US invasion. The 5th Infantry Regiment of 8th Division was transferred to Leyte in late July 1944, and by late December 1944 was nearly completely annihilated during the course of the Battle of Leyte. The remainder of the division were assigned to the 41st Army and suffered heavy losses during the Battle of Manila in January 1945. It fought on until the official surrender of Japan. It is partly famous for one of its officers, Hiroo Onada, a second lieutenant of the Division, who did not surrender until 10 March 1974.

card_unit_fukuoka_regiment.name: card_unit_fukuoka_regiment
card_unit_fukuoka_regiment.title: FUKUOKA REGIMENT
card_unit_fukuoka_regiment.text: Destruction: The enemy gains an extra kredit slot.
card_unit_fukuoka_regiment.flavorText: The 246th Infantry Regiment (Fukuoka) was part of the 112th Division of the Imperial Japanese Army. The division was formed in July 1944 in Korea and later stationed in the Jiandao area of Manchuria. When the Soviet Union invaded Manchuria on August 9th, 1945, the division engaged in heavy defensive battles against Soviet forces, and despite being only 35% combat effective, the division repelled several Soviet attacks, including an armored assault near Michiang on August 11th and another near Unggidong on August 15th. However, following Japan's surrender, the division was ordered to surrender and most of its soldiers were subsequently taken prisoner by the Soviet Red Army.

card_unit_hirosaki_regiment.name: card_unit_hirosaki_regiment
card_unit_hirosaki_regiment.title: HIROSAKI BRIGADE
card_unit_hirosaki_regiment.text: When a friendly unit loses Smokescreen, it gets +1+1 and -1 operation cost.
card_unit_hirosaki_regiment.flavorText: The 59th Infantry brigade (Hirosaki) was a brigade of the 69th Division of the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII. The division was formed on 2 February 1942 and nicknamed the Winning Division (勝兵団, Katsu Heidan). It was assigned to the 1st Army upon formation and tasked with garrisoning central and western Shanxi Province in China. In autumn 1943, it fought in Lanshan County during the Battle of Changde. In March 1944, the divisional headquarters moved to Yuncheng, and the 69th Division joined Operation Ichi-Go in May 1944. After the offensive ended in April 1945, the division was reassigned to garrison duty in China under the 13th Army, where it remained stationed until Japan’s surrender on August 15th, 1945.

card_unit_ki_30_ann.name: card_unit_ki_30_ann
card_unit_ki_30_ann.title: Ki-30 ANN
card_unit_ki_30_ann.text: When this unit attacks, deal 2 damage to the enemy HQ.
card_unit_ki_30_ann.flavorText: The Mitsubishi Ki-30, known to the Allies as the "Ann", was a Japanese light bomber used by the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII. Developed in the late 1930s, the Ki-30 was a monoplane with a single engine, featuring an enclosed cockpit, fixed landing gear, and a crew of two (pilot and observer/gunner). It was designed to be fast and maneuverable, capable of carrying small bomb loads for close air support and tactical bombing missions. The Ki-30 first saw combat during the Second Sino-Japanese War, where it proved effective in low-altitude bombing against Chinese forces. It was well-regarded early on for its simplicity, reliability, and ability to operate from rough airfields. However, by the time the Pacific War began, the Ki-30 was becoming obsolete due to its limited speed, range, and payload capacity compared to newer aircraft. It saw service during the early stages of the war in Southeast Asia, but was gradually phased out from frontline roles by 1942. The Ki-30 could not match the performance of more modern Allied fighters and bombers and was therefore relegated to training and secondary duties. A few surviving planes were also used as kamikaze aircraft later in the war. Despite this, the aircraft played an important role in Japan's early air campaigns and contributed to the initial wave of Japanese successes in Asia.

card_unit_type_4_chi_to.name: card_unit_type_4_chi_to
card_unit_type_4_chi_to.title: TYPE 4 Chi-To
card_unit_type_4_chi_to.text: Your units have +2 attack while they have Shock.
card_unit_type_4_chi_to.flavorText: The Imperial Japanese Army developed the Type 4 Chi-To medium tank towards the end of WWII to counter the M4 Sherman, and it was the most advanced Japanese tank to reach the production stage. It weighed 30 tons, was armed with a Type 5 75 mm gun and two Type 97 heavy machine guns, and was manned by a crew of five. Due to problems and delays in development and the low priority the Japanese gave to tank production, only two Type 4 Chi-To models were built by the end of the war, and they never saw combat.

card_unit_type_92_jyu_shokasa.name: card_unit_type_92_jyu_shokasa
card_unit_type_92_jyu_shokasa.title: TYPE 92 Jyu-Shokosha
card_unit_type_92_jyu_shokasa.text: Gets +1 attack when it damages the enemy HQ.
card_unit_type_92_jyu_shokasa.flavorText: The Type 92 Jyu-Shokosha (meaning heavy armored car), which entered service in 1933, was the first Imperial Japanese Army tankette designed and produced in Japan. Its purpose was to be used by the cavalry for scouting and infantry support. Armed with two machine guns, the Type 92 Jyu-Shokosha performed well against poorly armed enemies. It saw Combat in China and Manchuria during the Second Sino-Japanese War, but was outdated when WWII began. 169 Type 92 tankettes were built by 1939.

card_event_costly_victory.name: card_event_costly_victory
card_event_costly_victory.title: COSTLY VICTORY
card_event_costly_victory.text: Destroy target unit. Remove cards from the top of your deck equal to its attack.
card_event_costly_victory.flavorText: During WWII the Japanese tactical doctrine was built on their inherent faith in superiority of the offense, even when defending they used every effort to regain the offensive and take initiative. The Japanese emphasized on high risk operations, they advanced fast, leaving their forces exhausted, thinly spread and insufficiently supplied. Also, while most military forces kept a reserve, the Japanese were willing to throw their reserve into battle. When this worked, it worked well, especially early in the war as their ferocious attacks unnerved the opponent, who either surrendered or retreated, leaving rations and equipment behind. As the Allied forces adjusted to these shock tactics and started to hold their ground, even in cases where they were surrounded,  the Japanese were much less likely to achieve their objectives and would often suffer terrible losses, not only in combat but also due to starvation and disease.

card_event_experimental_flight.name: card_event_experimental_flight
card_event_experimental_flight.title: EXPERIMENTAL FLIGHT
card_event_experimental_flight.text: Choose and discard a card to add a random Japanese elite air unit to your hand.
card_event_experimental_flight.flavorText: The Nakajima Kikka (j. Orange Blossom) was Japan's first jet aircraft, and almost a copy of the Me 262. It was developed late in WWII and the first prototype had only flown once before the war ended. Another interesting aircraft was the J7W1 Shinden (Magnificent Lightning), a canard design with a pusher propeller and an estimated top speed of 466 miles per hour. Construction started in June 1944 and the prototype was ready 10 months later, but some problems with the engine and propeller delayed the flight tests until August, but by then Japan had surrendered. One design that saw limited use before the end of the war was the kamikaze Ohka Model 11, a manned rocket-powered flying bomb. It was designed to be carried beneath a Mitsubishi G4M Betty bomber until it was close to US fleets. Dropped from the bomber, the pilot of the Ohka would glide down, ignite the rocket engine, and dive into its target. Very few Ohkas ever made it near the US fleet as patrolling fighters shot down most of the G4M Betty bombers before they could get into range to launch their Ohkas.

card_event_greater_purpose.name: card_event_greater_purpose
card_event_greater_purpose.title: GREATER PURPOSE
card_event_greater_purpose.text: Your units get: "Destruction: Draw a card."
card_event_greater_purpose.flavorText: A combination of Bushidō (e. the way of warriors) and State Shintō, a nationalistic official religion of Imperial Japan, made Japanese soldiers extremely devoted religious warriors.  Obedience to the nation and the emperor became a religious duty and many believed that those who surrendered, instead of dying in suicide attacks, or by their own hand, would lose their honor. This is why many Japanese soldiers fought to the last man, and many civilians commited suicide during the last phase of WWII. Many individual soldiers did surrender, but there is no record of a Japanese military unit surrendering in battle.

card_event_outmaneuver.name: card_event_outmaneuver
card_event_outmaneuver.title: OUTMANEUVER
card_event_outmaneuver.text: Target Japanese unit has 0 operation cost this turn. If it has Smokescreen it gets +2+2.
card_event_outmaneuver.flavorText: Up until 1942 the Japanese naval air doctrine focused on long range strikes and surprise attacks where fighters and light attack bombers were used, usually in support of naval operations or amphibious landings. The focus was on swift surprise attacks where they tried to catch the enemy off guard. From 1942 and onward the strength of the Japanese naval air forces were greatly reduced and so was their offensive capability and the air doctrine focused mainly on defensive operations and/or desperate Kamikaze attacks.

card_event_reorganize.name: card_event_reorganize
card_event_reorganize.title: REORGANIZE
card_event_reorganize.text: Choose a card in hand and shuffle it into your deck. Draw a card.
card_event_reorganize.flavorText: The Japanese tactical doctrine throughout the war relied heavily on attack and surprise, to such an extent that the order of “retreat" was banned. Secrecy and deception were the key to almost every operational plan developed by the Japanese, which proved successful early in the war, but soon the Allies knew what to expect and were prepared.

card_event_seize_the_initiative.name: card_event_seize_the_initiative
card_event_seize_the_initiative.title: TAKE INITIATIVE
card_event_seize_the_initiative.text: Draw 1 card. Add TAKE INITIATIVE to the enemy hand with all numericals one higher.
card_event_seize_the_initiative.flavorText: From 1931 and up until 1942 the Japanese conquest of Asia and the Pacific campaign was an overwhelming success. The Allies repeatedly underestimated the strength of the Japanese forces and within 6 months after Pearl Harbor the territory conquered by the Japanese Empire had become immense, stretching over 8 million km2. However, the empire had overextended itself, making it impossible to defend all of its newly claimed territory and soon the Pacific Theater became a war of attrition and Japan was on the losing side.

card_event_sneak_attack.name: card_event_sneak_attack
card_event_sneak_attack.title: SNEAK ATTACK
card_event_sneak_attack.text: Destroy target unit. Remove copies of it from the owner's hand and deck.
card_event_sneak_attack.flavorText: When the Allies finally gained foothold in the Pacific, the Japanese military forces soon experienced one defeat after another, both on land and sea. After the catastrophic loss at the Battle of Midway 1942 the Japanese Navy never gained its offensive momentum again and both the navy and the army were forced on the defensive. By then many in the Japanese leadership knew the war was lost, but soldiers were ordered to stand their ground, no matter how outnumbered they were, and the strategy was to try to draw as much blood as possible from the Americans in the hopes of drawing them to the negotiation table. By the time the Americans had occupied the islands of Iwo Jima and Okinawa there was a force of  2 million men strong on the Japanese mainland, waiting for the final decisive battle, which never occurred. On August 6 and 9, 1945, the Americans dropped two atomic bombs on the cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki with such a devastating effect that the Japanese leadership finally decided to surrender to the Allies.

card_event_yamato.name: card_event_yamato
card_event_yamato.title: IJN YAMATO
card_event_yamato.text: Your Japanese units everywhere get: "Destruction: Deal 2 damage to the enemy HQ."
card_event_yamato.flavorText: The Yamato battleship, named after the ancient Japanese Yamato Province, was the lead ship of the Yamato class of the Imperial Japanese Navy during WWII. Yamato and her sister ship Musashi were the heaviest and most powerfully armed battleships ever built in history. Yamato exceeded other countries' battleships not only by the displacement and the calibre of her guns, but also by the construction of her hull, armour protection, gunnery and optics which gave her tremendous precision to her main gunfire. The construction of these ships was an incredible achievement for the Japanese naval engineering and shipbuilding industry by any international standard. In 1945 Yamato was dispatched on a mission to Okinawa with orders to beach herself and defend the island until destroyed. On her way to Okinawa she was spotted by US aircraft and submarines and sunk in an air raid of carrier based bombers and torpedo bombers. The Yamato was lost with almost all hands. Her sister ship Musashi was sunk during the Battle of Leyte Gulf in 1944.

card_unit_dinah_iii.name: card_unit_dinah_iii
card_unit_dinah_iii.title: Ki-46 DINAH III
card_unit_dinah_iii.text: Deployment: Draw two random 1-cost units from your deck.
card_unit_dinah_iii.flavorText: The Mitsubishi Ki-46, Allied code name “Dinah”,  was a Japanese twin engined reconnaissance aircraft used by the Imperial Japanese Army and Navy air forces during WWII. The aircraft came into service in 1941 and was used before and during the Pacific War, mostly for reconnaissance missions. The Ki-46 was considered a difficult aircraft to counter and only a few were intercepted by Allied pilots. Between 1944-45 a high altitude interceptor was developed. It had an armament of two 20mm cannons and one 37mm cannon in an upward position for fighting the B-29 Superfortresses that were bombing the Japanese islands. However, the interceptor variant did not perform well in its new role as it had almost no armor, it lacked self sealing fuel tanks and was slow to climb.

card_unit_japan_ki_100_goshiken.name: card_unit_japan_ki_100_goshiken
card_unit_japan_ki_100_goshiken.title: Ki-100 GOSHIKISEN
card_unit_japan_ki_100_goshiken.text: Is immune to damage during your turn.
card_unit_japan_ki_100_goshiken.flavorText: The Kawasaki Ki-100 was a Japanese fighter aircraft that was used during WWII. The Ki-100 was first used in combat in March 1945 and although very few aircraft were available, it proved to be one of the most advanced fighters of WWII. The Ki-100 was able to outmaneuver American fighters such as the Republic P-47N Thunderbolts and P-51D Mustangs and it performed very well as an interceptor against the B-29 Superfortresses. 396 Ki-100’s were produced in a short period of time, including a few variants.

card_unit_kawanishi_h6k.name: card_unit_kawanishi_h6k
card_unit_kawanishi_h6k.title: KAWANISHI H6K
card_unit_kawanishi_h6k.flavorText: The Kawanishi H6K  was a Japanese all-metal flying boat that was first used in service during the Sino-Japanese War in 1938. During WWII the H6K was used extensively for maritime reconnaissance and bombing roles, but in 1942 it was considered too vulnerable to the new generation of Allied fighters. The H6K remained in service until the end of the war, but was removed from frontline service and used for reconnaissance and transport duties in areas where little fighter opposition was expected. 215 aircraft were manufactured, including variants.

card_unit_ki_83.name: card_unit_ki_83
card_unit_ki_83.title: Ki-83
card_unit_ki_83.text: At the start of your turn, you draw a card and the enemy draws 2 cards.
card_unit_ki_83.flavorText: The Mitsubishi Ki-83 was a Japanese experimental long range heavy fighter that was designed near the end of WWII. Only four prototypes were produced in 1944 and during flight tests it showed great potential. The aircraft had great maneuverability, a speed of over 644 km/h and a powerful armament. However, before the Ki-83 entered production the war was over.

card_unit_mikawa_regiment.name: card_unit_mikawa_regiment
card_unit_mikawa_regiment.title: MIKAWA REGIMENT
card_unit_mikawa_regiment.text: Deployment: Increase the cost of all cards in your hand by 1.
card_unit_mikawa_regiment.flavorText: The 18th Infantry Regiment Mikawa was a regiment in the Imperial Japanese Army that was formed in 1884 and the majority of the soldiers came from the Mikawa region in the eastern Aichi prefecture of Japan. The regiment participated in the First Sino-Japanese War, the Russo-Japanese War and other conflicts. In 1944, the regiment was deployed to Guam in the Pacific theater as part of the 29th Division, where it was ultimately destroyed by Allied forces.

card_unit_toyama_regiment.name: card_unit_toyama_regiment
card_unit_toyama_regiment.title: TOYAMA REGIMENT
card_unit_toyama_regiment.flavorText: The 69th Infantry Regiment Toyama was a regiment of the 109th Division of the Imperial Japanese Army which was active from 1937 to 1945. The division was sent to China in 1937 where it saw combat but was later assigned to garrison duty in the Shanxi province. The 109th Division was dissolved in 1939 but reformed in 1944 and assigned to the 31st Army. The bulk of the division was assigned to garrison duty on the volcanic islands of Iwo Jima and Chichi Jima and would be wiped out in the Battle of Iwo Jima in 1945.

card_unit_type_92_105mm_field_gun.name: card_unit_type_92_105mm_field_gun
card_unit_type_92_105mm_field_gun.title: TYPE 92 105mm FIELD GUN
card_unit_type_92_105mm_field_gun.flavorText: The Type 92 10 cm cannon was Japanese field gun that was initially designed in the early 1920s but didn’t enter service until 1934. They had a distinct look with their long and slender gun barrels which made them difficult to transport. Despite this they were used in several conflicts and during WWII due to how accurate they were, especially at long ranges. Only 180 TYPE 92 105mm field guns were manufactured and they were deployed in Phillipine Islands and at Guadalcanal where they were used to bombard American positions at Henderson Field.

card_unit_type_97_kai.name: card_unit_type_97_kai
card_unit_type_97_kai.title: TYPE 97 SHINHOTO
card_unit_type_97_kai.flavorText: The Type 97 Shinhoto Chi-Ha was a Japanese medium tank that was used during WWII and was considered one of the best Japanese tanks to be used in the Pacific War. The tank was an upgraded version of the Type 97 Chi-Ha medium tank. It used a Type 97 Chi-Ha hull, but came with a larger three man turret that was armed with a high-velocity 47 mm gun instead of the 57 mm gun. Around 930 Type 97 Shinhoto were produced and quite a few of them were converted Type 97 Chi-Ha tanks. The tank had a crew of 5 (Commander, gunner, loader, bow gunner, driver) and a secondary armament of 2 x 7.7 mm Type 97 machine guns.

card_unit_utsunomiya_regiment.name: card_unit_utsunomiya_regiment
card_unit_utsunomiya_regiment.title: UTSUNOMIYA REGIMENT
card_unit_utsunomiya_regiment.text: When the enemy gives an order, deal 2 damage to the enemy HQ.
card_unit_utsunomiya_regiment.flavorText: The 59th Infantry regiment Utsunomiya was a regiment of the 14th Division (codenamed the Shining Division) of the Imperial Japanese Army and was first formed in 1905. During WWII the division was assigned to garrison duty in China in 1942. As the situation in the Pacific deteriorated the division was split up and deployed on various islands in the Pacific, including Angaur and Peleliu. One battalion of the 59th Infantry Regiment was stationed in the island of Angaur and the rest were sent to the Babeldaob island. The island of Babeldaob was never invaded by the Allies, but the Battle of Angaur and the Battle of Peleliu were among the bloodiest battles in the Pacific War and almost all defenders were killed.

card_unit_wakamatsu_regiment.name: card_unit_wakamatsu_regiment
card_unit_wakamatsu_regiment.title: WAKAMATSU REGIMENT
card_unit_wakamatsu_regiment.text: Destruction: Destroy all of your WAKAMATSU REGIMENT units.
card_unit_wakamatsu_regiment.flavorText: The 29th Infantry Regiment Wakamatsu was from 1940 attached to the 2nd Division of the Imperial Japanese Army, nicknamed the "Courageous Division". It was one of the divisions that occupied the Dutch East Indies in 1940. In 1942 it was transferred to Papua New Guinea, but from there it was deployed on Guadalcanal where it landed on the west coast of Matanikau River and suffered heavy losses in the Actions along the Matanikau and in the Battle for Henderson Field. After Guadalcanal the 2nd Division was assigned to garrison duties in Malaya and Singapore, but in 1944 the division was sent to Burma where it was almost destroyed while fighting the British reoccupation. The 29th Wakamatsu Regiment was disbanded after the war along with the 2nd Division.

card_unit_yamagata_regiment.name: card_unit_yamagata_regiment
card_unit_yamagata_regiment.title: YAMAGATA REGIMENT
card_unit_yamagata_regiment.text: Has Ambush, Blitz and Fury if you have no cards in hand.
card_unit_yamagata_regiment.flavorText: The 32nd Yamagata Infantry Regiment was attached to the 24th Division of the Imperial Japanese Army. The division was formed in Manchukuo in 1939 and was part of the Manchukuo territorial defense force under the command of the 5th Army group of the Kwantung Army. In 1944 companies from each of the division's regiments were sent to Woleai island in the Pacific. Most of the troops defending the Woleai island died from either starvation, disease or Allied air raids. The remainder of the 24th was sent to Okinawa to defend against an Allied invasion where the division was nearly annihilated during the  Battle of Okinawa in June 1945. Only the 1st and 3rd battalions of the 32nd Yamagata Infantry Regiment continued to fight the US occupation until they surrendered in late August that same year.

card_event_diplomatic_attache.name: card_event_diplomatic_attache
card_event_diplomatic_attache.title: DIPLOMATIC ATTACHÉ
