The regiment carried out harassment bombing raids and precision bombing missions and flew over 23,000 sorties, dropping over 3,000 tons of bombs and 26,000 incendiary shells on Axis targets. They flew Polikarpov U-2 biplanes, which were slow but maneuverable, however, since they could only carry two bombs at a time, each pilot often had to fly eight or more missions per night. The regiment was raised to guards status in 1943 and became known as the 46th "Taman" Guards Night Bomber Aviation Regiment.

card_event_no_retreat.name: card_event_no_retreat
card_event_no_retreat.title: NO RETREAT
card_event_no_retreat.text: Target unit gets: "Cannot Retreat or be Suppressed."
card_event_no_retreat.flavorText: During WWII the Red Army placed emphasis on dealing harshly with soldiers that retreated without orders. Special barrier troops were created that operated behind the front lines with orders to shoot or apprehend soldiers that retreated without permission. During the Battle of Stalingrad these barrier units made 45,000 arrests. 41,000 of the arrested soldiers were immediately returned to their units, while others were either shot or received various other types of punishment.

card_event_parade.name: card_event_parade
card_event_parade.title: PARADE
card_event_parade.text: Draw a random unit from your deck. Duplicate it.
card_event_parade.flavorText: During and shortly after WWII there were two memorable parades held on the Red Square in Moscow: The 1941 October Revolution Parade was held in honor of the October Revolution 24 years earlier and took place during the Battle of Moscow. The second one is the Moscow Victory Parade of 1945 which was dedicated to the Soviet and Allied victory against Nazi Germany and is the largest military parade ever held on Red Square.

card_event_veteran_pilots.name: card_event_veteran_pilots
card_event_veteran_pilots.title: VETERAN PILOTS
card_event_veteran_pilots.text: Choose One - Give a Soviet air unit +1+2 OR immune this turn.
card_event_veteran_pilots.flavorText: WWII didn’t start well for the Soviet Air Force as a large portion of their aircraft fleet was destroyed during the early stages of Operation Barbarossa. On top of that the Soviet pilots and ground crew lacked experience and were badly equipped compared to the German Luftwaffe. Gradually the tables turned and the Soviet Air Force managed to gain air supremacy, and although the Luftwaffe still had better performing pilots, they could not outperform the Soviet aircraft production combined with the aircraft received through the Lend-Lease program. The Soviet Air Force could not outclass the Axis air forces when it came to top scoring fighter aces, but they did outperform the Allied nations. The top Soviet fighter ace scored 66 victories during WWII while the top British and American aces scored 40 each.

card_unit_10th_guards_regiment.name: card_unit_10th_guards_regiment
card_unit_10th_guards_regiment.title: 10th GUARDS REGIMENT
card_unit_10th_guards_regiment.flavorText: The 10th Rifle Regiment was attached to the 45th Rifle Division that was formed in 1919 during the Russian Civil War. The division participated in the Polish-Soviet War (1919-21) and the Soviet Invasion of Poland in 1939. The division was destroyed in 1941 during Operation Barbarossa, but reformed in 1942 and sent to fight in the Battle of Stalingrad. The division was designated the 74th Guards Rifle Division in 1943 and participated in several battles and operations before it was disbanded in 1946.

card_unit_1271st_rifles.name: card_unit_1271st_rifles
card_unit_1271st_rifles.title: 1271st RIFLES
card_unit_1271st_rifles.text: Deployment: Add RESERVES to your hand.
card_unit_1271st_rifles.flavorText: The 1271st Rifle Regiment was attached to the 387th Rifle Division which was raised in 1941 as an infantry division of the Red Army. The division first saw combat during the Battle of Moscow in 1942 and later that year it joined the 2nd Guards Army to fight against the German Army Group Don that was sent to relieve the 6th Army at Stalingrad. For two years the 387th Rifle Division served under different commands, but rejoined the 2nd Guards Army in 1944 for the Crimean Offensive. Lastly the division was assigned to the 2nd Ukrainian Front and spent the last weeks of the war in Austria and Hungary. The 387th Rifle Division served for an additional three years into the postwar period and was disbanded in 1947.

card_unit_34th_guards.name: card_unit_34th_guards
card_unit_34th_guards.title: 34th GUARDS
card_unit_34th_guards.text: If in your hand, this unit costs 2 less each time your HQ takes friendly damage.
card_unit_34th_guards.flavorText: The 34th Guards Rifle Regiment was part of the 13th Poltava Guards Rifle Division of the Red Army during WWII. The division was originally formed in 1941 as the 87th Rifle Division, but re-formed and re-designated in 1942 as the 13th Guards Rifle Division. The division fought in several battles and campaigns such as the Battle of Kharkov, Battle of Stalingrad, Battle of Kursk, Operation Bagration and the Battle for Berlin. The division earned several honors and decorations for their outstanding service during WWII.

card_unit_6th_motor_rifles.name: card_unit_6th_motor_rifles
card_unit_6th_motor_rifles.title: 15th MOTOR RIFLES
card_unit_6th_motor_rifles.text: Your HQ is immune to damage on enemy turns.
card_unit_6th_motor_rifles.flavorText: The 15th Guards Rifle Regiment became part of the 2nd Guards RIfle Division in its second formation in 1942. After participating in the Novorossiysk-Taman offensive in 1943 the division was renamed to 2nd Guards (Tamanskaya) Motor Rifle Division and that same year it was under the command of the 56th Army in the Kerch-Eltigen Operation. In 1944 the division participated in the Crimean Offensive under the command of the Separate Coastal Army, and after that it was held in reserve with the 2nd Guards Army, or until July 1944 when the whole army was moved to the 1st Baltic Front. The division fought in the Battle of Memel in 1944 before it was transferred to the 3rd Belorussian Front to participate in the East Prussian offensive. When the war ended the 2nd Guards Motor Rifle Division was located in the Baltic Sea coast north of Primorsk.

card_unit_83rd_naval_brigade.name: card_unit_83rd_naval_brigade
card_unit_83rd_naval_brigade.title: 83rd NAVAL BRIGADE
card_unit_83rd_naval_brigade.text: Deployment: Destroy an enemy unit that is damaged.
card_unit_83rd_naval_brigade.flavorText: The 83rd Naval Infantry Brigade was formed in 1942 at Novorossiysk, which is a port city on the Black Sea. In 1943 the brigade took part in two amphibious operations in an attempt to seize Novorossiysk from German hands. The first operation was unsuccessful but in their second attempt they managed to capture the city. The 83rd Naval Infantry Brigade then became part of the 18th Landing Army which took part in an amphibious landing on the Kerch Peninsula of the Crimea where they managed to capture the peninsula. In 1944 the brigade became part of the Separate Coastal Army and participated in heavy fighting in Crimea, before being transferred to the 3rd Ukrainian Front where they participated in the offensives into Romania and Hungary. Their last amphibious landing was done in 1945 where they made an assault across the Danube River in Budapest and helped clear the city of Axis resistance. When the war ended the brigade was attached to the 5th Guards Tank Army in the Czechoslovakian capital of Prague.

card_unit_845th_rifles.name: card_unit_845th_rifles
card_unit_845th_rifles.title: 845th RIFLES
card_unit_845th_rifles.text: When this unit is dealt damage, your HQ gets equal amount of defense.
card_unit_845th_rifles.flavorText: The 845th Rifle Regiment was part of the 303rd Rifle Division during WWII. The division was formed shortly after the German invasion in 1941 and participated in the Yelnya Offensive and later in Operation Typhoon, where the division was destroyed. The division was formed again in 1942, but it wasn’t until 1943 that it saw active combat in the Battle of Kursk. The division participated in several engagements towards and after the end of the war, such as the Siege of Budapest and finally the Prague Offensive. The division was disbanded in the summer of 1946.

card_unit_kv_ii.name: card_unit_kv_ii
card_unit_kv_ii.title: KV-2
card_unit_kv_ii.text: Order damage to a friendly unit is reduced by its Heavy Armor.
card_unit_kv_ii.flavorText: The Kliment Voroshilov was a Soviet heavy tank, named after the Soviet defense commissar and politician Kliment Voroshilov, and used by the Red Army during WWII. The KV-2 was a heavy assault tank with a main armament of a M-10 152 mm howitzer, and due to the size of the turret it had a much higher profile than the KV-1 and much heavier as well. The KV-2 was produced at the same time as the KV-1, but due to its heavy weight and slow speed it was considered ineffective in combat and only 334 tanks were produced. The KV-2 had a crew of 6 and a secondary armament of 2× DT machine guns.

card_unit_mig_3.name: card_unit_mig_3
card_unit_mig_3.title: MIG 3
card_unit_mig_3.text: If in your hand, this unit costs 2 less each time an enemy countermeasure triggers.
card_unit_mig_3.flavorText: The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-3 was a Soviet fighter and interceptor aircraft used during WWII by the Soviet Air Force. The MiG-3 was built in large numbers in 1941-42 and at the beginning of Operation Barbarossa in June 1941, 981 aircraft were in Soviet service. However, due to the fact that the aircraft was designed for high-altitude combat it was difficult to use over the Eastern Front where aerial combat generally took place at low and medium altitudes. This made the the MiG-3 inferior, both to other Soviet and Allied contemporaries and the German Messerschmitt Bf 109. The Soviets also experimented with the MiG-3 as a fighter-bomber, but it was not suited for this role and before the end of WWII the aircraft was withdrawn from service. By that time 3,422 aircraft had been built and 1,432 of them had been shot down.

card_unit_polikarpov_po_2.name: card_unit_polikarpov_po_2
card_unit_polikarpov_po_2.title: POLIKARPOV PO-2
card_unit_polikarpov_po_2.flavorText: The Polikarpov Po-2 was a Soviet biplane produced from 1928 to 1952, and was one of the most produced aircraft in history, with as many as 30,000 built. The Po-2 served many roles in WWII, as a reconnaissance aircraft, light and short range bomber, night ground attack aircraft, transportation and military liaison aircraft, and from the beginning it was used as a civil and military trainer. A variant was also used as an agricultural aircraft, which earned it its nickname Kukuruznik (Russian for "crop duster"). German troops nicknamed it Nähmaschine (German for “sewing machine”) because of its rattling sound.

card_unit_polikarpov_po_2_ii.name: card_unit_polikarpov_po_2_ii
card_unit_polikarpov_po_2_ii.title: POLIKARPOV PO-2-II
card_unit_polikarpov_po_2_ii.text: Destruction: Add a FROM THE PEOPLE to your hand.

card_unit_p_40b_tomahawk.name: card_unit_p_40b_tomahawk
card_unit_p_40b_tomahawk.title: P-40B TOMAHAWK
card_unit_p_40b_tomahawk.text: Infantry units you deploy or add get +1+1.
card_unit_p_40b_tomahawk.flavorText: The P-40B Tomahawk was an American fighter and ground attack aircraft used during WWII by many Allied air forces. The Soviet military and naval air forces received 247 P-40Bs from the Americans through the Lend Lease agreement. The aircraft were shipped from Great Britain or from the US and many of them arrived incomplete and had to be assembled in the USSR. Soviet test flights showed some defects in test flights, but the Tomahawks were nevertheless used right away in front line services. The P-40Bs were a good match against the German BF 109s, the range and fuel capacity was superior to most of the Soviet fighters, but the biggest complaint was about its poor climb rate and problems with maintenance. The P-40 was mostly used by the Soviet Air Force in 1942 and early 1943, but after that many of them were replaced with the Soviet Lavochkin La-5 and Yakovlev fighters.

card_unit_su_85.name: card_unit_su_85
card_unit_su_85.title: SU-85
card_unit_su_85.text: Your HQ gains +3 defense when you attack with a Soviet tank.
card_unit_su_85.flavorText: The SU-85 was a Soviet self-propelled gun used by the Red Army during WWII. The full name of the gun was Samohodnaya ustanovka 85, it had a crew of 4 (commander, driver, gunner, loader) and a main armament of an 85 mm D-5T gun that was based on the chassis of a T-34 tank. The gun was produced in 1943 and supplied to the Red Army that was desperately in need of an anti-tank weapon that could counter the new German Tiger tank, and later the Panther tank. 2,050 SU-85s were manufactured from 1943 to 1944.

card_unit_t_70eot.name: card_unit_t_70eot
card_unit_t_70eot.title: T-70
card_unit_t_70eot.text: Destroyed at the end of the second turn on the battlefield.
card_unit_t_70eot.flavorText: The T-70 was a Soviet light tank used by the Red Army during WWII. It was used for reconnaissance and infantry support, but it was known for taking out enemy German tanks in combat. The T-70 had a 2 man crew, a main armament of a 45 mm Model 1932/38 20-K gun and a secondary armament of 7.62 mm DT coaxial machine gun. It was produced from 1942 to 1943 and 8,226 units were built.

card_unit_t_80.name: card_unit_t_80
card_unit_t_80.title: T-80
card_unit_t_80.text: Destruction: Deal 1 damage to your HQ.
card_unit_t_80.flavorText: The T-80 was a Soviet light tank that was used by the Red Army during WWII. The T-80 was a T-70 variant, and a more advanced version with a two man turret, increased firepower, improved armor, and a 3 man crew instead of 2. The tank came into service in 1943, and at a time when all other light tank production had been halted, so only a very small number was produced. The T-80 had a main armament of a 45 mm 20-K cannon and a secondary armament of a single 7.62 mm DT machine gun.

card_event_arctic_convoy.name: card_event_arctic_convoy
card_event_arctic_convoy.title: ARCTIC CONVOY
card_event_arctic_convoy.text: Draw two random units from your deck.
card_event_arctic_convoy.flavorText: The Arctic convoys were oceangoing merchant convoys which sailed the Norwegian Sea and the Arctic Ocean. The convoys sailed from the United Kingdom, Iceland, and North America to northern ports in the Soviet Union – primarily Arkhangelsk (Archangel) and Murmansk in Russia.

card_event_assault.name: card_event_assault
card_event_assault.title: FRONTAL ASSAULT
card_event_assault.text: Give your LIGHT INFANTRY units +1+2. If you have none, add two to your hand.
card_event_assault.flavorText: A frontal assault is a military tactic which is a direct movement of forces towards the front of an enemy position. Often this tactic is used as a last resort since the attackers are subjecting themselves to the maximum defensive power of the enemy. The risks can be minimized to some extent by the use of cover, such as smokescreen or darkness of night, and use of heavy supporting fire or diversionary attacks. There is a misconception that the Red Army relied mostly on frontal assaults or “human wave attack” tactics, but they did occur, same as in all armies fighting in WWII.

card_event_bloody_sickle.name: card_event_bloody_sickle
card_event_bloody_sickle.title: BLOODY SICKLE
card_event_bloody_sickle.text: Deal 1 damage to a unit and your HQ. Draw a card.
card_event_bloody_sickle.flavorText: A sickle is a tool for cutting grain, grass, etc. and although it would serve well as a melee weapon than what is being referred to here as the sickle and hammer, the coat of arms of the Soviet Union and Communist symbol represented the proletarian struggle.

card_event_blood_red_sky.name: card_event_blood_red_sky
card_event_blood_red_sky.title: BLOOD RED SKY
card_event_blood_red_sky.text: Give all friendly Soviet air units +2+2.
card_event_blood_red_sky.flavorText: Operation Barbarossa, the German invasion of Soviet Union, started disastrously for the Soviet Air Force. Just in the first couple of days of the invasion their air force lost roughly 2000 airplanes. However, they slowly gained the upper hand, with a modernized air force and better trained pilots that became an equal match to the Germans.

card_event_burning_sky.name: card_event_burning_sky
card_event_burning_sky.title: BURNING SKY
card_event_burning_sky.text: Deal 4 damage to an enemy air unit.
card_event_burning_sky.flavorText: The Soviet Air Defence Forces played a major role in defending Soviet cities against air attacks, mainly in industrial areas. Over the course of WWII they destroyed 7,313 German aircraft. More than 80,000 soldiers, sergeants, officers and generals of the Country Air Defence Forces were awarded state orders and medals, and 92 soldiers were awarded the title of Hero of the Soviet Union and one was twice given the honor.

card_event_close_combat.name: card_event_close_combat
card_event_close_combat.title: CLOSE COMBAT
card_event_close_combat.text: Friendly infantry units have +3 attack until end of turn.
card_event_close_combat.flavorText: Vasily Chuikov, the Soviet commander of 62nd Army, developed a close combat tactic during the Battle of Stalingrad that was referred to as “hugging the enemy”, by which under-armed Soviet soldiers kept the German army so close to them as to minimize the superior firepower enjoyed by the Wehrmacht.

card_event_critical_hit.name: card_event_critical_hit
card_event_critical_hit.title: CRITICAL HIT
card_event_critical_hit.flavorText: A critical hit does significantly more damage than usual. The image is taken from a Soviet propaganda poster and shows a tiger, representing the invading Axis forces, being stabbed through the mouth by a Red Army bayonet.

card_event_final_push.name: card_event_final_push
card_event_final_push.title: FINAL PUSH
card_event_final_push.text: Give a friendly unit +3 attack. Destroy it at the end of your turn.
card_event_final_push.flavorText: Perhaps the most famous final push occurred in the Battle or Berlin, which was the final major Soviet offensive of the European Theater. Before the battle was over, Hitler and several of his followers committed suicide, and it was followed by the unconditional surrender of the German forces. The Battle for Berlin marks the end of WWII in Europe.

card_event_from_the_people.name: card_event_from_the_people
card_event_from_the_people.title: FROM THE PEOPLE
card_event_from_the_people.flavorText: The war against Nazi Germany was called the Great Patriotic War in the Soviet Union, and for a good reason. It was not only the Soviet soldiers on the battlefield that made great sacrifices, but also the millions of workers that were mobilized in the rear to work for the war effort. History shows that many of these workers suffered unimaginable deprivations, but despite this, all the evidence points to the fact that workers willingly endured these hardships for the sake of the motherland and for the struggle against the German occupation.

card_event_mass_attack.name: card_event_mass_attack
card_event_mass_attack.title: MASS ATTACK
card_event_mass_attack.text: Deal damage to target equal to number of units you control.
card_event_mass_attack.flavorText: The battles on the Eastern Front of the Second WWII constituted the largest military confrontation in history. During the first phase of the conflict the Red Army was fighting a defensive war, but in November 1942 the Red Army launched a massive counteroffensive in an attempt to conquer Stalingrad. The Soviet forces managed to encircle and trap the German Sixth Army, which surrendered to the Red Army in early 1943. After the victory at Stalingrad the Red Army remained on the offensive until they were on German soil, which ended with the unconditional surrender of Germany in Berlin.

card_event_mother_russia.name: card_event_mother_russia
card_event_mother_russia.title: MOTHER RUSSIA
card_event_mother_russia.text: Add to hand a copy of each friendly Soviet unit destroyed so far this turn.
card_event_mother_russia.flavorText: Many Soviet WWII slogans urged Russians to fight for "Mother Russia", which symbolized the vast homeland which needed protection from the invading forces.

card_event_no_surrender.name: card_event_no_surrender
card_event_no_surrender.title: NO SURRENDER
card_event_no_surrender.text: Add LIGHT INFANTRY to your support line until it is full. Give them Blitz.
card_event_no_surrender.flavorText: In 1942 Joseph Stalin issued "Order 227", which stated that no commander had the right to retreat without an order. This was a symbolic drawing of a line, a decision that no further retreat was possible and that it was time for the Red Army to turn and face the enemy and make a stand. The order is most famous for its line "Not a step back!", which became a slogan of the Soviet resistance against the Nazi invasion.

card_event_order_no_227.name: card_event_order_no_227
card_event_order_no_227.title: ORDER 227
card_event_order_no_227.text: Give your damaged Soviet units +2 attack and fully repair them.
card_event_order_no_227.flavorText: Order 227 was an order issued by Joseph Stalin on July 28th, 1942. The order was issued in order to reestablish discipline in the Soviet Army against Nazi Germany, and it is most famous for its line "Not a step back!", which became a slogan of the Soviet resistance against the Nazi invasion.

card_event_patriotic_firestorm.name: card_event_patriotic_firestorm
card_event_patriotic_firestorm.title: PATRIOTIC FIRESTORM
card_event_patriotic_firestorm.text: Your support line units have + 2 attack until end of turn.
card_event_patriotic_firestorm.flavorText: This slogan derives from the term "The Great Patriotic War", a term used in Russia and many other former republics of the Soviet Union to describe the conflict between the Soviet Union and Nazi Germany and its Allies during WWII.

card_event_patriotic_war.name: card_event_patriotic_war
card_event_patriotic_war.title: GREAT PATRIOTIC WAR
card_event_patriotic_war.text: Set the defense of each HQ to 12.
card_event_patriotic_war.flavorText: The Great Patriotic War is a term used in Russia and other former republics of the Soviet Union (except for the Baltic states and Ukraine) to describe the conflict on the Eastern Front between the Soviet Union and Germany and its Allies, from June 22, 1941 to May 9, 1945. The Great Patriotic War is commemorated on May 9th each year.

card_event_red_banner.name: card_event_red_banner
card_event_red_banner.title: RED BANNER
card_event_red_banner.text: Destroy a friendly unit. Add a random unit from same nation that costs 2 more.
card_event_red_banner.flavorText: In Russia and other former Soviet countries, WWII is referred to as the Great Patriotic War, and it is a remembrance of a great sacrifice by the Soviet people, soldiers and civilians alike. Soviet losses during WWII are now estimated to be approximately 26.6 million citizens, and account for half of all WWII casualties, and the brutal battles fought by the Soviets on the Eastern Front (for example, the Siege of Stalingrad and the Battle of Kursk) had no parallel on the Western Front.

card_event_red_october.name: card_event_red_october
card_event_red_october.title: RED OCTOBER
card_event_red_october.text: Give a Soviet tank or infantry +3+3.
card_event_red_october.flavorText: The October revolution is the revolution of 1917 in Russia which was led by the by the Bolshevik Party of Vladimir Lenin. It ended with the overthrow of the provisional government led by Kerensky and the formation of the Soviet Union.

card_event_reserves.name: card_event_reserves
card_event_reserves.title: RESERVES
card_event_reserves.text: Add two LIGHT INFANTRY to your hand, plus one for each previously played RESERVES.
card_event_reserves.flavorText: During WWII the Soviet Red Army formed a group of Reserve Armies who operated in the rear. Their purpose was to train newly formed units and to reconstitute destroyed armies or to form new armies. When the Axis forces invaded the Soviet Union, the Red Army had 5.5 million men in active service and 14 million conscripts in reserves, ready to be mobilized. In comparison the Axis forces had a total of 3.8 million men deployed on the Eastern Front. In 1943 the Red Army manpower reserves were running low, but by then they had 10.3 million men and women in active service against the Axis forces which counted a total 3.93 million men.

card_event_scorched_earth.name: card_event_scorched_earth
card_event_scorched_earth.title: SCORCHED EARTH
card_event_scorched_earth.text: Set the operation cost of all units on the battlefield to 4.
card_event_scorched_earth.flavorText: A scorched-earth policy is a military strategy with the aim of destroying anything that may be useful to an advancing or retreating enemy. The fallback is that it often affects both friends and foe.

card_event_siberian_transfer.name: card_event_siberian_transfer
card_event_siberian_transfer.title: SIBERIAN TRANSFER
card_event_siberian_transfer.text: Add a T-34 1942 unit to the support line. Destroy it at end of turn.
card_event_siberian_transfer.flavorText: At the start of the war there were a large numbers of veteran Siberian divisions defending the eastern Soviet borders against a possible attack from the Japanese . After Stalin realized that the Japanese had no intention of attacking he ordered these divisions to be transferred to the front near Moscow in the winter of 1941 and were encountered all along the front protecting the city.

card_event_tamanskya.name: card_event_tamanskya
card_event_tamanskya.title: TAMANSKAYA!
card_event_tamanskya.text: Fully repair all friendly ground units.
card_event_tamanskya.flavorText: Tamanskaya is a nickname for the Soviet 2nd Guards Motor Rifle Division, an elite division which was named Tamanskaya in honor of the Bolshevik revolutionary and Soviet politician Mikhail Kalinin and the town of Taman.

card_event_the_hammer.name: card_event_the_hammer
card_event_the_hammer.title: THE HAMMER
card_event_the_hammer.text: Deal 6 damage to a ground unit.
card_event_the_hammer.flavorText: A hammer is a tool for beating nails, metal etc. and although it has been used as a melee weapon, what is being referred to here is the hammer (and sickle) in the coat of arms of the Soviet Union and Communist symbol for proletarian struggle.

card_event_ural_factories.name: card_event_ural_factories
card_event_ural_factories.title: URAL FACTORIES
card_event_ural_factories.text: Destroy a friendly unit. Add a random unit from same nation that costs 1 more.
card_event_ural_factories.flavorText: When the Germans invaded the Soviet Union in 1941 nearly 16 million Soviet civilians and 1500 large factories were moved to the eastern or middle part of the country. This meant that the Soviet Union managed to continue their military production in the Urals and Soviet Central Asia despite the loss of western industrial zones, and this helped them eventually surpass the Germans in arms production.

card_event_war_production.name: card_event_war_production
card_event_war_production.title: WAR PRODUCTION
card_event_war_production.text: Gain 2 additional kredits this turn. Discard all non-unit cards.
card_event_war_production.flavorText: After the United States, the Soviet Union was the second largest manufacturer during WWII, spending a total of 56.6 billion dollars on military productions. In total they manufactured 238,582 aircraft, 316,869 tanks, SPGs and other vehicles, 716,948 artillery pieces and mortars, 7,477,400 heavy and sub-machine guns. Most of their production efforts were focused on land and air warfare and not so much naval warfare. Only a couple of battleships and cruisers were built, as well as 25 destroyers and 52 submarines.

card_event_winter_war.name: card_event_winter_war
card_event_winter_war.title: WINTER WARFARE
card_event_winter_war.flavorText: The Russian winter was a substantial contributing factor in the Soviet victory over the invading German forces in WWII. The winter temperature in Moscow isn't extremely cold, but it so happens that the winter of 1941-1942 was the coldest of the 20th century. The Wehrmacht was by no means prepared for a winter war, the German high command thought the war would be over long before it would hit, and before winter struck they were already overextended and badly supplied. The Soviets were better prepared, with winter uniforms, equipment designed for the cold and having the huge advantage of being on the defending side, compared to attacking in winter cold.

card_event_workers_unite.name: card_event_workers_unite
card_event_workers_unite.title: WORKERS UNITE!
card_event_workers_unite.text: Discard your LIGHT INFANTRY units. Gain a kredit and draw a card for each.
card_event_workers_unite.flavorText: The essence of this slogan is that members of the working classes throughout the world should cooperate to achieve victory in WWII and overcome the class conflict.

card_event_zhukov.name: card_event_zhukov
card_event_zhukov.title: ZHUKOV
card_event_zhukov.text: Draw a random Soviet infantry. It gets +1+1 and Blitz when deployed.
card_event_zhukov.flavorText: Georgy Konstantinovich Zhukov (1896 –1974) was a Soviet Red Army General who became Chief of General Staff, Deputy Commander-in-Chief, Minister of Defense and a member of the Politburo (Political Bureau of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union). He participated in multiple battles and ended up being commander at the 1st Belorussian Front in the Battle of Berlin, which resulted in the defeat of Germany. Zhukov received multiple decorations and was awarded the Hero of the Soviet Union four times. There is controversy about his legacy as a military commander, but in the end he was a winning general and it is claimed that he never lost a battle.

card_unit_11th_signal_battalion.name: card_unit_11th_signal_battalion
card_unit_11th_signal_battalion.title: 329th ENGINEER BATTALION
card_unit_11th_signal_battalion.text: When another friendly unit is destroyed, your HQ gains +2 defense.
card_unit_11th_signal_battalion.flavorText: The Sappers from the 329th Engineer Battalion were attached to the 7th Guards Army which fought in numerous battles and campaigns on the Eastern Front during WWII, including the Battle of Stalingrad, the Battle of Kursk, the Budapest Offensive and the Prague Offensive. In 1943 during the Battle of Stalingrad, sappers of the 329th Engineer Battalion captured Field­Marshal von Paulus, commander of the 6th German Army, together with soldiers from the Motorized ­Rifle Division.

card_unit_13th_rifle_regiment.name: card_unit_13th_rifle_regiment
card_unit_13th_rifle_regiment.title: 13th RIFLE REGIMENT
card_unit_13th_rifle_regiment.text: Destruction: Add a random Soviet infantry to your hand.
card_unit_13th_rifle_regiment.flavorText: The 13th Rifle Regiment was attached to the 2nd Rifle Division of the Red Army, which served from the Russian Civil War until the end of  WWII. The division fought in numerous battles and operations, for example, the Battle of Moscow, the Siege of Sevastopol, the Leningrad–Novgorod Offensive and the Riga Offensive. The division was twice destroyed and reformed during the war, and was decorated with the Honorary Revolutionary Red Banner (1st Formation) and the Order of Kutuzov (3rd Formation).

card_unit_16th_rifles.name: card_unit_16th_rifles
card_unit_16th_rifles.title: 16th RIFLES
card_unit_16th_rifles.text: At the start of your turn gain +1+1.
card_unit_16th_rifles.flavorText: The 16th Rifle Regiment was attached to the 87th Rifle Division which became the 13th Guards Division in 1942. The division engaged in numerous military operations such as the Soviet invasion of Poland, the Winter War, the Battle of Kharkov, the Battle of Stalingrad, the Battle of Kursk, Operation Bagration, the Battle of Berlin and the Battle of Halbe.

card_unit_2nd_motor.name: card_unit_2nd_motor
card_unit_2nd_motor.title: 2nd RIFLES
card_unit_2nd_motor.text: Has +2 attack against units with Blitz.
card_unit_2nd_motor.flavorText: The 2nd Motorized Rifles Division was formed in 1940 as the 127th Rifle Division. In 1941 they were renamed to the 2nd Guards Rifle Division for their distinguished combat service, and throughout WWII they participated in numerous battles and campaigns on various military fronts. By the end of the war they were one of the most decorated divisions in the Soviet ground forces. In 1946 the division received the honorary name Tamanskaya, named after the Bolshevik revolutionary M. I. Kalinin. The division is still in active service today and their motto is: “Motherland, Honor, Glory”.

card_unit_321st_rifles.name: card_unit_321st_rifles
card_unit_321st_rifles.title: 321st RIFLE REGIMENT
card_unit_321st_rifles.text: Destruction: Add a 1/1 LIGHT INFANTRY to the support line.
card_unit_321st_rifles.flavorText: The 321st Rifle Regiment was attached to the 15th Rifle Division of the Red Army. In 1940 it took part in in the Soviet annexation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina in Romania. The regiment first saw combat in Operation Barbarossa, but participated in numerous battles and campaigns after that, including the Battle of Kursk, Operation Bagration, the East Pomeranian Offensive, and the Battle of Berlin in 1945.

card_unit_35th_rifles.name: card_unit_35th_rifles
card_unit_35th_rifles.title: 35th RIFLE REGIMENT
card_unit_35th_rifles.text: Deploys for 0 kredits if a friendly unit was destroyed this turn.
card_unit_35th_rifles.flavorText: The 35th Rifle Regiment was part of the 30th Rifle Division of the Red Army. The division participated in multiple battles and operations during WWII, including the Battle of Rostov in 1941 and the Tuapse Defensive Operation in 1942 where it fought bravely and was promoted and renamed to the 55th Guards Rifle Division for its actions. In 1943 the division fought at Rostov, Kiev, Zhitomir, and in the Carpathian Mountains, and by 1945 it was with the 38th Army of the 4th Ukrainian Front.

card_unit_3rd_guards.name: card_unit_3rd_guards
card_unit_3rd_guards.title: 3rd GUARDS REGIMENT
card_unit_3rd_guards.flavorText: The 3rd Guards Rifle Regiment was part of the 4th Guards Division, which was created in the aftermath of the fighting for Yelnya, where the Soviet Army won a tactical victory against the Wehrmacht. The 4th Guards fought with distinction in numerous battles and military operations, including the Siege of Leningrad, Operation Little Saturn, the Battle of Stalingrad, the Budapest Offensive and the Vienna Offensive.

card_unit_42nd_rifles.name: card_unit_42nd_rifles
card_unit_42nd_rifles.title: 42nd RIFLES
card_unit_42nd_rifles.text: At the start of your turn, fully repair this unit.
card_unit_42nd_rifles.flavorText: The 42nd Rifle Regiment was attached to the 180th Rifle Division which was first formed in 1940 in the Baltic Special Military District and became the 28th Guards Rifle Division on May 3, 1942. They engaged in the Baltic Operation, Demyansk Pocket, Ostrogozhsk Rossosh Offensive, the Battle of Kiev, the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive and the Siege of Budapest.

card_unit_45mm_anti_tank_gun.name: card_unit_45mm_anti_tank_gun
card_unit_45mm_anti_tank_gun.title: 45 mm ANTI-TANK GUN
card_unit_45mm_anti_tank_gun.flavorText: The 45 mm anti-tank gun M1937 (53-K) was a light and quick-firing anti-tank gun, manufactured and used in the first stage of the German-Soviet War. It was first produced in 1937, but replaced in 1942 by the long-barreled 45 mm anti-tank gun M1942 (M-42).

card_unit_554th_rifles.name: card_unit_554th_rifles
card_unit_554th_rifles.title: 554th RIFLE REGIMENT
card_unit_554th_rifles.flavorText: The 554th Rifle Regiment was attached to the 138th Rifle Division of the Red Army during WWII. It served as a standard rifle division but was converted to a mountain rifle division for two years, then back to a rifle division. The 138th fought in the Finnish Winter War, the Battle of the Kerch Peninsula and the Battle of Stalingrad. After that the division took part in the Belgorod-Kharkov Offensive Operation and then the Korsun Shevchenkovsky Offensive. It ended the war in eastern Czechoslovakia with the divisional honorific "Carpathian", the Order of the Red Banner and the Order of Suvorov. The 138th Division was disbanded after the war in 1945.

card_unit_6th_airborne.name: card_unit_6th_airborne
card_unit_6th_airborne.title: 6th AIRBORNE
card_unit_6th_airborne.text: Deployment: Add a T-34 1942 to your support line. Destroy it at end of turn.
card_unit_6th_airborne.flavorText: The 6th Airborne Guards were attached to the 1st Guards Airborne Division which was formed in 1942 and participated in numerous battles and operations during WWII. They fought in the Battle of the Dnieper, the Battle of the Korsun–Cherkassy Pocket, the Uman–Botosani Offensive, the Jassy–Kishinev Offensive, the Battle of Debrecen, the Siege of Budapest and the Prague Offensive. In August 1945 it was sent east and fought in the Soviet invasion of Manchuria.

card_unit_6th_naval_brigade.name: card_unit_6th_naval_brigade
card_unit_6th_naval_brigade.title: 6th NAVAL BRIGADE
card_unit_6th_naval_brigade.flavorText: During WWII the Soviet Navy began forming and training Infantry Navy Battalions and around 350,000 Red Navy sailors fought on land in the war. The Naval Infantry conducted over 114 landings, many were also parachute trained, but mostly they served as regular infantry. The 6th Naval Brigade served under the 138th Rifle Division from 1943 and participated in various battles and campaigns on the Eastern Front.

card_unit_756th_regiment.name: card_unit_756th_regiment
card_unit_756th_regiment.title: 756th REGIMENT
card_unit_756th_regiment.text: When this unit attacks and destroys a unit, deal excess damage to the enemy HQ.
card_unit_756th_regiment.flavorText: The 756th Regiment was part of the 150th Rifle Division. It was formed in 1939 and participated in the invasion of Poland. During the war on the Eastern Front it fought in many places, always distinguishing itself and was regarded as an elite force. It was given the honorific title of “Idritskaya” in July 1944 for its heroic battle in the town of Idritsa. But it most famous moment was being the unit that raised the Soviet banner on the roof of the Reichstag in Berlin in April 1945.

card_unit_76mm_howitzer_1939.name: card_unit_76mm_howitzer_1939
card_unit_76mm_howitzer_1939.title: 76 mm HOWITZER 1939
card_unit_76mm_howitzer_1939.flavorText: The 76-mm Howitzer 1939 was a Soviet 76.2 mm cannon used in WWII by the Red Army. It was a designated divisional gun, issued to batteries under the direct control of division headquarters. The gun was produced from 1939 to 1941, with 9,812 units built, and it was used extensively throughout the war.

card_unit_84th_infantry.name: card_unit_84th_infantry
card_unit_84th_infantry.title: 84th INFANTRY REGIMENT
card_unit_84th_infantry.flavorText: The 84th Infantry Regiment was attached to the 6th Rifle Division of the Red Army in WWII. In the opening stages of Operation Barbarossa the division was stationed in Brest in Belarus and took part in the defense of the Brest Fortress, which later became a symbol of Soviet resistance. The 6th Rifle Division took part in many military operations during WWII, including the Third Battle of Kharkov, the Battle of the Korsun Cherkassy Pocket, the Soviet invasion of Manchuria. The division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner twice and the Order of Suvorov 2nd Class for its valor in combat.

card_unit_85mm_d44.name: card_unit_85mm_d44
card_unit_85mm_d44.title: 85mm D-44 FIELD GUN
card_unit_85mm_d44.text: Units damaged by 85mm D-44 FIELD GUN and their adjacent units get pinned.
card_unit_85mm_d44.flavorText: The 85-mm divisional D-44 field gun was a Soviet artillery gun used during the late phases of WWII. It was designed to replace the 76 mm divisional gun M1942 (ZiS-3) and was produced from 1944 to 1953. It could fire up to 20 rounds per minute and had a maximum firing range of 15.65 km.

card_unit_89th_infantry.name: card_unit_89th_infantry
card_unit_89th_infantry.title: 89th INFANTRY REGIMENT
card_unit_89th_infantry.flavorText: The 89th Infantry Regiment were attached to the 23rd Rifle Division of the Red Army. During WWII the 23rd engaged in several military campaigns, including the Battle of Stalingrad, the Battle of Kiev in 1943, Operation Bagration and the Berlin Offensive. In 1943 it became the 71st Guards Rifle Division for its actions in the Battle of Stalingrad and was awarded the Order of the Red Banner, the Order of Suvorov 2nd Class, and the Order of Kutuzov 2nd Class for its actions.

card_unit_93rd_guards.name: card_unit_93rd_guards
card_unit_93rd_guards.title: 1st RIFLES
card_unit_93rd_guards.text: Destruction: Add a 2nd RIFLES to your support line.
card_unit_93rd_guards.flavorText: The 1st Rifles Regiment was attached to the 99th Rifle Division of the Red Army. In 1939 it took part in the Soviet invasion of Poland as part of 13th Rifle Corps of the 12th Army. In 1941, during Operation Barbarossa, most of the division was killed or captured in the Battle of Uman, and again in the Second Battle of Kharkov. The division was reorganized in 1942 and sent to fight in Stalingrad and from there it was transferred to the Don Front. In April 1943 the division was raised to Guards status and became the 88th Guards Rifle Division. During the final stages of the war the division fought with the 46th Army of the 2nd Ukrainian Front and by the end of the war it was disbanded.

card_unit_95th_rifles.name: card_unit_95th_rifles
card_unit_95th_rifles.title: 95th RIFLE REGIMENT
card_unit_95th_rifles.text: Deployment: Deal 1 damage to a unit and your HQ.
card_unit_95th_rifles.flavorText: The 95th Rifle Regiment was attached to the 14th Rifle Division of the Red Army which was formed in 1922 in Moscow. During WWII the division saw combat in Operation Silver Fox in 1941, which was a German-Finnish offensive with the objective of capturing the Soviet port at Murmansk, and later it took part in the Petsamo-Kirkenes Offensive in 1944 where the Red Army defeated the Wehrmacht's forces in the Arctic of Northern Finland and Norway. In December 1944 the division was transformed into the 101st Guards Rifle Division.

card_unit_a20_soviet.name: card_unit_a20_soviet
card_unit_a20_soviet.title: A-20B
card_unit_a20_soviet.text: Costs 1 less for each US unit you control.
card_unit_a20_soviet.flavorText: The Douglas A-20B Havoc was an American light bomber, intruder, and reconnaissance aircraft used by the Allied powers in WWII.  In total 7,478 units were manufactured, and through the Allied Lend-Lease program the Soviet Air Force received around one third of them, making it the most numerous foreign bomber in their inventory. The Soviets considered it a powerful and reliable aircraft that could be flown even by crews with minimal training.

card_unit_armored_train.name: card_unit_armored_train
card_unit_armored_train.title: BP-43 ARMORED TRAIN
card_unit_armored_train.text: Can't attack. At the end of your turn, add a LIGHT INFANTRY to the same front.
card_unit_armored_train.flavorText: The BP-43 was an armored transport train that was used by the Red Army during WWII. It was developed in 1943 and designed to withstand both Axis air and ground attacks while carrying huge amounts of supplies to the battlefield. The BP-43 had six separate armored cars, each protected with a 50 mm armor and mounted with a 76.2 mm gun in a T-34 Medium Tank turret, a 37 mm anti-aircraft gun and machine gun ports. The locomotive weighted 362.8 metric tons, plus the optional flat cars for transport, and had a crew of over 100 men. Around 21 BP-43 armored trains were created during WWII.

card_unit_b4_203mm_howitzer.name: card_unit_b4_203mm_howitzer
card_unit_b4_203mm_howitzer.title: B-4 203mm HOWITZER
card_unit_b4_203mm_howitzer.text: Units damaged by this unit get -3 attack until end of turn.
card_unit_b4_203mm_howitzer.flavorText: The B-4 203 mm howitzer M1931 was a heavy howitzer used by the Soviet Red Army during WWII. These guns were nicknamed "Stalin's sledgehammer" by German soldiers and were mainly used against heavy enemy fortifications and in urban combat for crushing protected buildings and bunkers. The 203mm howitzer was produced from 1932 to the 1940s and 871 units were built.

card_unit_bt_7.name: card_unit_bt_7
card_unit_bt_7.title: BT-7
card_unit_bt_7.flavorText: The BT 7 was a light tank and was produced between 1935 and 1940. It was nicknamed “Betka and/or Betushka” and was the last one of the BT series of Soviet cavalry tanks. In 1940 the BT 7 was more or less replaced by the T-34 medium tank.

card_unit_cossack_cavalry.name: card_unit_cossack_cavalry
card_unit_cossack_cavalry.title: 4th KUBAN COSSACKS
card_unit_cossack_cavalry.flavorText: Although the Cossacks fought for both sides during WWII, most of them fought for the Soviet Union. They led attacks during the Battle of Stalingrad and were able to keep the Germans from entering the Caucasus. The 4th Kuban Cossack Regiment was attached to the 4th Guards Kuban Cossack Corp and took part in heavy fighting against the German invading forces throughout the war. The regiment fought in Stalingrad and took part in the liberation of Southern Ukraine and Romania and became famous for their bravery. Their heroism was commemorated in 1945 when they were allowed to march in Red Square during the famous Victory Day Parade.

card_unit_isu_152.name: card_unit_isu_152
card_unit_isu_152.title: ISU-152
card_unit_isu_152.text: Deployment: Destroy all other damaged units.
card_unit_isu_152.flavorText: The ISU-152 was a self propelled gun developed and used by the Soviet Army in WWII. It was nicknamed the "beast killer" in response to German tanks bearing names such as Tiger and Panther. The ISU-152 had no turret, so repositioning the gun required turning the tank itself. Due to this it was often used as mobile artillery to support more mobile infantry and armor attacks. The  ISU-152 had a crew of 5 (driver, commander, gunner, breech operator and loader), a main armament of 152.4 mm ML-20S gun-howitzer and a secondary armament of 12.7 x 108 mm DShK anti-aircraft machine gun.

card_unit_is_i.name: card_unit_is_i
card_unit_is_i.title: IOSEF STALIN II
card_unit_is_i.text: If sent to hand, add a copy to your support line.
card_unit_is_i.flavorText: The Iosef Stalin II was a Soviet heavy tank of the IS series and used by the Red Army during and after WWII. The IS-2 tank was designed in 1943 and was first used in service in 1944 and was solely assigned to the Red Army's elite Guards Heavy Tank Regiments. They were often deployed to the frontlines and were mainly used to spearhead and support infantry assaults on fortified positions, but they could easily take out enemy tanks when required. The IS-2 had a crew of 4, a main armament of a D25-T 122 mm gun and secondary armament of 1x DShK and 3x DT machine guns.

card_unit_i_15_chaika.name: card_unit_i_15_chaika
card_unit_i_15_chaika.title: I-15 CHAIKA
card_unit_i_15_chaika.text: Destruction: Add a I-16 ISHAK fighter to the support line.
card_unit_i_15_chaika.flavorText: The I-15 Chaika, official name Polikarpov I-15, was a Soviet biplane fighter aircraft of the 1930s, but was still in use at the start of WWII and used in ground attacks by the Soviet Air Force. In late 1942 the I-15 were pulled from frontline service and used for second-line duties.

card_unit_i_16_ishak.name: card_unit_i_16_ishak
card_unit_i_16_ishak.title: I-16 ISHAK
card_unit_i_16_ishak.flavorText: The I-16 Ishak, officially named Polikarpov I-16, was a Soviet fighter aircraft that was first introduced in the mid-1930s and was the world's first low-wing cantilever monoplane fighter with retractable landing gear. It first saw combat in 1936 in the Spanish civil war, and although it was outclassed by many modern fighters at the start of WWII, the I-16 fighter was used by the Soviets until the end of the war. The pilots nicknamed it "Ishak" (meaning donkey or burro in Russian) because it was similar to the Russian pronunciation of "I-16".

card_unit_katyusha.name: card_unit_katyusha
card_unit_katyusha.title: KATYUSHA
card_unit_katyusha.text: When KATYUSHA attacks, it deals 0-1 additional damage.
card_unit_katyusha.flavorText: The Katyusha was a Soviet multiple rocket launcher that was first built and used in WWII. The Katyucha rocket launcher was cheap to produce, it could be fitted on any type of chassis, and mostly it was mounted on ordinary trucks. The rocket launcher could deliver explosives to a target more quickly than conventional artillery, but the accuracy was lower and it took a longer time to reload. Red Army troops nicknamed the rocket launcher Katyusha from Mikhail Isakovsky's popular wartime song bearing the same name. The German troops nicknamed it "Stalin's organ" since the launcher array resembled pipe organs, and due to the howling sound of the rocket motors when it launched.

card_unit_kv_1.name: card_unit_kv_1
card_unit_kv_1.title: KV-1 1939
card_unit_kv_1.flavorText: The KV-1 was a Soviet Kliment Voroshilov (KV) heavy tank variant used by the Red Army during WWII. The KV series were known for their heavy armor and were almost immune to the guns of the early Panzer III and Panzer IV tanks that were used by the Axis at the start of the war. The KV-1 had a crew of 5 and a main armament of a 76.2 mm M1941 ZiS-5 gun and a secondary armament of 3x to 4x DT machine guns. It was produced from 1939 to 1945 and 5,219 units were built.

card_unit_kv_1_1941.name: card_unit_kv_1_1941
card_unit_kv_1_1941.title: KV-1 1941
card_unit_kv_1_1941.text: Each time the enemy draws a card, deal 2 damage to the enemy HQ.
card_unit_kv_1_1941.flavorText: The Kliment Voroshilov (KV) tanks were a series of heavy tanks used and developed by the Soviets during WWII. The KV-1 1941 was, as the name suggests, produced in 1941 and unlike the previous model it had reinforced armor added to the turret, hull front and sides. The turret was cast instead of welded and it was armed with a longer-barreled ZiS-5 tank gun. 1,121 units were produced of the 1941 series.

card_unit_la_3.name: card_unit_la_3
card_unit_la_3.title: LA-5
card_unit_la_3.flavorText: The Lavochkin La-5 was a Soviet fighter aircraft used by the Red Army in WWII. Soviet pilots considered the La-5 an effective fighter, it had a a top speed and acceleration at low altitude on par with German fighters, but did not do as well at higher altitudes. The aircraft also had its defects, there was a lack of ventilation in the cockpit and exhaust gas often entered the cockpit which forced pilots to ignore orders and fly with their canopies open. 9,920 La-5 were built, but no intact aircraft exists today.

card_unit_light_anti_air_battery.name: card_unit_light_anti_air_battery
card_unit_light_anti_air_battery.title: 37 mm ANTI-AIRCRAFT GUN
card_unit_light_anti_air_battery.text: Enemy air units cost +2 to operate.
card_unit_light_anti_air_battery.flavorText: The Soviet 37 mm anti-aircraft gun was developed during the late 1930s and used during WWII. The gun had a maximum firing range of 5 km and was used on the Eastern Front against dive bombers and other low-and medium-altitude targets, but it was also effective against ground targets. It is believed that crews of the 37 mm anti-aircraft gun shot down 14,657 Axis planes.

card_unit_petlyakov_pe_2.name: card_unit_petlyakov_pe_2
card_unit_petlyakov_pe_2.title: PETLYAKOV PE-2
card_unit_petlyakov_pe_2.flavorText: The Petlyakov Pe-2 was a Soviet light bomber used in WWII. Although it was mainly used as a ground attack aircraft, it was also successful in its roles as a heavy fighter, reconnaissance and night fighter. The Pe-2 was fast, maneuverable and proved itself as a very capable frontline bomber and was used in all major Soviet fronts, both against the Axis in Europe and against Japanese forces in Manchuria. In total 11,427 Pe-2 aircraft were built in WWII.

card_unit_sturmovik.name: card_unit_sturmovik
card_unit_sturmovik.title: SHTURMOVIK Il-2M
card_unit_sturmovik.text: When this unit attacks and destroys a unit, deal excess damage to the enemy HQ.
card_unit_sturmovik.flavorText: The Shturmovik, or Ilyushin Il-2, was a Soviet ground-attack aircraft used during WWII. It was one of the most produced military aircraft in history, with a total of 36,183 units being built, and it played a crucial role on the Eastern Front. The pilots called it "Ilyusha", but soldiers referred to it as the "Hunchback", the "Flying Tank" and the "Flying Infantryman".

card_unit_su_152.name: card_unit_su_152
card_unit_su_152.title: SU 152
card_unit_su_152.text: Deployment: Your other tanks get +1 attack and +1 Heavy Armor.
card_unit_su_152.flavorText: The SU-152 (Samokhodnaya Ustanovka-152) was a Soviet self-propelled heavy howitzer used in WWII. It mounted a 152 mm gun-howitzer on the chassis of a KV-1S heavy tank and an optional 1× 12.7 mm DShK machine gun as secondary armament. The SU-152 was cheap to produce and proved to be an effective heavy tank killer although it was not initially designed for that purpose. In combat it was used either for long range artillery fire support or as a heavy tank destroyer, usually in ambush.

card_unit_su_76.name: card_unit_su_76
card_unit_su_76.title: SU-76M
card_unit_su_76.text: Deployment: Deal 2 damage to your HQ.
card_unit_su_76.flavorText: The SU-76, also known as Samokhodnaya Ustanovka 76, was a Soviet self-propelled gun used during and after WWII. A lengthened and widened version of the T-70 light tank chassis was used as a base and due to its simple construction it was the second most produced Soviet armored vehicle in WWII, after the T-34. It was liked by the crews for its reliability and ease of use, but the steering was sometimes considered difficult and due to its light armor it was sometimes referred to as "the bare-arsed Ferdinand", Ferdinand being a reference to the German Heavy Ferdinand/Elefant Tank Destroyer.

card_unit_t_34.name: card_unit_t_34
card_unit_t_34.title: T-34 1942
card_unit_t_34.flavorText: The T-34 was a legendary Soviet medium tank that had an unrivaled combination of mobility, firepower and protection when it was first introduced in WWII. Although better designs were introduced later in the war it is considered one of the most effective and influential tank designs of WWII. The T-34 has a crew of 4 (later variants had 5), a main armament of 76.2 mm F-34 tank gun (later 85 mm ZiS-S-53 gun) and a secondary armament of 2 × 7.62 mm DT machine guns.

card_unit_t_34eot.name: card_unit_t_34eot
card_unit_t_34eot.title: T-34 1942
card_unit_t_34eot.flavorText: The T-34 was a legendary Soviet medium tank that had an unrivaled combination of mobility, firepower and protection when it was first introduced in WWII. Although better designs were introduced later in the war it is considered one of the most effective and influential tank designs of WWII. The T-34 has a crew of 4 (later variants had 5), a main armament of 76.2 mm F-34 tank gun (later 85 mm ZiS-S-53 gun) and a secondary armament of 2 × 7.62 mm DT machine guns.

card_unit_t_34_85.name: card_unit_t_34_85
card_unit_t_34_85.title: T-34-85
card_unit_t_34_85.text: When the opponent targets T-34-85 with an order, draw a card.
card_unit_t_34_85.flavorText: The T-34-85 was a Soviet medium tank used in WWII by the Red Army. It was an upgraded T-34 tank, with an enlarged turret ring which allowed it to be fitted with an 85 mm gun. For secondary armament it had two DT 7.62 mm (0.3 in) machine-guns, one coaxial and one in the hull. The T-34-85 was introduced in 1943 and it was instantly liked by its crew. To begin with they were delivered to Elite and Guard units, but at the start of Operation Bagration the T-34-85's formed the bulk of Soviet tank units. By the end of the war 23,213 units had been manufactured.

card_unit_t_34_flame.name: card_unit_t_34_flame
card_unit_t_34_flame.title: OT-34
card_unit_t_34_flame.text: Deals double damage against infantry and HQ.
card_unit_t_34_flame.flavorText: The T-34 flame-thrower tank, also known as OT-34, was fitted with an internally mounted flamethrower replacing the hull machine-gun. Usually it was a modified Model 1941 with the ATO-41 flamethrower or Model 1942 with ATO-42. During WWII 1172 OT-34 tanks were produced.

card_unit_t_70.name: card_unit_t_70
card_unit_t_70.title: T-70
card_unit_t_70.flavorText: The T-70 was a Soviet light tank used by the Red Army during WWII. It was used for reconnaissance and infantry support, but it was known for taking out enemy German tanks in combat. The T-70 had a 2 man crew, a main armament of a 45 mm Model 1932/38 20-K gun and a secondary armament of 7.62 mm DT coaxial machine gun. It was produced from 1942 to 1943 and 8,226 units were built.

card_unit_yak_3.name: card_unit_yak_3
card_unit_yak_3.title: YAK 3
card_unit_yak_3.text: Deployment: Gains +1 attack and Ambush if you control a non-Soviet unit.
card_unit_yak_3.flavorText: The Yak-3, or Yakovlev, was a Soviet fighter aircraft used in WWII. It was first used in the front line in 1944 and it was used mostly as a tactical fighter, flying low over battlefields and engaging in dogfights below 4 km. Quite a few variants were designed and overall the Yak was considered to be a highly successful dog-fighter.

card_unit_yak_9.name: card_unit_yak_9
card_unit_yak_9.title: YAK 9
card_unit_yak_9.text: Destruction: Draw a random Soviet card.
card_unit_yak_9.flavorText: The Yakovlev Yak-9 was a single-engine fighter aircraft designed and used by the Soviet Union in WWII. The aircraft first saw combat in late 1942 and took on various roles later in the war. It was used as a light bomber, in long-range escort roles and as an anti-tank aircraft, but it was also highly maneuverable, very fast and performed well against the Bf 109 and Fw 190A enemy fighters. In total there were 14,579 Yak 9s manufactured during the war and it suffered lower losses on average, with only 383 lost in combat.

card_event_front_formation.name: card_event_front_formation
card_event_front_formation.title: FRONT FORMATION
card_event_front_formation.text: Your HQ gets: "At the start of your turn, take 1 damage and add a T-34 1942 to your support line. Destroy it at the end of the turn."
card_event_front_formation.flavorText: A Front was a military formation in the Soviet Army, equivalent to an army group of most other countries and generally containing three to five armies. It would be in control of all ground units and have its own army sized air formation. A Front was mobilized for a specific operation and the crucial Fronts were supplied with the greatest resources and reserves to ensure success.

card_event_hull_down.name: card_event_hull_down
card_event_hull_down.title: HULL DOWN
card_event_hull_down.text: Choose a tank in hand. When it is deployed, it gets +1+2 and fights a random enemy unit.
card_event_hull_down.flavorText: In armored warfare a hull down position means that the hull of the tank is hidden behind an obstacle, a ridge, in a prepared position or in any other way that shields the hull from sight while leaving only its turret exposed. This makes the tank a much smaller target and protects vulnerable areas. In flat or gently rolling terrain a hull down position is hard to find, however a hull down position can be created by digging shallow “tank scrapes”. This gives the tank a much stronger defensive position.

card_event_iron_victory.name: card_event_iron_victory
card_event_iron_victory.title: IRON VICTORY
card_event_iron_victory.text: Discard your hand. For each card discarded, add a T-34 1942 with 1 operation cost to hand.
card_event_iron_victory.flavorText: The Soviet Union produced approximately 105,000 tanks from 1941 to 1945, including self-propelled artillery, assault guns and tank destroyers. For comparison, Germany manufactured a total of 49,777 tanks from 1939 to 1945. Estimates suggest that the Soviet Union had around 30,000 to 35,000 tanks in service or reserve by the end of the war, while Germany had about 5,000 to 7,000 tanks remaining, largely due to heavy losses on multiple fronts and their inability to match Soviet production rates. The Soviet Union’s industrial mobilization and mass production capabilities allowed it to outproduce Germany in tanks and armored vehicles, which was crucial to sustaining large-scale offensives from Stalingrad to Berlin. This difference in tank numbers gave the Soviet Red Army a decisive advantage in the final stages of the war in Europe.

card_event_shock_tactics.name: card_event_shock_tactics
card_event_shock_tactics.title: SHOCK TACTICS
card_event_shock_tactics.text: Choose One - Give a ground unit Blitz OR Shock. Apply both if you control a unit with 4 or more attack.
card_event_shock_tactics.flavorText: Shock tactics are an offensive maneuver that attempts to place the enemy under psychological pressure by rapid and overwhelming attack incapacitating the defenders or causing them to retreat. The Red Army took this concept to the next level in WWII, creating Shock armies with a specific structure to break through the enemy lines.

card_event_turning_point.name: card_event_turning_point
card_event_turning_point.title: TURNING POINT
card_event_turning_point.text: Your T-34s operate for free this turn and their excess attack damage is dealt to the enemy HQ.
card_event_turning_point.flavorText: A turning point is a crucial engagement where an important change occurs. The tide of the war in Europe shifted with the Soviet victory of Stalingrad. More than one million Soviet troops and tens of thousands of civilians died in the battle, but it ended with the Soviet Operation Uranus which led to the encirclement and  the destruction of the German 6th Army. This marked the beginning of the end for the third Reich.

card_event_vystrel_course.name: card_event_vystrel_course
card_event_vystrel_course.title: VYSTREL COURSE
card_event_vystrel_course.text: Target a friendly tank or infantry. At the start of your next turn give it +3+3.
card_event_vystrel_course.flavorText: The Higher Rifle Tactical Course for the Improvement of Infantry Commanders "Vystrel", commonly called Vystrel Course, was an officer training course of the Soviet Armed Forces. The school's task was officer training for the infantry, but also research and development of weaponry and the production of educational literature. The course, provided twice a year for five and a half month periods, trained battalion and regiment level command and political personnel for the rifle arm (infantry) of the Red Army. A reasonable combination of theory and practice in training yielded high results, and good feedback was received from the troops about the graduates of the course. Officers who attended the Vystrel course formed the core of officers and more than 200 graduates were awarded the title Hero of the Soviet Union.

card_unit_12th_guards_mechanised.name: card_unit_12th_guards_mechanised
card_unit_12th_guards_mechanised.title: 12th GUARDS MECHANISED
card_unit_12th_guards_mechanised.text: Becomes Veteran when you deploy a tank with 4 or more attack.
card_unit_12th_guards_mechanised.flavorText: The 12th Guards Mechanised Brigade fought closely along the tanks of the Red Army. It belongs to the 5th Guards Mechanized Corps. During the battle of Kursk in 1943, the Corps was part of the 5th Guards Tank Army and it fought in the southern part of the salient. It participated in the Battle of Prokhorovka, remained with the main striking force of the army and liberated Belgorod. It took part in the Battle of the Korsun-Cherkassy Pocket and finally the Battle of Berlin in 1945. It ended up with several honors including the Order of the Red Banner for exemplary performance during the capture of the capital of Germany, and for the valor and courage displayed in doing so.

card_unit_190th_guard_rifles.name: card_unit_190th_guard_rifles
card_unit_190th_guard_rifles.title: 190th GUARD RIFLES
card_unit_190th_guard_rifles.text: Cannot attack or move. Becomes Veteran when you have destroyed 4 enemy units.
card_unit_190th_guard_rifles.flavorText: The 190th Guards Rifle Regiment was a unit of the 5th Rifle Division of the Soviet Red Army. The division was formed in 1918 and fought in the Russian Revolution and the Polish-Soviet War (1919-1921). After the launch of Operation Barbarossa in 1941, the division fought in the Baltic Operation and the Leningrad Strategic Defensive. In the winter of 1941-1942, it took part in the Battle of Moscow, fighting near Kalinin (now Tver). In the summer of 1942, the division participated in the Rzhev-Vyazma Offensive and was raised to Guards status for its performance. In February 1943, it fought in offensives around Mtsensk and Kalinin and in July it participated in Operation Kutuzov where it captured the city of Orel, earning the "Orel" honorific. It then fought in the Bryansk and Gomel-Rechitsa Offensives, reaching the Dnieper. In early 1944, it took part in the Rogachev-Zhlobin Offensive, receiving the Order of the Red Banner. During Operation Bagration, it was awarded the Order of Suvorov and later the Order of Kutuzov for capturing Vawkavysk. In 1945, it fought in the Berlin Offensive and was awarded the Order of Lenin before disbanding in June 1946.

card_unit_204th_guards.name: card_unit_204th_guards
card_unit_204th_guards.title: 204th GUARDS
card_unit_204th_guards.text: After this unit destroys a unit in combat give it Shock.
card_unit_204th_guards.flavorText: The 204th Guards Rifle Regiment was an infantry unit of the 69th Guards Rifle Division, which was active between 1943 and 1953. The division first served in Stalingrad where it cleared out the remaining resistance after the Axis surrender. The division entered combat during the Soviet  Belgorod-Kharkov Offensive in August 1943, and continued its advance towards the Dnieper River and Kyiv in the autumn. In early 1944, it participated in the encirclement at Korsun-Shevchenkivskiy, after which it was rewarded with a battle honor. The division then advanced to the Dniester River and took part in the capture of the Romanian city of Iași in August, which earned it the Order of the Red Banner. After Romania left the Axis, the division fought in several battles and operations in Hungary and Austria, including the Budapest Offensive and the Vienna Offensive. In 1953 the 69th Guards Rifle Division was reorganized as the 70th Guards Mechanized Division.

card_unit_269th_rifles.name: card_unit_269th_rifles
card_unit_269th_rifles.title: 269th RIFLES
card_unit_269th_rifles.text: Becomes Veteran when you deploy a tank with 4 or more attack.
card_unit_269th_rifles.flavorText: The 269th Rifle Regiment was part of the 10th NKVD Rifle Division, formed on 1 February 1942, during WWII. It primarily included Border Troops from the Ural and Siberian regions, along with the 269th and 270th Regiments largely composed of Stalingrad citizens. Initially tasked with capturing enemy parachutists and saboteurs, the division became one of the first to defend Stalingrad in July 1942. In two days, the 269th Regiment inflicted over a thousand casualties and disabled 20 tanks. Throughout the battle, the division suffered heavy losses but inflicted 15,000 German casualties, destroyed 113 tanks, 8 armored vehicles, 2 aircraft, and captured a German regiment’s banner. For exemplary service in defending Stalingrad, the Soviet High Command awarded the 10th NKVD Division the Order of Lenin on 2 December 1942. However, due to heavy losses, the division was demobilized in early October 1942, with only 200 of the original 7,568 men remaining.

card_unit_4th_guards_rifles.name: card_unit_4th_guards_rifles
card_unit_4th_guards_rifles.title: 4th GUARDS RIFLES
card_unit_4th_guards_rifles.text: If in your hand, reduce cost by 1 each time the enemy draws a card.
card_unit_4th_guards_rifles.flavorText: The 4th Guards Rifle Regiment was an infantry regiment of the 6th Guards Rifle Division, known as "Rovenskaya". It was awarded the Orders of Lenin, the Red Banner, and Suvorov, and it was one of the most notable units that fought in the Oryol region during WWII. It was formed in Livny as the 120th Rifle Division and fought continuously in this area from October 1941 to the summer of 1943. The division took part in major battles, including Moscow, Kursk, and Kyiv, and played a role in the liberation of cities like Yelnya and Rovno. Three of its commanders became Heroes of the Soviet Union: Filipp Cherokmanov, Dmitry Onuprienko, and Georgy Ivanov.

card_unit_57th_rifles.name: card_unit_57th_rifles
card_unit_57th_rifles.title: 57th RIFLES
card_unit_57th_rifles.text: When you deploy or add a T-34 tank, it fights a random enemy unit.
card_unit_57th_rifles.flavorText: The 57th Motor Rifle Brigade was part of the 16th Guards Tank Division during WWII. The division was an elite armored unit of the Red Army,  notorious for its role in some of the most critical battles on the Eastern Front. It was originally formed as the 16th Tank Corps, but was promoted to Guards status in 1943 for its bravery and effectiveness in combat, particularly in the Battle of Stalingrad, where it played a significant role in surrounding and defeating the German forces. The division continued to prove itself valuable in following operations, including the Battle of Kursk in 1943, where it contributed to the Soviet victory in the largest tank battles in history. Later, the 16th Guards Tank Division participated in major Soviet offensives, such as Operation Bagration in 1944, helping push German forces back through Belarus and eventually to Eastern Europe. By the end of the war, the division had advanced into Germany where it participated in the Battle of Berlin, which led to the final defeat of Nazi Germany. After the war the division was stationed in Eastern Germany until 1991 when the Soviet Union was dissolved, resulting in the withdrawal of remaining units from Germany.

card_unit_654_rifles.name: card_unit_654_rifles
card_unit_654_rifles.title: 654th RIFLES
card_unit_654_rifles.text: Deployment: Add a T-70 to your support line. Give it Shock.
card_unit_654_rifles.flavorText: The 654th Infantry Rifle Regiment was part of the 148th Rifle Division. It took part in some of the largest offensives from 1943 until the end of the war. The division fought heavily around Voronezh and then in the northern part of the Kursk salient. It was involved in heavy fighting and a battle of attrition around the train station at Ponyri. Following this, it crossed the Dnieper river and went on to participate in the 1944 summer offensive, during which it liberated Lviv. In the final stages of the war it took part in the Berlin strategic offensive operation and in the liberation of Prague.

card_unit_t_34_76d.name: card_unit_t_34_76d
card_unit_t_34_76d.title: T-34/76D
card_unit_t_34_76d.text: Destruction: Draw a T-34 from your deck and reduce its cost by 2.
card_unit_t_34_76d.flavorText: The T-34 was a legendary Soviet tank which entered production in 1940 after the Red Army realized the deficiencies of their existing T-26 and BT tanks during the battles of Khalkhin Gol and the Winter War. It was designed to fulfill the need for a more heavily armed and armored universal tank. Throughout the war the T-34 was constantly upgraded and the T-34/76D was introduced in 1943. Its main feature was the new hexagonal turret, nicknamed “Mickey Mouse” because of its appearance with the twin, round turret hatches open. This variant of T-34 tanks would be the main Soviet battle tank of the important battle of Kursk and the following Soviet offensive.

card_unit_t_34_85_1945.name: card_unit_t_34_85_1945
card_unit_t_34_85_1945.title: T-34-85 1945
card_unit_t_34_85_1945.text: Cannot be Suppressed or lose Shock.
card_unit_t_34_85_1945.flavorText: The T-34-85 1945 was an upgraded version of the Soviet T-34-85 1944 and became the most produced variant of the T-34-85. The 1945 variant featured several key upgrades to enhance its combat effectiveness. It was equipped with an electrically powered turret traverse motor, allowing for faster and more precise turret rotation compared to manual systems, as well as a larger cupola with a one-piece hatch. Additionally, the T-34-85 1945 included the TDP smoke system, which used electrically detonated MDSh canisters to deploy smoke for battlefield concealment, helping the tank maneuver under cover and avoid enemy fire. These improvements made the T-34-85 more efficient and survivable in combat.

card_event_at_all_cost.name: card_event_at_all_cost
card_event_at_all_cost.title: AT ALL COST
card_event_at_all_cost.text: Destroy a friendly unit. Deal 2 damage to all.
card_event_at_all_cost.flavorText: At the start of Operation Barbarossa the Soviet Union faced the largest invasion in history. In the first five months of the invasion the Red Army suffered one catastrophic defeat after another and were driven back in disarray. Finally, at the gates of Moscow, the Red Army managed to turn the tables and what followed was the bloodiest conflict in history which ended with the unconditional surrender of Nazi Germany. During the conflict Soviet Union alone suffered 26,6 millions dead, 14,6 million civilians and 12 millions soldiers, which was 14% of the Soviet pre-war population. The  economic damages were also huge, between 1940-1945 the Soviet GDP fell by 20% and what followed was years of drought, famine and typhus epidemics. It is a fact that the sacrifices of the people of Soviet Union were by far the greatest of the Allied nations.

card_event_by_the_sword.name: card_event_by_the_sword
card_event_by_the_sword.title: BY THE SWORD
card_event_by_the_sword.text: Draw cards equal to the number of enemy units on the battlefield.
card_event_by_the_sword.flavorText: "Whoever comes to us with a sword will die by the sword!" is a quote attributed to Alexander Nevsky (1221- 1263), the Novgorod prince, who allegedly uttered this phrase when his enemies begged for peace after being defeated in battle. There is no evidence that this phrase was ever uttered by the prince, but since the 18th century Alexander Nevsky has been the symbol of the defender of Russia and Eisenstein's film about him that premiered in 1941, when the Great Patriotic War had begun, gave new life to this image. The film had such a strong influence on public consciousness that the Order of Alexander Nevsky was established in 1942 and the Novgorod prince became a central theme of Russia’s heroic past in war Soviet propaganda.

card_event_confusion.name: card_event_confusion
card_event_confusion.title: CONFUSION
card_event_confusion.text: Take control of an enemy unit with cost 3 or less until end of turn.
card_event_confusion.flavorText: “The whole secret lies in confusing the enemy, so that he cannot fathom our real intent.” -Sun Tzu, The Art of War

card_event_lesser_of_two_evils.name: card_event_lesser_of_two_evils
card_event_lesser_of_two_evils.title: LESSER OF TWO EVILS
card_event_lesser_of_two_evils.text: Draw two cards, then choose and discard a card.
card_event_lesser_of_two_evils.flavorText: The non-aggression treaty between Germany and Soviet Union, known as the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, was made on 23 August 1939, but following Operation Barbarossa, the German invasion of Soviet Union, the treaty was declared null and void. The Soviet Union then entered an alliance with the UK and USA in the fight against the Axis powers. This military alliance is called the Grand Alliance, or the Big Three, but some call it the “Strange Alliance” due to the fact that it united the Communist State of Soviet Union with the capitalist state of USA and the colonial power of the UK. Although there were tensions, especially between Soviet Union and the Anglo-American powers, the alliance held throughout the war. After WWII there was much geopolitical tension between the Eastern and Western bloc, and in 1946 the Grand Alliance was terminated and what followed was the Cold War.

card_event_minority_recruits.name: card_event_minority_recruits
card_event_minority_recruits.title: MINORITY RECRUITS
card_event_minority_recruits.text: Take control of an enemy unit.
card_event_minority_recruits.flavorText: Switching sides during WWII was not uncommon, even for nations. At the start of WWII Romania, Bulgaria, Finland and Italy were allied with the Axis powers, but the war’s developments in later years would influence these countries decisions to switch their allegiance to the Allies.

card_event_reckless_assault.name: card_event_reckless_assault
card_event_reckless_assault.title: RECKLESS ASSAULT
card_event_reckless_assault.text: Your units get +2+2 and: "When this unit deals damage, deal equal damage to your HQ."
card_event_reckless_assault.flavorText: What has often been associated with the Red Army during WWII are human wave attacks, and although it is true that they were used to some extent, and often with disastrous results, it was not standard tactics of the Red Army. It is clear that the Red Army’s victory over the German forces came at a heavy cost of human life, but this was not due to disregard for human life. Also, the numerical superiority of the Red Army became significant over time and at great cost, but it was not as overwhelming as often depicted in Hollywood or German myth.

card_event_spy_ring.name: card_event_spy_ring
card_event_spy_ring.title: SPY RING
card_event_spy_ring.text: Add a random Research card to your hand.
card_event_spy_ring.flavorText: The Soviet Union had an elaborate ring of secret agents working for them during WWII. One of them was Richard Sorge who worked undercover as a German journalist in both Germany and Japan and provided vital wartime intelligence before he was caught and hanged by the Japanese in 1944. Many of the spies were double agents that had infiltrated, not only the Axis ranks, but also the ranks of the Allies, f.ex. Harold “Kim” Philby, one of the Cambridge Five, who was a senior officer in Britain’s Secret Intelligence Service. Another one was Klaus Fuchs who was the primary physicist on the Manhattan Project and passed on secrets about the A-bomb to Moscow. Many of the Soviet moles continued their work long into the Cold War, most were driven by ideology, but others by money or adventure.

card_event_winter_offensive.name: card_event_winter_offensive
card_event_winter_offensive.title: WINTER OFFENSIVE
card_event_winter_offensive.flavorText: The Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42, also known as the  Moscow Strategic Offensive Operation, was a turning point in WWII. The Battle of Moscow  was the first significant defeat of the Germans in WWII, and although it was a costly victory for the Red Army, it debunked the myth of the invincibility of the Germany army and restored faith in Allied victory on the Eastern Front.

card_unit_117th_zhytomyr.name: card_unit_117th_zhytomyr
card_unit_117th_zhytomyr.title: 71st ZHYTOMYR
card_unit_117th_zhytomyr.text: Your units with Ambush deal double combat damage.
card_unit_117th_zhytomyr.flavorText: The 71st Zhymotyr was originally an infantry regiment of the 23rd Rifle Division of the Red Army. The division fought in several battles and campaigns, including the Battle of Stalingrad, Operation Bagration, The East Pomeranian Offensive and the Berlin Offensive. For its actions at the Battle of Stalingrad the division was raised to Guards status and became the 71st Guards Rifle Division. The division received several awards, including the Order of Lenin, Order of the Red Banner and the honorific “Zhytomyr”.

card_unit_128th_rifles.name: card_unit_128th_rifles
