It also featured a more spacious three-man turret, improving the crew's working conditions and the tank's overall efficiency. This model was an essential part of the Soviet armored forces in the later stages of the war and was known for its reliability, ease of production, and combat effectiveness. The T-34-85 model of 1943 set the standard appearance for the series until 1945. However, the 1944 version came with a simpler ZiS-S-53 85mm gun, radio moved from the hull into a turret with improved layout and new gunner's sights.

card_unit_t_35_winter.name: card_unit_t_35_winter
card_unit_t_35_winter.title: T-35
card_unit_t_35_winter.text: Deals 1 damage to each HQ at the end of your turn.
card_unit_t_35_winter.flavorText: The T-35 was a Soviet multi-turreted heavy tank developed during the interwar period. It was one of the largest and heaviest tanks ever produced, and often called a land battleship. However, by the time WWII began, the T-35 was considered technologically outdated. During the initial stages of the war, the T-35 tanks were still in service with the Red Army and they were used in the early phases of Operation Barbarossa in 1941. But, the tank had several significant issues that hindered its effectiveness and its complicated design made it challenging to maintain and repair. The tank was slow, suffered from mechanical problems and had limited maneuverability. As a result, most T-35 tanks were quickly lost in the early stages of the conflict, either destroyed, disabled, or abandoned due to mechanical issues. Because of its limitations and the impracticality of its design, the T-35 was gradually phased out of service during the early years of the war. A total of 56 T-35 tanks were built and only one survived and is preserved in running condition at the Patriot Park near Moscow.

card_event_hasty_reinforcements.name: card_event_hasty_reinforcements
card_event_hasty_reinforcements.title: HASTY REINFORCEMENTS
card_event_hasty_reinforcements.text: Units you deploy or add this turn randomly get +1+1, Blitz or Ambush.
card_event_hasty_reinforcements.flavorText: During WWII the Red Army grew extensively and by the war's end around 30 million Soviet men and women had been drafted to military service. Prior to the war the Soviet Union did not have a comprehensive military draft so many of the people that were drafted during WWII had no military experience. In general most recruits spent 3 months in training and were properly prepared when they reached the frontlines. However, in Oct-Nov 1941 the training of many units was cut short due to the lack of manpower. Most fresh recruits were distributed among more seasoned troops in the frontlines where they finished their training. In these cases the training was mostly about surviving the first 3 attacks, which is the most critical period for fresh recruits.

card_event_machines_of_war.name: card_event_machines_of_war
card_event_machines_of_war.title: MACHINES OF WAR
card_event_machines_of_war.text: Add the top Soviet infantry unit in your deck to your support line.
card_event_machines_of_war.flavorText: During the opening stages of the German invasion of the Soviet Union the Red Army faced a serious shortage of weapons. The course of the war went on in such a way that most of the available munitions were lost, along with its troops who were either killed or captured, destroyed during a retreat or captured by the enemy in warehouses. The development and manufacturing of munitions in the Soviet Union had begun before the invasion, but in 1941 they stepped up their game and most of their weapon production was done during the invasion, in some cases under siege and isolation. From 1941 to 1945, the Soviet Union managed to produce over 30 million rifles and submachine guns, 1,476 million machine guns, 516,648 artillery guns, 347,900 mortars, 119,769 tanks and self-propelled guns, 265,600 army trucks, 213,742 military aircraft, 2 cruisers, 25 destroyers and 52 submarines.

card_event_monastyr.name: card_event_monastyr
card_event_monastyr.title: MONASTYR
card_event_monastyr.text: Destroy all units with 1 or fewer combat keywords.
card_event_monastyr.flavorText: Operation Monastyr (e. Operation Monastery) was a Soviet intelligence operation that lasted from 1941 to 1944 and involved using a “radio game” which was standard technique in radio counterintelligence at the time. The operation was conducted by NKVD agents and the goal was to use Soviet moles to relay misinformation to the Abwehr, the German military intelligence. The operation was considered a great success, it resulted in the capture of several German agents and collaborators. However, one of its major contributions was disinformation about major Soviet offensive operations near the town of Rzhev, which the Germans took at face value. This was partly true, but this rendered the Germans blind to the much more important Operation Uranus, the major Soviet offensive at Stalingrad.

card_event_out_with_the_old.name: card_event_out_with_the_old
card_event_out_with_the_old.title: OUT WITH THE OLD
card_event_out_with_the_old.text: Trigger the destruction effects on a damaged Soviet air unit, then Convert it into YAK 9.
card_event_out_with_the_old.flavorText: At the start of WWII, the Soviet Air Forces fielded outdated aircraft like the I-15 biplane and I-16 monoplane, many of which were outclassed by German fighters. However, the war triggered a rapid transformation in Soviet aircraft design and production. Engineers streamlined manufacturing, adopted mixed-construction techniques, and focused on rugged, combat-effective designs that could be built quickly and in massive numbers. The Yakovlev Yak-9 exemplified this shift. Introduced in 1942, it used lightweight materials and modular construction, allowing rapid adaptation to various combat roles. The Yak-9T carried a 37 mm cannon for tank busting, while other variants served as long-range escorts or dogfighters. Its agility and ease of maintenance made it a favorite among Soviet pilots. Alongside the Yak-9, newer Lavochkin and Ilyushin models replaced older types across the front. Factories evacuated east of the Urals kept up relentless output, delivering modern aircraft even under extreme wartime conditions. By 1945, the Soviet Union’s air force had transformed into a formidable, modern force capable of meeting the Luftwaffe head-on.

card_event_surazh_gate.name: card_event_surazh_gate
card_event_surazh_gate.title: SURAZH GATE
card_event_surazh_gate.text: Pin target unit. Deal 2 damage to adjacent units.
card_event_surazh_gate.flavorText: The Surazh Gate, also known as the Vitebsk Gate, was the name given to the corridor connecting the Soviet Union and the German occupied territories of Belarus in 1942. This was an area of 40 km, between the Russian towns of Usvyaty and Velizh, which at the time was the point of contact between the German Army Group North and Army Group Center. The gate was created by the Soviet 4th Shock Army during the Toropets–Kholm Offensive in the winter of 1941-42 and it created a large gap in the German defensive lines. The Soviet units were aided by partisan groups who destroyed German garrisons and guarded the area. The Surazh Gate did not only serve as a gate into the occupied territories, but it also allowed transports out of them of both men and supplies. However, the Red Army did not launch another offensive in this area and in September 1942 the Germans launched a counteroffensive and managed to close the gate.

card_unit_39th_rifle_regiment.name: card_unit_39th_rifle_regiment
card_unit_39th_rifle_regiment.title: 39th RIFLE REGIMENT
card_unit_39th_rifle_regiment.text: Deployment: Take control of an enemy unit with cost 2 or less.
card_unit_39th_rifle_regiment.flavorText: The 39th Rifle Regiment was a regiment of the 4th Rifle Division of the Soviet Red Army. The division was first formed in 1919 during the Russian Civil War and fought on the western front in that war, and later in the Polish Soviet War of 1919 -1921. In 1939 the division participated in the Finnish Winter War as part of the 13th Army and suffered heavy losses in the Battle of Kelja. In 1941, after Operation Barbarossa, the division was fighting the invading German forces as part of 12th Army, but it was disbanded in 1942 after heavy losses in the Battle of the Caucasus. The 4th Division was reformed in 1943 and participated in the Lublin-Brest Offensive in 1944 and the Battle of Berlin in May 1945. Shortly after the war ended in Europe the division was disbanded.

card_unit_52_k.name: card_unit_52_k
card_unit_52_k.title: 52-K
card_unit_52_k.text: Deployment: Deal 4 damage to target enemy air unit.
card_unit_52_k.flavorText: The Soviet 85 mm M1939, aka 52-K, anti aircraft gun was used by the Red Army during WWII. The gun entered service in 1939 in regiments of 16 guns each and was used effectively against  German aircraft between 1941 and 1945. In its secondary role the 52-K was used as an anti tank weapon and some gun barrels were mounted on vehicles such as the SU-85 tank destroyer. After the war most Soviet nations had the 52-K in its arsenal and in some cases they were refitted for peaceful purposes as anti-avalanche guns.

card_unit_60th_cavalry_regiment.name: card_unit_60th_cavalry_regiment
card_unit_60th_cavalry_regiment.title: 60th CAVALRY REGIMENT
card_unit_60th_cavalry_regiment.text: Players can only give one order each turn.
card_unit_60th_cavalry_regiment.flavorText: The 60th Cavalry Regiment was a military unit of the 3rd Cavalry Division of the Red Army of the Soviet Union. The division was first formed in 1923 and participated in the invasion of Poland in 1939, but at the start of Operation Barbarossa in 1941 it defended against the Axis invaders as part of the 5th Cavalry Corps of the 6th Army of the Southwestern Front. That same year the division was redesignated to 5th Guards Cavalry Division for its skillful combat performance against the Axis forces. From 1944 to 1945 the division served under the 1st and 2nd Baltic Front, but was moved to 3rd Belorussian Front where it served until the end of the war.

card_unit_bryansk_irregulars.name: card_unit_bryansk_irregulars
card_unit_bryansk_irregulars.title: BRYANSK IRREGULARS
card_unit_bryansk_irregulars.text: Destruction: Deal 3 damage to each unit that dealt damage to this unit this turn.
card_unit_bryansk_irregulars.flavorText: It is believed that there were around 60,000 Soviet partisans operating in and around Bryansk during WWII and by 1942 they effectively held an area of 14,000 km². The partisans often fought alongside other Red Army forces in battles, but their main goal was to operate behind the enemy lines, to interrupt supply lines and communications or to gather intelligence. The Bryansk region is known for its dense woodland which formed an excellent natural defense, it gave the partisans protection during their raids as well as making it easy for them to hide their movements and their bases. The partisan units in Bryansk were mostly supplied by air and had at least three operative air strips under their control, and several partisan brigades operated their own aircraft.

card_unit_ilyushin_10.name: card_unit_ilyushin_10
card_unit_ilyushin_10.title: ILYUSHIN IL-10
card_unit_ilyushin_10.text: Destruction: Add your last destroyed ground unit to your support line.
card_unit_ilyushin_10.flavorText: The Ilyushin Il-10 was the Soviet Union’s last ground-attack aircraft introduced during WWII. Designed to replace the Il-2, it featured stronger armor, better speed and improved handling at low altitudes. These qualities were vital for surviving concentrated ground fire during close support missions. Powered by the AM-42 engine, the Il-10 carried two 23 mm cannons, two machine guns, and a rear 12.7 mm gunner. It could also deliver up to 600 kilograms of bombs. Unlike the heavier Il-8, which was tested at the same time, the Il-10 proved more agile and reliable. It entered production in September 1944 and began arriving at frontline units in early 1945. Three assault regiments flew Il-10s in combat during the final weeks of the war in Europe. They attacked German defensive positions and supply routes. Crews praised its improved protection and firepower. Some aircraft were lost to Flak and engine failures, but performance was a clear step forward. The Il-10 also took part in the Soviet offensive against Japan in August 1945. Though its time in WWII was short, it marked the Air Forces’ shift to more modern and versatile strike aircraft.

card_unit_p_39_airacobra.name: card_unit_p_39_airacobra
card_unit_p_39_airacobra.title: LITTLE COBRA
card_unit_p_39_airacobra.text: Deployment: Destroy another random friendly unit.
card_unit_p_39_airacobra.flavorText: The Bell P-39 Airacobra was one of the most unusual American fighters of WWII, featuring a mid-mounted engine and tricycle landing gear. While the US and British air forces found it underwhelming at high altitudes, the Soviet Union turned it into a formidable low-altitude weapon. Delivered through the Lend-Lease program, over 4,700 P-39s were sent to the USSR, making it one of the most-used American aircraft on the Eastern Front. Soviet pilots valued the P-39’s durability, firepower, and performance at low to medium altitudes, where most of their air combat took place. Its 37 mm cannon, firing through the propeller hub, proved deadly against both aircraft and lightly armored ground targets. Ace pilots like Aleksandr Pokryshkin and Grigori Rechkalov achieved dozens of aerial victories flying Airacobras. Unlike their Western allies, the Soviets flew the P-39 aggressively in frontline roles well into 1945. Though often dismissed in the West, the P-39 became a workhorse in Soviet hands and contributed significantly to the air war on the Eastern Front.

card_event_air_blitz_tut.name: card_event_air_blitz_tut
card_event_air_blitz_tut.title: AIR BLITZ
card_event_air_blitz_tut.text: Deal 2 damage to the enemy HQ.

card_event_gunship_assault_tut.name: card_event_gunship_assault_tut
card_event_gunship_assault_tut.title: GUNSHIP ASSAULT
card_event_gunship_assault_tut.text: Deal 2 damage to a target in the enemy support line.

card_event_carrier_cover.name: card_event_carrier_cover
card_event_carrier_cover.title: CARRIER COVER
card_event_carrier_cover.text: Choose one - Your fighters get +1+1 OR are moved into the frontline, if possible.
card_event_carrier_cover.flavorText: Throughout WWII the Americans built 152 aircraft carriers, 30 fleet carriers and 122 escort carriers which were both slower and smaller than fleet carriers, but much cheaper to build. Allied aircraft carriers provided air support in both land and sea operations, and in the Atlantic they were primarily used in anti-submarine warfare, both as convoy escorts and later in independent hunting groups.

card_event_counter_strike.name: card_event_counter_strike
card_event_counter_strike.title: COUNTER STRIKE
card_event_counter_strike.text: When a unit attacks your HQ, destroy the unit.
card_event_counter_strike.flavorText: A counter strike, or counterattack is a tactic employed in response to an attack with the objective of regaining lost ground or to destroy an attacking enemy. This is a tactic that was frequently employed in WWII, for example, during the Battle of the Bulge, American troops successfully resisted German attacks in the Battle for St. Vith. After some resistance the Americans finally evacuated the town, but did so by falling back to entrenched positions and continued their resistance. This slowed down the German advance even more and dealt a major setback to their timetable.

card_event_embargo.name: card_event_embargo
card_event_embargo.title: EMBARGO
card_event_embargo.text: The enemy gets 2 fewer kredits next turn.
card_event_embargo.flavorText: When Japan invaded French Indochina in 1940, the United States decided to embargo all oil exports to Japan. Later, due to increased Japanese hostilities in the Pacific, the war against China, and the Japanese alliance with Germany and Italy, the United States also froze Japanese assets in America. They also embargoed scrap-metal shipments to Japan and closed the Panama Canal to Japanese shipping. These actions hit the Japanese economy hard since 80% of their oil imports and 74% of scrap-metal imports came from the United States. In answer to this the Japanese decided to attack Pearl Harbor. Japan’s leaders at the time were confident that an attack on Pearl Harbor would force the United States to negotiate a compromise and lift the heavy sanctions, rather than fight the long and bloody war that later came.

card_event_magic.name: card_event_magic
card_event_magic.title: MAGIC
card_event_magic.text: Choose one - a unit is fully repaired OR it loses Guard, Ambush and Smokescreen.
card_event_magic.flavorText: Magic was an Allied cryptanalysis project during WWII. It involved a combined force of cryptographers, both from the US Navy and Army, and later civilian experts and technicians, all under the same roof and working on a series of codes and cyphers that were intercepted from the Axis powers. Their most important breakthroughs involved RED, BLUE and PURPLE, which were secret operating codes used by the Japanese in WWII.

card_event_naval_task_force.name: card_event_naval_task_force
card_event_naval_task_force.title: NAVAL TASK FORCE
card_event_naval_task_force.text: Choose one - add a NAVAL BOMBARDMENT to hand OR add a SUPPLY SHIPMENT to hand.
card_event_naval_task_force.flavorText: A Naval Task Force is a unit or formation that is assembled to work on a single task or mission. During WWII the US Navy alone created around 100 naval task forces. A Fast Carrier Task Force was a group formation used as the main striking force of the US Navy during the Pacific War from 1944 to 1945. An ideal composition for this kind of task force consisted of 3-4 aircraft carriers, 4-6  support vessels, cruisers or fast battleships and 18-24 destroyers. Fast Carrier Task Forces were used in all US Navy’s battles in the Pacific and usually 1-2 task groups were utilized in raids against island strong points in the Pacific such as Iwo Jima or Chichi Jima.

card_event_shore_bombardment.name: card_event_shore_bombardment
card_event_shore_bombardment.title: SHORE BOMBARDMENT
card_event_shore_bombardment.text: Choose one - deal 3 damage to a unit OR give a unit +2+3.
card_event_shore_bombardment.flavorText: Shore bombardment, also known as naval gunfire support, is the use of naval artillery fire support for amphibious assaults and to support other troops operating ashore. This tactic had evolved greatly during WWII as modern technology such as the hand carried radio systems allowed observers ashore to forward targeting information to the firing vessels and to adjust the accuracy in an instant. Shore bombardment was widely used during WWII in both the European and Pacific theaters, both by the Allies and the Axis forces.

card_event_strafing.name: card_event_strafing
card_event_strafing.title: STRAFING
card_event_strafing.text: Choose one - destroy target artillery unit OR pin all units in the frontline.
card_event_strafing.flavorText: Strafing is a military tactic which involves attacking ground targets from low-flying aircraft using aircraft-mounted automatic weapons. Strafing was frequently practiced in WWI, but developments of the tactics continued through WWII with dedicated aircraft on both sides. For the US, the Republic P-47 Thunderbolt (armed with 8 .50 calibre machine guns) and the North American B-25 Mitchell were the two best strafing aircraft.

card_event_strategic_planning.name: card_event_strategic_planning
card_event_strategic_planning.title: STRATEGIC PLANNING
card_event_strategic_planning.text: Double the attack and defense of your units.
card_event_strategic_planning.flavorText: D-Day, the Allied invasion of Normandy in June 1944, was one of the most complicated and difficult military operation in history. It involved approximately 3 million military personnel, 7,000 ships and 11,000 aircraft. This was a combined effort of 12 countries, involving primarily American, British and Canadian troops, and the success of the operation lay not least in the meticulous planning and forethought of the parties involved.

card_event_supply_front.name: card_event_supply_front
card_event_supply_front.title: SUPPLY FRONT
card_event_supply_front.text: Fully repair all units in the frontline and give them +1+2.
card_event_supply_front.flavorText: Delivering supplies to frontline troops in war is always a logistical challenge. After the successful landings in Normandy, the Allied forces moved quickly through Europe, and to expedite cargo shipments to the front a convoy system was put into operation. The convoy system was called Red Ball Express and it was primarily staffed with African-American soldiers who operated 5,958 vehicles and carried 12,500 tonnes of supplies a day. The convoy express operated non-stop for 83 days, or until port facilities at Antwerp, Belgium were opened, French rail lines were repaired, and portable gasoline pipelines were deployed.

card_unit_106th_quartermasters.name: card_unit_106th_quartermasters
card_unit_106th_quartermasters.title: 106th QUARTERMASTERS
card_unit_106th_quartermasters.text: When you gain an extra kredit slot, draw a card.
card_unit_106th_quartermasters.flavorText: During WWII the 106th Quartermaster Company were part of the 106th Infantry Division of the US Army. During the war the division participated in the Siegfried (Allied advance from Paris to the Rhine), the Battle of the Bulge, and lastly it took part in the Allied invasion of Germany. The 106th Quartermaster Company was responsible for supervising stores, barracks and distributing supplies and provisions for the division. The author Kurt Vonnegut served in the 106th Infantry Division and wrote about his experience in the Battle of the Bulge and later as a POW in Germany in his book “Slaughterhouse-Five”.

card_unit_109th_combat_engineers.name: card_unit_109th_combat_engineers
card_unit_109th_combat_engineers.title: 109th COMBAT ENGINEERS
card_unit_109th_combat_engineers.text: When another friendly unit moves into the frontline, give it +1 attack.
card_unit_109th_combat_engineers.flavorText: The 109th Combat Engineers Battalion was part of the 34th Infantry Division of the US Army during WWII. The 34th was the first American division to be deployed in Europe in 1943 where it fought in the Italian Campaign. Prior to that the division had participated in Operation Torch in 1942 (Allied invasion of French North Africa) and the Tunisian Campaign that same year. During WWII the division saw 517 days of front line combat, second to the 32nd Infantry Division with 617 days of front line combat.

card_unit_11th_infantry_regiment.name: card_unit_11th_infantry_regiment
card_unit_11th_infantry_regiment.title: 11th INFANTRY REGIMENT
card_unit_11th_infantry_regiment.text: Deployment: Fully repair a friendly unit, then give it +1+1.
card_unit_11th_infantry_regiment.flavorText: The 11th Infantry Regiment was formed in 1862 in the American Civil War and has been active to this day. At the start of WWII the regiment was attached to the 5th Infantry Division of the US Army. In 1942 the division was deployed in Iceland where it stayed for 15 months before it was moved to England in preparation for D-Day. The division participated in the Normandy landings and fought its way across Europe as part of Patton’s Third Army where the 11th Infantry Regiment played vital roles in the Battle for Metz and the Battle of the Bulge. The regiment ended the war in Czechoslovakia and was retired on its return to the US, but reactivated in 1954 and has stayed active to this day.

card_unit_12th_infantry_regiment.name: card_unit_12th_infantry_regiment
card_unit_12th_infantry_regiment.title: 12th INFANTRY REGIMENT
card_unit_12th_infantry_regiment.text: Deployment: Spend your remaining kredits. This unit gets +X+X where X is kredits spent.
card_unit_12th_infantry_regiment.flavorText: The 12th Infantry Regiment was formed in 1861 and has been a unit of the US Army to the present day. On D-Day, 1944, the regiment spearheaded the landing assault on Utah Beach in Normandy with the 4th Infantry Division. During WWII the regiment fought with the 4th Infantry Division in several European battles and campaigns, in France, Belgium, Luxembourg and Germany, for which it received numerous awards for valor in combat. The regiment was retired in 1946, but reactivated in 1947 and is still active today.

card_unit_1st_marines.name: card_unit_1st_marines
card_unit_1st_marines.title: 1st MARINES
card_unit_1st_marines.text: When this unit moves into the frontline, give your HQ Smokescreen until your next turn.
card_unit_1st_marines.flavorText: The 1st Marine Regiment was first activated in 1913 during the so-called Banana-Wars in the Caribbean, later in the Haitian campaign (1915–1916) and the Dominican Republic campaign (1916). During WWII the regiment first saw combat in the Guadalcanal Campaign in 1942 and would afterwards fight in several campaigns and operations in the Pacific. The last WWII engagement of the 1st Marine Regiment was the Battle of Okinawa in 1945, but afterwards it was deployed to North China where it would help garrison the area until 1949. The regiment has remained active since WWII and has participated in most major American wars since then.

card_unit_a_36_apache.name: card_unit_a_36_apache
card_unit_a_36_apache.title: A-36 APACHE
card_unit_a_36_apache.text: When A-36 APACHE attacks, friendly ground units get +1+1.
card_unit_a_36_apache.flavorText: The A-36 Apache was an American ground-attack and dive bomber aircraft used in WWII by the US Army Air Force and the Royal Air Force. The A-36 first came into service in 1943 and was used in in North Africa Campaign, and then later in the Allied invasion of Sicily and the China-Burma-Indian Theater. The aircraft looked very similar to the P-51A Mustang fighter but had two more .50 caliber machine guns inside the lower engine housing that shot through the propeller arc. The A-36 also had dive breaks installed which limited the dive speed to 630 km/h and made it a very accurate dive bomber. The A-36 Apache was used in service until 1945 but many were withdrawn from service in 1944 and replaced with the P-40 Warhawk and P-47 Thunderbolt. A total of 500 aircraft were manufactured.

card_unit_b_25h.name: card_unit_b_25h
card_unit_b_25h.title: B-25 H
card_unit_b_25h.text: Deployment: Add a GUNSHIP MISSION to your hand.
card_unit_b_25h.flavorText: The North American B-25 Mitchell was an American medium bomber that was used by many Allied air forces and in all theaters of WWII. The B-25 Mitchell bombers were frequently used at low altitude and acted as a ground attack aircraft instead of as medium bombers. As a result, modifications were made to the aircraft and B-25G variants and onward, including B-25H, had guns added and unnecessary weight and space was eliminated in order to make it lighter. 1,000  B-25H variants were produced which featured two additional fixed 12.7 mm machine guns in the nose and four in fuselage-mounted pods. Nearly 10,000 aircraft were built in total, including numerous variants.

card_unit_b_29_super_fortress.name: card_unit_b_29_super_fortress
card_unit_b_29_super_fortress.title: B-29 SUPERFORTRESS
card_unit_b_29_super_fortress.text: Deployment: Distribute 6 damage randomly between enemies.
card_unit_b_29_super_fortress.flavorText: The Boeing B-29 Superfortress was an American heavy bomber used in WWII by the US Army Air Force, the US Air Force and the Royal Air Force. The B-29 was primarily used for high-altitude strategic bombing against Japan, but also proved very good for night incendiary bombing at low altitude. The aircraft was also used to drop the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. The B-29 was one of the largest aircraft built during WWII and its design included very advanced technology for its time, such as a pressurized cabin and an analog computer controlled firing system that allowed crew members to remotely control four machine gun turrets. 3,970 B-29s were built and the aircraft stayed in use until 1960.

card_unit_f4f_3_wildcat.name: card_unit_f4f_3_wildcat
card_unit_f4f_3_wildcat.title: F4F-3 WILDCAT
card_unit_f4f_3_wildcat.flavorText: The Grumman F4F Wildcat was an American carrier based fighter aircraft that was used during WWII by the US Navy and the Royal Navy. The aircraft was first used by the British in 1940 during the Battle of the Atlantic, and from 1941 to 1942 it was the only fighter available to the Marine Corps and the US Navy during the Pacific War. The aircraft was slower and less maneuverable than the Japanese Zero, but it had greater firepower and it was more durable and could withstand heavy battering without going down. A total of 7,885 Wildcats were manufactured, including quite a few variants, and most of them served on escort carriers.

card_unit_m4a1.name: card_unit_m4a1
card_unit_m4a1.title: M4A1
card_unit_m4a1.text: Can't be targeted by enemy orders. Draw this unit from deck if enemy makes you discard.
card_unit_m4a1.flavorText: The M4A1 was a Sherman medium tank variant and the first type to be used in US front line service. The M4A1 differed from other variants by its fully cast upper hull and its rounded appearance. The tank was first used by US forces in the North Africa Campaign and was the main Sherman type tank until late 1944 when the US Army began to replace them with the preferred M4A3 variant. The M4A1 was nevertheless used in front line service by the US and the Allies throughout the duration of the war.

card_unit_m8_howitzer.name: card_unit_m8_howitzer
card_unit_m8_howitzer.title: M8 HOWITZER
card_unit_m8_howitzer.text: Deployment: Distribute 3 damage randomly between all enemies.
card_unit_m8_howitzer.flavorText: The 75 mm Howitzer Motor Carriage M8 was an American self-propelled howitzer gun used during WWII by the US Army and the French Army. The M8 had a M116 howitzer in an M7 mount and used the chassis of the M5 Stuart tank. The M8 was used from 1942 and throughout the war but in 1944 the US Army started to replace it with the 105mm howitzer variant of the M4 Sherman tank.The M8 was used in the Italian Campaign, the Pacific War and on the Western Front, by both the US and French Army. A total of 1,778 M8s were built.

card_unit_motorized_infantry.name: card_unit_motorized_infantry
card_unit_motorized_infantry.title: 5th INFANTRY REGIMENT
card_unit_motorized_infantry.text: Gets +1+1 when it moves into the frontline.
card_unit_motorized_infantry.flavorText: The origin of the 5th Infantry Regiment of the US Army dates back to 1808 and it has participated in American conflicts since The War of 1812. During WWII the regiment was being trained as a light infantry unit capable of operating in harsh conditions, including both mountain and desert combat. However, a light infantry division was not needed at the time and the regiment was dispatched to Europe in 1945 as a regular infantry regiment. The 5th Infantry Regiment fought with the 79th Infantry Division in the south of Germany and captured the cities of Nuremberg, Fulda and Bayreuth. The regiment was the first US Army unit to cross the Danube River and the first to invade Austria where it performed occupation duty after the war.

card_unit_p_61_black_widow.name: card_unit_p_61_black_widow
card_unit_p_61_black_widow.title: P-61 BLACK WIDOW
card_unit_p_61_black_widow.text: At the start of your turn, give a random friendly air unit immune this turn.
card_unit_p_61_black_widow.flavorText: The Northrop P-61 Black Widow was an American night fighter introduced in 1944 and used for the remainder of the war. The P-61 was the first aircraft designed to carry a radar and although it was sufficiently armed it lacked the speed to engage some of the German fighters and medium bombers. 706 P-61 aircraft were built and were used in front line service in all theaters of the war and remained in service until 1954.

card_event_air_defense.name: card_event_air_defense
card_event_air_defense.title: AIR DEFENSE
card_event_air_defense.text: Deal 3 damage to an attacking unit. If it's an air unit, destroy it instead.
card_event_air_defense.flavorText: During WWII the US Army anti-aircraft systems were quite competent. American radar technology and aircraft design was advanced for its time, and so were their anti-aircraft guns. On the ground machine guns were used for low altitude air targets, but larger cannons for higher altitudes, such as the 120 mm M1 gun stratosphere gun, which was the most powerful AA gun of its time with an altitude capability of 18 km (60,000 ft).

card_event_awoken_giant.name: card_event_awoken_giant
card_event_awoken_giant.title: AWOKEN GIANT
card_event_awoken_giant.text: Deal 2 damage to target enemy unit in the frontline. If this destroys it, draw a card.
card_event_awoken_giant.flavorText: The USA was by far the leading industrial power in WWII.  The total value of goods produced, and services provided grew from $88.6 billion to $135 billion between year 1939 and 1944. To sum it up, half of the worldwide military production during WWII came from the United States.

card_event_cadet_nurse_corps.name: card_event_cadet_nurse_corps
card_event_cadet_nurse_corps.title: CADET NURSE CORPS
card_event_cadet_nurse_corps.text: Fully repair all friendly units and give them +1+1.
card_event_cadet_nurse_corps.flavorText: The United States Cadet Nurse Corps was established in 1943 to ensure the country had enough nurses to care for its citizens at home and abroad during WWII. The program was open to women only between the ages of 17 and 35, in good health, who had graduated from high school. The Cadet Nurse Corps operated from 1943 until 1948, and during this period 179,294 student nurses enrolled in the program.

card_event_death_from_above.name: card_event_death_from_above
card_event_death_from_above.title: DEATH FROM ABOVE
card_event_death_from_above.flavorText: The USA alone had a total of 197,000 bombers in their air force, almost five times more than the Axis powers combined.

card_event_enemy_spotted.name: card_event_enemy_spotted
card_event_enemy_spotted.title: ENEMY SPOTTED
card_event_enemy_spotted.text: If your enemy captures the frontline, draw 3 cards.
card_event_enemy_spotted.flavorText: In warfare, spotting the enemy as fast as possible could often mean the difference between life and death. Besides relying on eyesight, troops used binoculars and periscopes, but were also heavily reliant on ground and air surveillance units, plus the radar technology to locate enemies and to predict their next movement. In 1942 US officers commenced special training in recognizing enemy aircraft and ships, using a special technique referred to as the Renshaw Training System for Aircraft and Ship Recognition. Officers studied pictures of planes and vessels and learned to identify them by their form in a fraction of a second. Over a million combined Navy and Army personnel learned Renshaw’s techniques and it is believed to have saved an untold amount of lives during the war.

card_event_for_freedom.name: card_event_for_freedom
card_event_for_freedom.title: FOR FREEDOM
card_event_for_freedom.text: Give a unit +1+1. Draw a card.
card_event_for_freedom.flavorText: "Freedom" by definition of the Wiktionary: The state of being free, of not being imprisoned or enslaved.

card_event_gunship.name: card_event_gunship
card_event_gunship.title: GUNSHIP MISSION
card_event_gunship.text: Deal 2 damage to a target in the enemy support line. Your HQ gains +2 defense.
card_event_gunship.flavorText: A gunship is a military aircraft armed with heavy guns, primarily intended for attacking ground targets.

card_event_industrial_might.name: card_event_industrial_might
card_event_industrial_might.title: INDUSTRIAL MIGHT
card_event_industrial_might.text: Draw a card for each unit you have deployed or added this turn.
card_event_industrial_might.flavorText: For America WWII meant the end of the Great Depression, as the government started to spend huge amounts of money to improve the industries in the USA, both to support themselves and their Allies during the war. Unemployment in the US  by 1945 had fallen to 1.9% from 14.6% in 1940, and from 1939 to 1944 the US government spent in total 106.3 billion dollars on munitions production, which was more than half of what the Allied powers spent in total.

card_event_in_the_navy.name: card_event_in_the_navy
card_event_in_the_navy.title: IN THE NAVY
card_event_in_the_navy.text: When a friendly unit is attacked, give your unit +1+2 before damage.
card_event_in_the_navy.flavorText: The US Navy played the central role in the war against Japan, and a major role in the European war against Germany and Italy (after the British Royal Navy). The peak strength of the US Navy was on July 31, 1945 with 3,405,525 people serving. The US Navy motto is "Semper Fortis", meaning "Always Courageous".

card_event_land_of_the_free.name: card_event_land_of_the_free
card_event_land_of_the_free.title: LAND OF THE FREE
card_event_land_of_the_free.text: Reduce the operation cost of target unit to 0.
card_event_land_of_the_free.flavorText: In 1939 the total aircraft production for the US military was less than 3000 aircraft. By the end of the war it had became the countries leading industry with a total of 300,000 aircraft being manufactured. Around 97,000 of these aircraft were bombers, ranging from light bombers to very heavy bombers.

card_event_mobilization.name: card_event_mobilization
card_event_mobilization.title: MOBILIZATION
card_event_mobilization.text: Draw 2 units from your deck. Discard them at the end of turn.
card_event_mobilization.flavorText: The US Mobilization for WWII was immensely rapid and played a major role in the outcome and victory for the Allied Forces. Throughout the war over 16 million US citizens served in the military and after the war the US emerged as an undisputed superpower.

card_event_naval_bombardment.name: card_event_naval_bombardment
card_event_naval_bombardment.title: NAVAL BOMBARDMENT
card_event_naval_bombardment.text: Send a unit to hand. Costs 2 less if the enemy controls the frontline.
card_event_naval_bombardment.flavorText: Naval bombardment is also called naval gunfire support (NGFS) (also known as shore bombardment), which means that battleships, cruisers and destroyers provide fire support, sometimes for days, in the hope of reducing fortifications and defending forces.

card_event_overwhelming_force.name: card_event_overwhelming_force
card_event_overwhelming_force.title: OVERWHELMING FORCE
card_event_overwhelming_force.text: Choose and discard a unit. Give its attack and defense to target friendly infantry or tank.
card_event_overwhelming_force.flavorText: Although the Americans did not possess the largest military force during WWII, they managed to assemble a large fighting force in a short period of time. From the year 1939 to 1945 the US military personnel grew from 334,473 to 12,209,238 members. Of these men and women 38.8% (6,332,000) were volunteers and 61.2% (11,535,000) were draftees.

card_event_patriotic_zeal.name: card_event_patriotic_zeal
card_event_patriotic_zeal.title: PATRIOTIC ZEAL
card_event_patriotic_zeal.text: Double the attack and defense of a friendly unit.
card_event_patriotic_zeal.flavorText: Some say that American patriotism was at its peak when the country entered the war. Although the country was reluctant to join the war at first, Japans attack on Pearl Harbor soon changed that and seemingly united the nation in determination to achieve total victory over the Axis powers in Asia and Europe.

card_event_patton.name: card_event_patton
card_event_patton.title: PATTON
card_event_patton.text: Units you deploy cost 1 less kredit and have Blitz this turn.
card_event_patton.flavorText: General George Smith Patton Jr. (November 11, 1885 – December 21, 1945), aka “Old Bloods and Guts”, was a brilliant but controversial general. He successfully lead US troops in North Africa where he fought and won against Rommel, and during the Invasion of Sicily he was the first Allied commander to reach Messina. One of his most famous achievements was at the Battle of the Bulge, where he turned and force-marched his entire army to the relief of the besieged Americans at Bastogne.

card_event_seaborne_invasion.name: card_event_seaborne_invasion
card_event_seaborne_invasion.title: SEABORNE INVASION
card_event_seaborne_invasion.text: All enemy units in the frontline retreat. Add two US infantry units there with total attack of 6.
card_event_seaborne_invasion.flavorText: Many seaborne invasions were carried out by the Allied forces during WWII, but perhaps the most famous and largest seaborne invasion in history was the Allied landings in Normandy on June 6, 1944 (D-Day). The target was a 80 kilometer stretch of the Normandy coast which was defended by the German forces. In total the Allies deployed around 156,000 troops in Normandy on D-Day, 73,000 American, 61,715 British, 21,400 Canadian, the rest came from Australia, Belgium, Czechoslovakia, Denmark, France, Greece, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway and Poland. The invasion ended with Allied victory and by June 11th 54,186 troops, 104,428 vehicles and 547,428 tonnes of supplies had been landed on the beaches.

card_event_strategic_bombing.name: card_event_strategic_bombing
card_event_strategic_bombing.title: STRATEGIC BOMBING
card_event_strategic_bombing.text: Deal 3 damage to all targets in the enemy support line. The enemy loses a kredit slot.
card_event_strategic_bombing.flavorText: The US Air Force started strategic bombing of German positions in 1942, and air raids on Japan began in October 1944, which ended in the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki on and August 6th and 9th, 1945. In total the US Air Force dropped 1,463,423 tons of bombs during WWII, both on non-military and military targets.

card_event_supply_chain.name: card_event_supply_chain
card_event_supply_chain.title: SUPPLY CHAIN
card_event_supply_chain.text: Draw a card. If SUPPLY CHAIN is discarded, add 2 copies to your hand with a cost of 1.
card_event_supply_chain.flavorText: Many historians think that the supply chain built and managed by the Allies during WWII was the most advanced of its time and a major contributor to the Allied victory. Their supply chain management helped them move military supplies and armaments across the Pacific Ocean at strategic times. As an example, during the invasion of Normandy on June 6, 1944, the Allies constructed two artificial harbors on Omaha Beach and Gold Beach known as Mulberry A and B. Mulberry A was destroyed by a severe storm 10 days after its construction, however, Mulberry B accommodated over 2.5 million troops, 500,000 vehicles and 4 million tonnes of supplies until its decommissioning in April 1945.

card_event_supply_shipment.name: card_event_supply_shipment
card_event_supply_shipment.title: SUPPLY SHIPMENT
card_event_supply_shipment.text: Give a unit in the frontline +2+3.
card_event_supply_shipment.flavorText: Supply shipments play a major role in military logistics as soldiers must have food, water, medicine, weapons, transports and shelter in order live to fight another day.

card_event_the_alliance.name: card_event_the_alliance
card_event_the_alliance.title: THE ALLIANCE
card_event_the_alliance.text: Give all your non USA units +2+2.
card_event_the_alliance.flavorText: During WWII the major Allied powers were USA, United Kingdom, Soviet Union and China. Other Allied countries included, in alphabetic order, Australia, Belgium, Bolivia, Brazil, Canada, Denmark, France, Greece, Mexico, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, South Africa, Yugoslavia.

card_event_the_war_machine.name: card_event_the_war_machine
card_event_the_war_machine.title: THE WAR MACHINE
card_event_the_war_machine.flavorText: The Wiktionary definition for War Machine is: 1) An individual weapon for war, especially a mechanical one such as a siege engine or tank. 2) The military resources of a belligerent country considered as a whole.

card_event_torpedo_attack.name: card_event_torpedo_attack
card_event_torpedo_attack.title: TORPEDO ATTACK
card_event_torpedo_attack.text: Destroy an enemy unit that is in the frontline.
card_event_torpedo_attack.flavorText: During WWII many ships, submarines and aircraft were armed with torpedoes which were mainly used against enemy warships on the high seas. The torpedo was set to run at a depth just beneath the ship, and armed with a magnetic exploder that was set to activate at the appropriate time.

card_event_uncle_sam.name: card_event_uncle_sam
card_event_uncle_sam.title: UNCLE SAM
card_event_uncle_sam.text: Duplicate a random unit in your hand.
card_event_uncle_sam.flavorText: Uncle Sam (initials U.S.) is a common personification of the American government or the United States, and according to legend it came into use during the War of 1812. An image of Uncle Sam, drawn by  Montgomery Flagg, was used on posters during WWI and WWII and were designed to instill in the public a positive outlook and a sense of patriotism and confidence. The posters called upon every man, woman, and child to endure the personal sacrifice and domestic adjustments during wartime.

card_event_unity_is_strength.name: card_event_unity_is_strength
card_event_unity_is_strength.title: UNITY IS STRENGTH
card_event_unity_is_strength.text: Give a friendly infantry +1+1 for each friendly infantry unit on the battlefield.
card_event_unity_is_strength.flavorText: "Unity is Strength" is a motto of the 6th Infantry Regiment of the US Army. The regiment landed in North Africa in 1942, and landed in Italy on October 28, 1943, and served later as the 6th Armored Infantry Battalion under the 1st Armored Division. The unit participated in numerous military campaigns, including Operation Torch in French Morocco, the Tunisian Campaign and the Allied invasion of Italy.

card_event_usace.name: card_event_usace
card_event_usace.title: USACE
card_event_usace.flavorText: USACE stands for United States Army Corps of Engineers. The Corps of Engineers was established at the time of the American Revolutionary War. During WWII the Corps of Engineers took on over 27,000 military and industrial projects, including the Manhattan Project, and played a major role in the European and Pacific Theater.

card_event_war_bonds.name: card_event_war_bonds
card_event_war_bonds.title: WAR BONDS
card_event_war_bonds.text: Gain 2 extra kredit slots. Draw an additional card at the beginning of next turn.
card_event_war_bonds.flavorText: In order to support the war effort the US government sold war bonds for $18.75 a piece, which would be bought back for $50 ten years later. Larger denominations were also available in $1000 and 85 cent saving stamps were also sold to those who wanted to save up for a bond. 185 million Americans bought war bonds for a total amount of $185 billion.

card_event_we_can_do_it.name: card_event_we_can_do_it
card_event_we_can_do_it.title: WE CAN DO IT!
card_event_we_can_do_it.text: Give your units and HQ +3 defense and draw a card.
card_event_we_can_do_it.flavorText: "We Can Do It!", also known as "Rosie the Riveter" was an American WWII wartime poster produced by J. Howard Miller in 1943 for Westinghouse Electric as an inspirational image to boost worker morale. Today, the image and slogan has become very widely known, far beyond its defined purpose during WWII.

card_unit_101st_airborne.name: card_unit_101st_airborne
card_unit_101st_airborne.title: 101st AIRBORNE
card_unit_101st_airborne.text: Deployment: Deal 2 damage to a target in the enemy support line.
card_unit_101st_airborne.flavorText: The 101st Airborne Division, aka "Screaming Eagles", was an elite infantry division trained for air assault operations. During WWII it was famous for its role in Operation Overlord, Operation Market Garden, the liberation of the Netherlands and for their defense of the city of Bastogne during the Battle of the Bulge.

card_unit_10th_engineering_battalion.name: card_unit_10th_engineering_battalion
card_unit_10th_engineering_battalion.title: 10th ENGINEERS BATTALION
card_unit_10th_engineering_battalion.flavorText: The 10th Engineers Battalion were a support unit of the 30th Infantry Regiment of 3rd Infantry Division. During WWII they saw active military service in Algeria-French Morocco, Tunisia, Sicily, Naples-Foggia, Anzio, Rome-Arno, Southern France (with arrowhead), Rhineland, Ardennes-Alsace and Central Europe.

card_unit_17th_infantry_regiment.name: card_unit_17th_infantry_regiment
card_unit_17th_infantry_regiment.title: 17th INFANTRY REGIMENT
card_unit_17th_infantry_regiment.flavorText: The 17th Infantry Regiment, nicknamed "The Buffalos", dates back to 1812 and has fought in most American conflicts since then. During WWII the regiment was deployed in the Pacific Theater as part of the 7th Infantry Division and fought the Japanese forces in the Aleutian Islands, Eastern Mandates, Leyte and Ryukyus.

card_unit_1918_155mm.name: card_unit_1918_155mm
card_unit_1918_155mm.title: 155mm 1918 MODEL
card_unit_1918_155mm.text: When this unit attacks, it deals 1 damage to a random enemy.
card_unit_1918_155mm.flavorText: 155mm 1918 Model was a French howitzer variant, originally designed by Schneider. The Model 1918 was built in the United States and differed in some way from the originally French model, and was mainly built for use in WWI. It saw limited use early on in WWII, and was for most parts replaced in 1942 with the American 155 mm howitzer M1.

card_unit_30th_regiment.name: card_unit_30th_regiment
card_unit_30th_regiment.title: 30th REGIMENT
card_unit_30th_regiment.flavorText: The 30th Infantry Regiment was attached to the 3rd Division of the United States Army during WWII. It was formed in 1813 and has been involved in nearly every military action undertaken by the United States since then. During WWII the 30th participated in numerous battles and military operations including Operation Torch, Operation Husky, Operation Avalanche, Operation Shingle and Operation Anvil. In the final stages of the war the 30th Regiment was attached to the XV Corps that was tasked as the Spearhead across the Rhine into Germany. Their motto is "Our Country Not Ourselves".

card_unit_332nd_engineers.name: card_unit_332nd_engineers
card_unit_332nd_engineers.title: 332nd ENGINEER REGIMENT
card_unit_332nd_engineers.text: Deployment: Gain 1 extra kredit slot. Your HQ gains +2 defense.
card_unit_332nd_engineers.flavorText: The 332nd Engineer General Service Regiment was formed in May 1942. It shipped soon to England to build facilities for US troops to station in. After the Normandy Invasion it was attached to many advanced commands to build bridges and hospitals and repair roads and railroads. It’s greatest accomplishment was reconstructing the Duisburg-Hochfield Rail Bridge, a 858m (2,815 feet) long bridge spanning the Rhine in a record time of less than 7 days. The bridge was completed on the May 8, 1945 and was named the “Victory Bridge”.

card_unit_463rd_battalion.name: card_unit_463rd_battalion
card_unit_463rd_battalion.title: 463rd BATTALION
card_unit_463rd_battalion.text: When 463rd BATTALION attacks, deal 1 damage to a random enemy in same front.
card_unit_463rd_battalion.flavorText: The 463rd Parachute Field Artillery Battalion was formed in 1944 on the Anzio Beachhead in Italy. The battalion participated in various conflicts in the European Theater, including the invasion of Normandy and the Battle of Bastogne where it was attached to the 101st Airborne Division.

card_unit_506th_airborne.name: card_unit_506th_airborne
card_unit_506th_airborne.title: 506th AIRBORNE
card_unit_506th_airborne.flavorText: The 506th Parachute Infantry Regiment (506th PIR) is an airborne light infantry regiment of the United States Army. During WWII the regiment was attached to the 101st Airborne Division and participated in the D-day landings, Operation Market Garden, and the Battle of the Bulge. The 506th Airborne were the subject of the HBO miniseries Band of Brothers.

card_unit_75_mm_pack_howitzer.name: card_unit_75_mm_pack_howitzer
card_unit_75_mm_pack_howitzer.title: 75mm PACK HOWITZER
card_unit_75_mm_pack_howitzer.flavorText: The 75mm Pack Howitzer M1 was an American made artillery piece used by the United States and their Allies. It was designed for moving over difficult terrain and was primarily used by airborne units of the United States Army and the US Marine Corps.

card_unit_7th_regiment.name: card_unit_7th_regiment
card_unit_7th_regiment.title: 7th REGIMENT
card_unit_7th_regiment.text: Draw a card when 7th REGIMENT moves into the frontline.
card_unit_7th_regiment.flavorText: The 7th Infantry Regiment,  also known as "Cottonbalers", were part of the 3rd Infantry Division. During World War II, the regiment fought German forces on three fronts, North Africa, Italy, and Northwest Europe. Some claim that no other regiment exceeded the 7th’s combat time in WWII.

card_unit_8th_cavalry_regiment.name: card_unit_8th_cavalry_regiment
card_unit_8th_cavalry_regiment.title: 8th CAVALRY REGIMENT
card_unit_8th_cavalry_regiment.text: Your HQ is immune to damage on your turn.
card_unit_8th_cavalry_regiment.flavorText: The 8th Cavalry Regiment of the United States Army was formed in 1866 during the American Indian Wars. During WWII the regiment saw combat in the Pacific Theater and participated in the Manus Island invasion and the Leyte invasion in 1944 and in 1945 they pushed towards the northern outskirts of Manila along with the 1st Cavalry Division. After the Japanese surrendered, the regiment was given the responsibility of occupying the entire city of Tokyo along with the 1st Division.

card_unit_99th_infantry.name: card_unit_99th_infantry
card_unit_99th_infantry.title: 99th INFANTRY BATTALION
card_unit_99th_infantry.text: Deployment: If you control the frontline, give another friendly unit +2+2.
card_unit_99th_infantry.flavorText: The 99th Infantry Battalion was a unit that consisted of Norwegian soldiers in the US army. They were not attached to a regiment and were considered a separate unit. The 99th Battalion participated in several campaign. They landed on Omaha Beach, attended the final battle at Cherbourg and took part in the Battle of the Bulge.

card_unit_a20_havoc.name: card_unit_a20_havoc
card_unit_a20_havoc.title: A-20 HAVOC
card_unit_a20_havoc.text: Deployment: Your bombers operate for 2 less this turn.
card_unit_a20_havoc.flavorText: The Douglas A-20 Havoc was an American light bomber, intruder, and reconnaissance aircraft used in WWII by the United States Army Air Force (USAAF) and several Allied air forces. The A-20 variant was ordered by the USAAF for high-altitude bombing and performed well as such. The first operation involving A-20 Havoc bombers took place in 1942, when several of them engaged in an attack from Port Moresby against Japanese positions further north in Australian Papua on the island of New Guinea. By 1944, 370 A-20 Havoc bombers were in active duty with the Fifth Air Force who deployed them in the Allied campaigns in the South Pacific, both as low altitude bombers and ground attack aircraft.

card_unit_a26_invader.name: card_unit_a26_invader
card_unit_a26_invader.title: A-26 INVADER
card_unit_a26_invader.flavorText: The Douglas A-26 Invader was an American light bomber and ground attack aircraft, built by the Douglas Aircraft Company during WWII. The aircraft was first used in combat in 1944 in Europe, and then in the Pacific War in 1945. Although the service of the A-26 Invader was short in WWII, it was highly effective and was one of the finer aircraft developed during the war. A total of 2,503 aircraft were built, including variants, and it was used in service for many years after the war, both by the Americans and other countries.

card_unit_a_24_banshee.name: card_unit_a_24_banshee
card_unit_a_24_banshee.title: A-24 BANSHEE
card_unit_a_24_banshee.text: Deployment: Deal damage to target enemy unit equal to your unspent kredits.
card_unit_a_24_banshee.flavorText: The A-24 Banshee was a Douglas SBD Dauntless variant used by the U.S. Army Air Force in WWII. It was a scout plane and dive bomber that was first manufactured in 1941, same as Douglas SBD Dauntless variants, but land based and lacked the tail hook for carrier landings. The A24's were used to a very minor degree by the US Air Force in early stages of the war.

card_unit_b_17.name: card_unit_b_17
card_unit_b_17.title: B-17 FLYING FORTRESS
card_unit_b_17.flavorText: The Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress was an American four-engine heavy bomber used by the United States Army Air Forces and the Royal Air Force in WWII. The B-17 was primarily used for strategic bombing of German industrial and military targets, but also in the Pacific War where it was used in raids against Japanese shipping and airfields. The aircraft had the reputation of being a very effective bomber and it dropped more bombs than any other U.S. aircraft in WWII. The B-17 was also known for being able to endure heavy battle damage, while still being able to reach its target and bring the crew home safe.

card_unit_b_24.name: card_unit_b_24
card_unit_b_24.title: B-24 LIBERATOR
card_unit_b_24.flavorText: The Consolidated B-24 Liberator was an American heavy bomber used by the Allies during WWII. The B-24 was used for a wide variety of roles, for example, for heavy bombing, antisubmarine warfare and for maritime patrol and reconnaissance missions. The aircraft holds the record of being the worlds most produced heavy bomber in the world, with almost 19,000 units built.

card_unit_b_25_mitchell.name: card_unit_b_25_mitchell
card_unit_b_25_mitchell.title: B-25 MITCHELL
card_unit_b_25_mitchell.text: Deployment: Deal 3 damage to a random enemy unit.
card_unit_b_25_mitchell.flavorText: The North American B-25 Mitchell was an American twin-engine medium bomber. Originally it was designed for a three man crew, but later productions added room for 2-3 more crew members in various gun positions. The Mitchell was an exceptionally sturdy aircraft that could withstand tremendous punishment. It was used by many Allied air forces and served in every theater of WWII.

card_unit_b_26_marauder.name: card_unit_b_26_marauder
card_unit_b_26_marauder.title: B-26 MARAUDER
card_unit_b_26_marauder.text: Your non-targeting deployment effects trigger twice.
card_unit_b_26_marauder.flavorText: The Martin B-26 Marauder was an American medium bomber built and used by the Allies from 1941 to 1945. It was used in the Pacific Theater in early 1942, but later in the Mediterranean Theater and in Western Europe. In total 5,288 units were built and it was considered the most successful medium-range bombers used by the US Army Air Forces during WWII. By the end of the war the B-26 had flown more than 110,000 sorties and dropped 150,000 tonnes of bombs.

card_unit_corsair_f4u.name: card_unit_corsair_f4u
card_unit_corsair_f4u.title: CORSAIR F4U-1C
card_unit_corsair_f4u.flavorText: The Vought F4U Corsair was an American fighter aircraft used in World War II and later in the Korean War. The Corsair was both used as a carrier-based and land-based aircraft and served both the US Navy and the US Marines. Japanese pilots considered it a fearful aircraft in dogfights, and according to the US Navy it had a 11:1 kill ratio.

card_unit_corsair_f4u_1d.name: card_unit_corsair_f4u_1d
card_unit_corsair_f4u_1d.title: CORSAIR F4U-1D
card_unit_corsair_f4u_1d.text: Destruction: Destroy a random enemy unit.
card_unit_corsair_f4u_1d.flavorText: The Vought F4U Corsair was an American fighter aircraft used in World War II and later in the Korean War. The Corsair was both used as a carrier-based and land-based aircraft and served both the US Navy and the US Marines. Japanese pilots considered it a fearful aircraft in dogfights, and according to the US Navy it had a 11:1 kill ratio.

card_unit_f4f_wildcat.name: card_unit_f4f_wildcat
card_unit_f4f_wildcat.title: F4F-4 WILDCAT
card_unit_f4f_wildcat.text: Add a BREWSTER F2A beside this unit when it moves into the frontline.
card_unit_f4f_wildcat.flavorText: The Grumman F4F Wildcat was an American carrier-based fighter aircraft used in WWII by the United States Navy and the British Royal Navy. The Wildcat was the most effective fighter available to the United States Navy and Marine Corps in the Pacific Theater up until 1942. It had a top speed of 512 km/h (318 mph), and although it was outperformed by longer-ranged Mitsubishi A6M Zero, it performed well and had a kill ratio of 6.9:1. Throughout the war 7,885 Wildcats were built, including a few variants.

card_unit_grumman_hellcat2.name: card_unit_grumman_hellcat2
card_unit_grumman_hellcat2.title: F6F-3 HELLCAT
card_unit_grumman_hellcat2.text: When this unit attacks it gets +1+1.
card_unit_grumman_hellcat2.flavorText: The Grumman F6F Hellcat was an American carrier-based fighter of WWII, designed to replace the earlier F4F Wildcat and to counter the Japanese Mitsubishi A6M Zero. It was produced from 1942 to 1945 with 12,275 units built and it became the US Navy's dominant fighter in the Pacific War. The aircraft claimed 5,163 kills which counted for 56% of all U.S. Navy/Marine air victories of WWII.

card_unit_m16_halftrack.name: card_unit_m16_halftrack
card_unit_m16_halftrack.title: M16 HALF-TRACK
card_unit_m16_halftrack.text: Deployment: An enemy air or infantry unit must retreat.
card_unit_m16_halftrack.flavorText: The M16 Multiple Gun Motor Carriage, also known as the M16 Half-track, was an American self-propelled anti-aircraft weapon built and used during WWII. The M16 had a main armament of 4 x 12.7 mm M2 Browning machine guns and was nicknamed "The Meat Chopper" for its deadly firepower, which made it popular with the troops. It was mainly used by the US forces and saw action in the Italian Campaign, Operation Overlord, the Battle of Arracourt and the Ardennes Offensive.

card_unit_m18_hellcat.name: card_unit_m18_hellcat
card_unit_m18_hellcat.title: M18 HELLCAT
card_unit_m18_hellcat.flavorText: The M18 Hellcat (official named 76 mm Gun Motor Carriage M18 or M18 GMC) was an American tank destroyer of World War II. The Hellcat had a higher kill to loss ratio than any tank or tank destroyer in the US forces in WWII. It had a crew of 5 (Commander, gunner, loader, driver, assistant driver), a main armament of a 76 mm gun and a secondary armament of a .50 caliber Browning machine gun.

card_unit_m1_155mm_long_tom.name: card_unit_m1_155mm_long_tom
card_unit_m1_155mm_long_tom.title: LONG TOM
card_unit_m1_155mm_long_tom.text: When LONG TOM attacks, distribute 3 damage between random enemies.
card_unit_m1_155mm_long_tom.flavorText: The 155 mm Gun M1 (nickname Long Tom) was an American 155 millimeter caliber field gun used by the United States military and Allied forces during WWII. The gun could fire a 45.36 kg (100 lb) shell to a maximum range of 22 km (13.7 miles). 1,882 guns were produced 1940-1945.

card_unit_m24_chaffee.name: card_unit_m24_chaffee
card_unit_m24_chaffee.title: M24 CHAFFEE
card_unit_m24_chaffee.text: When M24 CHAFFEE moves to the frontline, add a copy beside it.
card_unit_m24_chaffee.flavorText: The M24 Chaffee, officially called Light Tank M24, was an American tank used by the Allies in WWII. It was given the name Chaffee after the United States Army General Adna R. Chaffee, Jr.. It had a crew of 5 (commander, gunner, loader, driver, assistant driver/radio operator), a main armament of 75 mm Gun M6 in Mount M64 and a secondary armament of .50 cal Browning M2HB machine gun.

card_unit_m26_pershing.name: card_unit_m26_pershing
card_unit_m26_pershing.title: M26 PERSHING
card_unit_m26_pershing.text: While in the frontline, your HQ cannot be reduced below 1 defense.
card_unit_m26_pershing.flavorText: The M26 Pershing was an American heavy tank which came into service during the final months of WWII during the invasion of Germany, but was used extensively after that in the Korean War. The M26, and later variants, had a crew of 5 (Commander, Gunner, loader, driver, co-driver), a mounted 90 mm gun as main armament and a secondary armament of 2x Browning .30-06 machine guns.

card_unit_m36_destroyer.name: card_unit_m36_destroyer
card_unit_m36_destroyer.title: M36 JACKSON
card_unit_m36_destroyer.text: If the enemy discards M36 JACKSON from your hand, put it on the battlefield instead.
card_unit_m36_destroyer.flavorText: The M36 Jackson, formally known as 90 mm Gun Motor Carriage, M36, was an American tank destroyer used by US forces during WWII. The M36 combined the hull of the M10 tank destroyer, which had a M4 Sherman's chassis, and a new turret mounting a 90 mm gun M3. It was designed in 1943 and first served in combat in October 1944, as a replacement for the M10 tank destroyer. The M36 had a crew of 5 (Commander, gunner, loader, driver, assistant driver) and a secondary armament of .50 caliber (12.7 mm) Browning M2HB machine gun. The M36 was well liked by US troops as it was one of the few armored vehicles available to the US forces that was capable of destroying heavy German tanks from a distance. It was generally referred to by American soldiers as "TD" (Tank Destroyer).

card_unit_m3_stuart.name: card_unit_m3_stuart
card_unit_m3_stuart.title: M5 STUART
card_unit_m3_stuart.flavorText: The M5 Stuart, formally known as Light Tank M5, was an American light tank used by the Allied forces during WWII. It had a crew of 4 (commander, gunner, driver, assistant driver) and a speed of 58 km/h (36 mph) on road. The tank had a main armament of a 37 mm Gun M6 and and a secondary armament of 3x .30 caliber Browning machine guns. The British and Commonwealth forces were the first to call it "Stuart" after American Civil War Confederate General J. E. B. Stuart. However, the Americans usually referred to the tank as "Light Tank M5".

card_unit_m4_sherman.name: card_unit_m4_sherman
card_unit_m4_sherman.title: M4 SHERMAN
card_unit_m4_sherman.text: Deployment: If you have a US unit in the frontline, draw 2 cards.
card_unit_m4_sherman.flavorText: The M4 Sherman was a medium tank used by the American and Allied forces during WWII. It had a crew of 5 and was mounted with a 75 or 76 mm gun, or a 105 mm howitzer, a.50 caliber Browning machine gun and 2—.30 caliber Browning machine guns. It was considered very reliable, relatively cheap to produce and was available in great numbers.The M4 Sherman did well against German lighter tanks and Italian tanks, but later in the war it lacked in firepower and armor compared to the heavier German tanks. To compensate for this some M4 variants were fitted with bigger guns, such as 76 mm gun M1, or as the British Sherman Firefly that was refitted with an Ordnance QF 17-pounder.

card_unit_m4_sherman_flam.name: card_unit_m4_sherman_flam
card_unit_m4_sherman_flam.title: M4A3R3 ZIPPO
card_unit_m4_sherman_flam.text: Has +4 attack against infantry and enemy HQ.
card_unit_m4_sherman_flam.flavorText: The M4A3R3 "Zippo" was a Sherman tank variant, equipped with a flamethrower and commonly used in attacks against fortifications or confined spaces. The M4A3R3 "Zippo" was used in the Battle of Iwo Jima in 1945 and proved very effective at clearing Japanese defensive positions. Typically, the maximum range of a flamethrower was less than 150 meters, which made it relatively useless in an open battlefield. However, when attacking fortified positions it also proved to be a very powerful psychological weapon. In many cases the enemy surrendered or fled when seeing a flame tank approaching, rather than risk being burned alive.

card_unit_m7_priest.name: card_unit_m7_priest
card_unit_m7_priest.title: M7 PRIEST
card_unit_m7_priest.text: Deployment: Gains +1+1 if you control the frontline.
card_unit_m7_priest.flavorText: The 105 mm Howitzer Motor Carriage M7 was a self-propelled artillery vehicle produced by the US and used by the Allies during WWII. The M7 Priest had a crew of 8 and was mounted with a 105 mm Howitzer and 1 x 0.5 Browning machine gun. It was called M7 Priest by the British since the machine gun ring looked like a pulpit.

card_unit_m8_greyhound.name: card_unit_m8_greyhound
card_unit_m8_greyhound.title: M8 GREYHOUND
card_unit_m8_greyhound.text: While in the frontline, units in your support line have +1 attack.
card_unit_m8_greyhound.flavorText: The M8 Greyhound was an American light armored car and was mainly used by the Americans and the British who gave it the nickname Greyhound due to its high speed on normal roads. The M8 Greyhound was mainly used for reconnaissance as the 37 mm gun was not very effective against enemy armor.

card_unit_marines.name: card_unit_marines
card_unit_marines.title: 3rd MARINE REGIMENT
card_unit_marines.flavorText: During WWII the 3rd Marine Regiment was attached to the 2nd Marine Brigade. They fought at Bougainville and Guam and during this period their members were awarded four Medals of Honor for their acts of valor. During the Battle of Iwo Jima the 3rd Marines were kept in reserve and were not sent ashore.

card_unit_p38_lightning.name: card_unit_p38_lightning
card_unit_p38_lightning.title: P-38D LIGHTNING
card_unit_p38_lightning.flavorText: The Lockheed P-38 Lightning was an American fighter aircraft used in WWII. The P-38 was used for various purposes, including interception, dive bombing, level bombing, ground attack, night fighting, photo reconnaissance, radar and visual path-finding for bombers and evacuation missions, and extensively as a long-range escort fighter when equipped with drop tanks under its wings.

card_unit_p40n.name: card_unit_p40n
card_unit_p40n.title: P-40 N-5
card_unit_p40n.text: Units deployed by the enemy have +2 operation cost.
card_unit_p40n.flavorText: The P-40 N was introduced in 1943 and became the most produced variant of the Curtiss P-40 Warhawk, with 5220 aircraft built. This variant was made lighter than its predecessor, the undercarriage wheels were made smaller, two guns were removed and aluminum radiators and oil coolers were installed. This made the P-40 N the fastest Warhawk, reaching a speed of 378 mph below 12,000 feet. Many of the P-40 Ns were shipped to Allied air forces under Lend-Lease and many were sent to the USSR. Most of the P-40 Ns operational flying took place in the Pacific Theater in fighter-bomber or escort roles, both by the Americans and other Allied air forces.

card_unit_p40_warhawk.name: card_unit_p40_warhawk
card_unit_p40_warhawk.title: P-40 WARHAWK
card_unit_p40_warhawk.flavorText: The Curtiss P-40 Warhawk was an American single-engine, single-seat fighter and ground-attack aircraft that was all metal. The P-40 was agile at low and medium altitudes and was used by most Allies during World War II. War-records claim that over 200 fighter pilots from 7 different nations became Aces flying the P-40.

card_unit_p47d_thunderbolt.name: card_unit_p47d_thunderbolt
card_unit_p47d_thunderbolt.title: P-47D THUNDERBOLT
card_unit_p47d_thunderbolt.text: When this unit destroys an enemy unit, draw a card.
card_unit_p47d_thunderbolt.flavorText: The Republic P-47 Thunderbolt was an American fighter aircraft produced from 1941 to 1945 and used by the US Air force and Allied air forces during WWII. The Thunderbolt was effective as a short-to-medium range escort fighter in high-altitude air-to-air combat and ground attack in both the European and Pacific Theaters. The aircraft was equipped with a primary armament of eight .50-caliber machine guns and in the fighter-bomber ground-attack role it could carry five-inch rockets or a bomb load of 1,103 kg (2,500 pounds). By the end of the war 15,636 units had been built, including variants.

card_unit_p51_mustang.name: card_unit_p51_mustang
card_unit_p51_mustang.title: P-51 MUSTANG
card_unit_p51_mustang.text: Deployment: Deal 5 damage to a random enemy air unit.
card_unit_p51_mustang.flavorText: The P-51 Mustang was an American long-range, single-seat fighter and fighter-bomber used by the Allied forces in WWII. The Mustang was first developed for the RAF and was first used as a tactical-reconnaissance aircraft and fighter-bomber. Later variants were designed to perform better at higher altitude (above 15,000 ft), allowing the aircraft to compete with the Luftwaffe's fighters. In WWII the aircraft was used by the British and Americans alike, both as an escort for bombing raids over Germany and as a fighter-bomber. It is claimed that Mustang pilots destroyed 4,950 enemy aircraft and that it played a large role in ensuring Allied air superiority in 1944.

card_unit_sbd3_dauntless.name: card_unit_sbd3_dauntless
card_unit_sbd3_dauntless.title: SBD 3 DAUNTLESS
card_unit_sbd3_dauntless.flavorText: The SBD 3 Dauntless was a Douglas SBD Dauntless scout plane and dive bomber variant that was first manufactured in 1941. It was flown both from land air bases and aircraft carriers and earned its nickname “Slow But Deadly“ after delivering the fatal blows to the Japanese carriers at the Battle of Midway.

card_unit_t19_howitzer.name: card_unit_t19_howitzer
card_unit_t19_howitzer.title: T19 HOWITZER
card_unit_t19_howitzer.text: Units attacked by T19 HOWITZER lose Guard this turn.
card_unit_t19_howitzer.flavorText: The T19 Howitzer Motor Carriage (HMC) was a 105 mm howitzer mounted on a M3 Half-track chassis. Its secondary armament consisted of an air-cooled .50 in (13 mm) M2 machine gun for local defense. The T19 was first used in service by the U.S. Army in 1942, but was soon replaced in armored divisions by the M7 Priest, although some were still in use as late as 1944 during the Allied invasion of France.

card_unit_tbf_avanger.name: card_unit_tbf_avanger
card_unit_tbf_avanger.title: TBF-1 AVENGER
card_unit_tbf_avanger.text: Deployment: Destroy a random enemy unit with 5 or more defense.
card_unit_tbf_avanger.flavorText: The Grumman TBF Avenger was an American torpedo bomber developed for the Marine Corps and United States Navy and used by the Allied forces in WWII. It first saw combat in 1942 in the Battle of Midway, and although 5 out of 6 TBF-1s were lost in its combat debut it became later known as one the best torpedo bombers of WWII. In total 9,839 Avengers were built, and numerous variants were designed for various purposes, and it remained in use by various naval aviation services around the world until the 1960s.

card_unit_us_signal_corps.name: card_unit_us_signal_corps
card_unit_us_signal_corps.title: 593rd JASCO
card_unit_us_signal_corps.text: Damage dealt to your HQ is reduced by 1.
card_unit_us_signal_corps.flavorText: The Joint Assault Signal Company (JASCO) were joint service units that provided ship to shore, air to ground communications to coordinate and control naval gunfire and close air support to the United States Army. During WWII they were composed of detachments supplied to Army and Marine Corps divisions, regiments and battalions. The 593rd JASCO was attached to the 96th Infantry Division which fought in the Pacific Theater in the military campaigns of Leyte, Southern Philippines, Okinawa and Ryukyus.

card_event_air_corps_ferrying.name: card_event_air_corps_ferrying
card_event_air_corps_ferrying.title: AIR CORPS FERRYING
card_event_air_corps_ferrying.text: Give a friendly unit +1+1. If you have 5 or more unspent kredits, apply this to all friendly units.
card_event_air_corps_ferrying.flavorText: With the North Atlantic sea lanes vulnerable to German U-boat attacks, Major General Henry H. Arnold established the Air Corps Ferrying Command in May 1941 to deliver lend-lease aircraft. Its mission was "to move aircraft by air from factories to such terminals as may be designated by the Chief of the Air Corps," and "to maintain such special air ferry services as may be required to meet specific situations." During WWII, Ferrying Command expanded far beyond its initial role and it became the established military air transport service over the North Atlantic.

card_event_bocage_warfare.name: card_event_bocage_warfare
card_event_bocage_warfare.title: BOCAGE WARFARE
card_event_bocage_warfare.text: Give a unit in your support line: "Gets +2+2 when it moves into the frontline."
card_event_bocage_warfare.flavorText: Bocage warfare refers to the intense fighting that took place in the dense hedgerow countryside of Normandy, France, during WWII. The “Battle of the Hedgerows” occurred in June and July 1944, with extremely deadly fighting raging for three weeks. This challenging bocage landscape, characterized by small fields, high hedges, and muddy lanes, created natural defenses for the German army and slowed down the Allied progression. The hedgerows provided excellent cover for German infantry, tanks, and artillery, allowing them to set up ambushes and resist the Allies push inland. American troops had to adapt quickly, developing new tactics and modifying equipment to navigate and fight in the bocage. For instance, tanks were fitted with improvised "hedge cutters", known as Rhino attachments, to break through the thick hedgerows. Allied infantry also adopted close-quarters combat tactics to clear fortified positions hidden within the terrain. Despite high casualties and slow progress, these adaptations allowed the Allies to eventually break through the German defenses and continue their advance in Normandy.

card_event_hell_on_wheels.name: card_event_hell_on_wheels
card_event_hell_on_wheels.title: HELL ON WHEELS
card_event_hell_on_wheels.text: Duplicate a friendly tank and reduce its operation cost by 2. Double its attack if a Sherman.
card_event_hell_on_wheels.flavorText: The 2nd Armored Division was a US armored division during WWII. The division earned its nickname "Hell on Wheels" from General George S. Patton during training maneuvers in the United States in the early 1940s. Patton, who was known for his colorful language and larger-than-life personality, was impressed by the division speed, aggressiveness and mobility in mock combat exercises. He remarked that they moved like “hell on wheels,” a phrase that stuck and became the division’s official nickname. The division's first major action came during Operation Torch in 1942, where it fought alongside Allied forces to push the Axis troops out of French North Africa. Following the success in North Africa, Hell on Wheels participated in the invasion of Sicily in 1943 and later the D-Day landings on Omaha Beach on June 6th, 1944. The division advanced through France and Belgium, where it participated in the Battle of the Bulge, and crossed the Rhine River into Germany. After the war the division remained stationed in Germany as part of the Allied occupation forces, before returning to the United States in 1946.

card_event_pontoon_bridge.name: card_event_pontoon_bridge
card_event_pontoon_bridge.title: PONTOON BRIDGE
card_event_pontoon_bridge.text: Give a friendly unit +1+2. If it had 4 or more attack, set its operation cost to 0 as well.
card_event_pontoon_bridge.flavorText: A pontoon bridge is a bridge that uses floats or shallow draft boats for support and enables river crossings in combat zones. Pontoon bridges have been used since ancient times, but during WWII the US Army Corps of Engineers frequently employed pontoon bridges to cross rivers like the Rhine Germany, allowing Allied forces to maintain their offensive momentum. Pontoon bridges were quick to assemble and disassemble and were used in key operations during WWII, including the D-Day invasion and the final push into Germany.

card_event_women_at_work.name: card_event_women_at_work
card_event_women_at_work.title: WOMEN AT WORK
